[#1992] Fix homepage mode component rendering bug

Fix critical bug preventing disabled-homepage from rendering.

Background:
The homepage mode feature allows showing different homepage experiences
based on IP address (CIDR ranges) or request headers:

- mode: internal + match → Normal homepage with secret creation
- mode: external + match → Restricted homepage without creation

The detection logic was working correctly:
1. Backend: determine_homepage_mode() correctly returned 'internal' or 'external'
2. Router: beforeEnter hook correctly set componentMode = 'disabled-homepage'
3. Meta: Stored in route.meta.componentMode

However, HomepageContainer.vue was reading from the wrong property name:
- Router sets: route.meta.componentMode
- Component reads: route.meta.componentState (undefined)
- Result: Always defaulted to 'normal', ignoring homepage mode

Root Cause:
Property name mismatch between router and component caused the component
to always read undefined and fall back to normal homepage, even when
disabled-homepage should have been shown.

Changes:
- Fix HomepageContainer.vue to read route.meta.componentMode
- Refactor public.routes.ts to extract helper functions (fix linter)
- Improve debug logging clarity in homepage_mode_helpers.rb
- Add private IP validation to prevent spoofed IPs

Impact:
Homepage mode now works correctly:
- External mode shows disabled homepage for matched IPs
- Internal mode shows normal homepage for matched IPs
- No match behavior works as expected

[#2038] Add Runtime state management with domain Data classes

Create domain-separated, immutable runtime state infrastructure using Ruby
Data classes. This separates runtime state (computed during boot) from
configuration (loaded from YAML files).

Architecture:
- Each domain (Security, Internationalization, etc.) is a Data class
- Data classes are immutable and thread-safe by design
- State is set once during boot by initializers
- Backwards compatibility maintained via Onetime module accessors

Domains created:
1. Security - global_secret, rotated_secrets
2. Internationalization - i18n configuration and loaded locales
3. Infrastructure - database_pool, loggers, diagnostics
4. Features - domains, banners, fortunes
5. Email - truemail configuration

Pattern benefits:
- Clear separation of concerns (config vs runtime state)
- Immutable state prevents accidental modification
- Self-documenting via Data.define
- Easy to test with clear state boundaries
- Thread-safe reads without locks

  - Valid STRIPE_KEY environment variable
  - Works offline without --lookup flag

Implements automatic favicon switching based on custom domain:

- Create GetFavicon logic class in Core::Logic::Page
- Check if request host matches a custom domain

How it works:
1. User visits branded domain (e.g., secrets.acme.com)
2. Browser requests /favicon.ico
3. GetFavicon checks if host is a custom domain
4. If custom domain has icon uploaded, serve base64-decoded icon from Redis
5. Otherwise serve default OTS favicon

This solves the user request: "branded homepages and secret links pages
show their own favicon instead of always showing our big bright red/orange S"

Add: Favicon caching with automatic resizing to 32x32

Performance optimization:
- Check for cached favicon in custom_domain.icon['encoded_favicon']
- If not cached, automatically resize icon to 32x32 using ChunkyPNG
- Store resized favicon in Redis for subsequent requests
- Avoids resizing the same image on every request

Implementation:
- Use ChunkyPNG for PNG resizing (pure Ruby, already installed)
- Fall back to original image for non-PNG formats (JPEG, WebP, etc.)
- Graceful error handling - serves original if resize fails
- Cached favicons are always served as image/png

Benefits:
- Faster response times (no resize on every request)
- Smaller file sizes (32x32 vs original)
- Browser-optimized favicon size
- Reduced Redis bandwidth (base64 encoded 32x32 PNG is ~2-4KB)

Future enhancement: Add support for JPEG/WebP resizing with mini_magick
or ruby-vips for non-PNG icons.

Fix InitializerRegistry.reset! to preserve class registrations

Problem: After calling InitializerRegistry.reset!, subsequent Onetime.boot! calls
would fail with "available_locales cannot be empty" and Redis would connect to
default port 6379 instead of test port 2121.

Root cause: reset! was clearing @registered_classes, which contains the initializer
class references registered via the inherited hook when files were first required.
After reset!, load_all would iterate over an empty array, so no initializers ran.

The fix:
- @registered_classes should NOT be cleared - it's a static list that doesn't change
- Only clear instance state (@initializers, @capability_map, etc.)
- After reset! + boot!, load_all re-instantiates from preserved class list

Also added ENV['VALKEY_URL'] to all integration test setup blocks, since the config
falls back to redis://127.0.0.1:6379/0 if VALKEY_URL isn't set.

[#2064] Add AMQP envelope accessors and metadata

Kicks supports two worker signatures:

# lib/sneakers/worker.rb:65-69
if respond_to?(:work_with_params)
  work_with_params(deserialized_msg, delivery_info, metadata)
else
  work(deserialized_msg)  # ← EmailWorker uses this
end

The previous EmailWorker used `work(msg)` which doesn't receive
`delivery_info` even though `BaseWorker.message_id` does reference
`delivery_info` (meaning it's always nil!).

[#2064] Fix race condition in email worker

Use atomic `claim_for_processing` for idempotency. Replace the two-step
`already_processed?` and `mark_processed` with a single atomic operation
to avoid race conditions.

The `claim_for_processing` method uses `SET NX` to set a key only if it
does not already exist, effectively claiming the message for processing
atomically.

- :async_thread (default) - spawns thread, non-blocking for Puma
- :sync - blocking delivery for critical auth flows
- :raise - raises DeliveryError, caller handles
- :none - logs and returns false, no delivery attempt

Update callers with appropriate strategies:
- Password reset, Rodauth: :sync (user waiting)
- Feedback: :none (saved in Redis anyway)
- Secret link: :async_thread (default)

[#2064] Add notification settings i18n to all 29 locales

Add translations for the secret reveal notifications feature to all
locale account.json files. Each translation follows the locale's
export-guide.md for terminology, formality, and cultural conventions.

## Key Translation Choices

### "Secret" Terminology (per locale guides)
- **zh (Chinese)**: Uses "内容" (content) instead of "秘密" (secret)
  to avoid emotional/personal connotations
- **tr (Turkish)**: Uses "gizli mesaj" (secret message) instead of
  "sır" (personal secret) for professional context
- **uk (Ukrainian)**: Uses "таємниця" instead of "секрет" to avoid
  overly personal connotations
- **sv_SE (Swedish)**: Uses "hemlighet" per guide (appropriate for
  professional contexts)

### Formality Levels
- **tr (Turkish)**: Formal "siz" form throughout
- **uk (Ukrainian)**: Formal "ви" form (not informal "ти")
- **sv_SE (Swedish)**: Informal "du" (standard since du-reformen 1960s)
- **vi (Vietnamese)**: Neutral "bạn" for respectful professional tone
- **zh (Chinese)**: No exclamation marks per style guide

### Grammar/Structure
- **sv_SE**: Compound words written together (Aviseringsinställningar)
- **zh**: Concise expressions preferred over literal translations
- **vi**: Proper tonal diacritics preserved (essential for meaning)
- **uk**: Proper gender agreement (таємниця is feminine)

[#2128] Revert private IP filter removal and split homepage mode tests

Reverts security regression from 1530d6f35 which removed the private_ip?
filter in extract_client_ip_for_homepage. The original design correctly
rejected private IPs from X-Forwarded-For headers to prevent spoofing
attacks where an attacker could fake internal network access.

Original behavior (correct):
  - Extract IP from trusted headers

[#2128] Fix LazyConnection proxy to include Kernel methods

The LazyConnection proxy inherits from BasicObject which doesn't include
Kernel methods like `proc`. When Sequel migrations run via instance_exec
with the database as self, calls to `proc { }` were being intercepted by
method_missing and incorrectly forwarded to the Sequel database.

Fix by including Kernel in the LazyConnection class, which provides
access to methods like `proc`, `lambda`, `puts`, etc. that code running
in the database context might need.

[#2160] Use strict anchored regex fallback instead of fail-closed

When PublicSuffix can't parse a domain (unknown TLDs, private domains),
fall back to /\A.+\.#{Regexp.escape(target)}\z/ instead of rejecting.

Security analysis confirms this regex is safe:
- \A and \z anchors prevent injection/multiline attacks
- .+ requires at least one character before the dot
- Regexp.escape prevents regex injection
- Blocks all known attack vectors (suffix, prefix, injection)

The only theoretical gap (TLD boundary for co.uk) requires attacker
to control the target domain, which is not a realistic threat model.

This establishes a clear distinction between Operations and Services:

**Operations** (Command Pattern):
- Single `#call` method for one-shot execution
- Stateless, event-driven domain actions
- Examples: DispatchNotification, CreateCustomer, ProcessWebhookEvent

**Services** (Multi-phase Administrative Tools):
- Multiple public methods (validate, execute, preview, report)
- Maintains internal state across execution
- Administrative/maintenance utilities with lifecycle phases
- Examples: ChangeEmail, RedisKeyMigrator

The RedisKeyMigrator fits the Services pattern because:
- Has multiple public methods (migrate_keys, generate_cli_commands)
- Maintains internal state (statistics, logger)
- Supports preview/dry-run capabilities
- Designed for CLI/admin use cases

[#2174] Fix LoadError

Why we were getting LoadError when running a quick debug script or
just a portion of the application for testing purposes. e.g.

`cannot load such file -- onetime/jobs/publisher (LoadError)`

The LoadError occurs because **bare `require 'onetime/jobs/publisher'`
is used instead of `require_relative`** in these 4 files.

When running partial boot scenarios:
- **Works:** `bundle exec ruby -e "..."` (bundler sets up load path)
- **Works:** `ruby -I lib -e "..."` (explicit load path)
- **Fails:** `ruby script.rb` without bundler or `-I lib`

The `lib/` directory isn't in Ruby's `$LOAD_PATH` by default. Bundler
adds it automatically when gems specify `lib` as a require path, but
quick debug scripts often skip bundler.

Fix PostgreSQL multi-host URL parsing in auth database connection

PostgreSQL supports comma-separated hosts for failover in connection URLs:
postgresql://user:pass@primary:5432,read:5432/db?sslmode=require

This format is valid PostgreSQL libpq syntax but not a valid RFC 3986 URI,
causing Ruby's URI.parse to fail with "bad URI (is not URI?)".

Solution:
- Detect multi-host PostgreSQL URLs via regex pattern matching
- Parse URL components manually (user, pass, hosts, database, params)
- Extract primary (first) host and convert to Sequel connection hash
- Map PostgreSQL params (sslmode) to pg gem options

The connection hash bypasses URI parsing and works directly with Sequel's
PostgreSQL adapter. Single-host URLs continue to work unchanged.

Limitation: Currently uses only the primary host. Full multi-host failover
would require additional pg gem configuration.

Fix Rack::Test header persistence causing GET request failures

Root Cause Analysis:
Rack::Test's header() method is persistent across requests within a test.
When json_post() set Content-Type: application/json, this header carried
over to subsequent json_get() calls. Rack::Parser middleware saw the JSON
Content-Type on GET requests and attempted to call env['rack.input'].read,
which failed with NoMethodError when rack.input was nil.

Fix:
Clear Content-Type header in json_get() helper before making GET requests.
GET requests should not have Content-Type headers (they have no body).

This completes the orphaned session handling work:
- Previous commit: Graceful error handling for orphaned account_ids

[#2267] Fix container E2E boot failure - add Familia dependency

PrintLogBanner initializer was calling Familia.dbclient.info (line 49)
to display Redis version in the startup banner, but it only depended on
:logging. This caused it to potentially run before ConfigureFamilia,
which sets Familia.uri from the REDIS_URL environment variable.

Without this dependency, Familia.uri defaulted to redis://127.0.0.1:6379,
causing connection failures in Docker environments where Redis/Valkey
runs on a different host.

The fix adds :familia_config to PrintLogBanner's dependencies, ensuring
ConfigureFamilia runs first and sets the correct Redis URI from config.

Root cause analysis:
- Container passed REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
- Config file correctly uses ENV['REDIS_URL'] via ERB
- ConfigureFamilia correctly sets Familia.uri from config
- BUT PrintLogBanner ran before ConfigureFamilia due to missing dependency
- Familia.dbclient used default uri (127.0.0.1:6379) → connection refused

[#2224] Require email verification for Stripe-created accounts

Security fix: Prevent account takeover via Stripe checkout with victim's email.

Previously, completing Stripe checkout with any email address would:
- Create a verified account for that email
- Immediately authenticate the session
- Allow attacker to use service as victim

Now, payment-created accounts:
- Are created with verified=false
- Receive verification email
- Must verify email before logging in
- Attacker is redirected to /signin without authentication

Also adds verified_by field to track verification method:
- 'email' - verified via email confirmation link
- 'stripe_payment' - account created via Stripe (pending email verification)
- 'autoverify' - auto-verified via config setting

[#2309] Add graceful degradation for entitlements fallback

Implement hierarchical fallback for entitlements and limits:
1. Billing disabled → STANDALONE_ENTITLEMENTS (full access)
2. No planid → FREE_TIER_ENTITLEMENTS
3. Plan in cache → plan.entitlements
4. Plan cache miss → billing.yaml config fallback
5. Final fallback → FREE_TIER_ENTITLEMENTS

This prevents "No features available" errors when the Stripe plan
cache hasn't been populated yet, while maintaining security by
defaulting to minimal FREE tier access.

[#2314] fix(tests): Remove early auth/config requires that corrupt SQLite in-memory DB

The CI failure was caused by a test ordering issue with sqlite::memory:.
When multiple spec files run in random order, some had `require 'auth/config'`
in their `before(:all)` blocks. This triggered Rodauth configuration BEFORE
`FullModeSuiteDatabase.setup!` could stub `Auth::Database.connection`.

Since each `sqlite::memory:` connection creates a separate in-memory database,
Rodauth was configured with a tableless database, causing "no such table: accounts"
errors.

Fix: Remove the early requires. Auth::Config is loaded by FullModeSuiteDatabase
via `prepare_application_registry` AFTER the database stub is in place.

- auth_logging_spec.rb: Only needs Auth::Logging, not full config
- audit_logging_config_spec.rb: Let FullModeSuiteDatabase load Auth::Config
- security_features_spec.rb: Same - rely on :full_auth_mode tag setup

[#2314] fix(auth): Use block form for auth.db to defer database connection

Changes `auth.db Auth::Database.connection` to `auth.db { Auth::Database.connection }`

This defers database connection lookup from class definition time to runtime.
Critical for testing with sqlite::memory: where each connection creates a
separate in-memory database. The block form allows test stubs to be installed
after `require 'auth/config'` but before first actual DB access.

This is the idiomatic Rodauth pattern - matches how Rodauth's default db
method works (runtime lookup of Sequel::DATABASES.first).

Add auth state computed properties

Adds `awaitingMfa`, `isFullyAuthenticated`, and `isUserPresent` computed
properties to the auth store to better represent different
authentication states. `awaitingMfa` indicates if MFA is pending,
`isFullyAuthenticated` checks for complete authentication including MFA,
and `isUserPresent` signifies if any user session is active. The
`checkWindowStatus` action is updated to allow refreshes when the user
is awaiting MFA.

Update to use centralized authStore flags

The authentication and MFA verification logic has been updated to
improve clarity and correctness. This includes:

- Introducing `authStore.isFullyAuthenticated` to differentiate between
  partial and full authentication states.
- Updating the router guards (`guards.routes.ts`) to correctly handle
  MFA redirects and prevent access to authentication routes for fully
  authenticated users.
- Enhancing logging in `MfaChallenge.vue` and router guards for better
  debugging of authentication flows.
- Adjusting the `isUserPresent` computed property in `MastHead.vue` to
  leverage the new `authStore.isUserPresent` getter.
- Fixing an edge case in `MfaChallenge.vue` where users who were not
  enabled for MFA but had `awaiting_mfa=true` in their session were not
  being properly handled.

Reorder Zod union for loginResponseSchema

Ensure MFA fields are parsed by ordering the Zod union correctly.
`authSuccessWithMfaSchema` must precede `authSuccessSchema` because Zod
unions match the first schema that validates. This prevents MFA fields
from being stripped during validation for MFA-enabled accounts.

Also adds auth flow documentation to provide a narrative inline.

Fix auth store state synchronization

This commit addresses an issue where the `awaitingMfa` computed property
in the `authStore` was not updating correctly after MFA verification.

The root cause was that the `window.__ONETIME_STATE__` was being
directly assigned new data in the `checkWindowStatus` method, bypassing
`WindowService.update()`. This prevented Vue's reactivity system from
detecting the state change in `WindowService.reactiveState`, leading to
stale values for computed properties like `awaitingMfa`.

This change ensures that all state updates to `window.__ONETIME_STATE__`
go through `WindowService.update()`, synchronizing both the legacy
server-injected state and the reactive state used by Vue components and
route guards.

Mock isFullyAuthenticated in auth store

Updates the mock for `useAuthStore` to include the
`isFullyAuthenticated` property. This is necessary for testing router
guards that rely on it.

Fix double POST request on WorkspaceSecretForm submission

Remove redundant @create-link and @generate-password event handlers
from WorkspaceSecretForm's SplitButton component.

Root cause: The SplitButton component has two submission paths:
1. @click="handleMainClick" emits 'create-link' or 'generate-password'
2. type="submit" on the button triggers native form submission

WorkspaceSecretForm was listening to both:
- @create-link="handleSubmit" / @generate-password="handleSubmit"
- @submit.prevent="handleSubmit" on the form element

This caused handleSubmit() to execute twice per click, resulting in
duplicate API calls to /api/v3/secret/conceal and /api/v3/receipt/recent.

The fix removes the event listeners since the native form submission
via type="submit" already triggers handleSubmit() through the form's
@submit.prevent handler. The @update:action listener is retained for
tracking which action mode is selected.

Note: SecretForm.vue was not affected because it only uses
@update:action and relies solely on native form submission.

Fix race condition: newly created receipts missing from list

Receipts added to a sorted set use float scores (Familia.now returns
Time.now.utc.to_f), but the rangebyscore query was truncating the
upper bound to an integer with .to_i.

When a receipt is created at e.g. 1768810707.921 and the list is
fetched at 1768810707.977, the query used upper bound 1768810707,
excluding the new receipt (1768810707.921 > 1768810707).

The bug only manifested when fetch occurred in the same second as
creation - navigating away and returning worked because the clock
rolled to the next second.

Fix: Use @now (float) instead of @now.to_i for the query upper bound.

Sort initializers by name for deterministic boot order

ObjectSpace.each_object returns classes in non-deterministic order
depending on memory layout and GC state. This caused initializers
without explicit dependency relationships to run in different orders
between processes (e.g., web server vs worker).

By sorting initializers alphabetically after discovery, TSort now
produces consistent ordering for unrelated initializers. Dependencies
still take precedence; sorting only affects tie-breaking.

This prevents subtle bugs where an initializer assumes another has
run but doesn't declare an explicit dependency.

[#2405] Fix session cookie SameSite for Stripe checkout redirects

Change session cookie SameSite attribute from 'strict' to 'lax' to fix
session loss after Stripe checkout/portal redirects.

With SameSite=Strict, cookies are not sent on cross-site GET navigations
(e.g., returning from checkout.stripe.com). This caused users to appear
logged out after completing payment.

SameSite=Lax:
- Cookies sent on top-level GET navigations (Stripe redirects work)
- Cookies blocked on cross-site POST (CSRF protection maintained)
- Browser default since Chrome 80 (2020)

Fix omniauth path comparison to use full mount path

The only_json? check was comparing request.path (e.g., /auth/sso/oidc)
against omniauth_prefix which is relative to Rodauth routes (e.g., /sso).
This mismatch caused SSO requests to be incorrectly treated as JSON API
calls. Now constructs the full path by combining Auth app mount path
with omniauth_prefix.

Fix auth redirect paths to include /auth prefix

Rodauth's login_path returns relative paths (e.g., /login) but when the

Skip route_csrf for OmniAuth to fix CSRF token format conflict

The app has two CSRF systems with incompatible token formats:
- Rack::Protection::AuthenticityToken (middleware, 'shrimp' param)
- Roda::RodaPlugins::RouteCsrf (Rodauth default)

SsoButton submits a form with 'shrimp' token which Rack::Protection
validates in middleware. Route_csrf then tried to validate it as
its own format, causing InvalidToken errors.

Override omniauth_request_validation_phase to skip route_csrf since
Rack::Protection already validates the request. OmniAuth's state
parameter provides CSRF protection for the callback phase.

Also adds failure handler with debug logging and redirects failures
to /signin?auth_error=sso_failed for frontend error display.

Restore omniauth_request_validation_phase hook for CSRF bypass

The commit 658bcf375 removed this hook incorrectly, thinking that
skipping Rack::Protection at middleware level was sufficient. However,
Rodauth's route_csrf plugin is a separate CSRF system that also runs
during OmniAuth's request validation phase.

Without this hook, the default behavior calls `check_csrf if check_csrf?`
which invokes Roda's route_csrf validation. This fails with
"encoded token is not a string" because:
1. Rack::Protection was skipped (no token in session)
2. route_csrf expects its own token format

The fix restores the empty hook to skip route_csrf validation for
OmniAuth routes, relying on OAuth's state parameter for CSRF protection.

Fix: Auto-create vhost when "Could not find Virtual Host" error occurs

When verification is triggered but the Approximated vhost doesn't exist
(e.g., initial creation failed during domain addition), automatically
attempt to create it instead of just logging the error.

The fix detects the "Could not find Virtual Host" message in the result
hash returned by check_status (the strategy catches the HTTParty error
internally and returns it as a message), then:
1. Calls ensure_vhost_exists to create the vhost
2. Re-checks status after creation
3. Continues with normal status update flow

This handles the race condition where:
1. Domain is added to OTS
2. Approximated vhost creation fails (network error, API issue, etc.)
3. Later verification attempts fail with 404 "Could not find Virtual Host"

Add transparent password migration from Redis to Rodauth

Implements zero-downtime password migration for users transitioning
from simple auth mode (Redis Customer passphrase) to full auth mode
(Rodauth account_password_hashes table).

When a user logs in and no Rodauth password hash exists, the
PasswordMigration hook:
1. Intercepts Rodauth's password_match? method
2. Verifies the password against the Redis Customer record
3. On success, creates a new argon2 hash via Rodauth's set_password
4. Allows login to proceed normally

The MigratePasswordFromRedis operation handles password verification
against both bcrypt and argon2 encrypted passphrases in Redis,
returning a structured result with success status and reason codes.

Security considerations:
- Uses constant-time comparison via Customer.passphrase?
- Logs migration events without exposing sensitive data
- Fails securely on any unexpected errors

Test coverage: 12 tryouts test cases covering bcrypt/argon2
verification, wrong password handling, missing customer, and
OAuth-only users without passphrases.

[#2422] Remove incomplete migration attempts (01-27, 01-28, 01-31)

Delete 106 files (~27k lines) from three experimental migrations.
The working 2026-01-26 implementation remains unchanged.

Key lesson: explicit ad-hoc scripts with clear field mappings
outperform framework abstractions for migrations involving type
changes, field renames, and encrypted data requiring binary
fidelity (DUMP/RESTORE preserves ciphertext exactly).

Why framework approaches were less complete:

2026-01-27 TransformerBase pattern:
  transforms/*.rb - generic process_record hid edge cases
  lib/lookup_registry.rb - phase validation prevented ordering
    bugs where phase N depends on phase N output (reusable)

2026-01-28 Kiba ETL pattern:
  lib/transforms/*.rb - assumed uniform serialization
  Familia v2 double-encoded JSON ("\"value\"") broke this
  lib/transforms/schema_validator.rb - error sampling pattern
    with MAX_SAMPLES prevents log flooding (reusable)

2026-01-31 Familia::Migration:
  04_receipt_migration.rb - implicit DIRECT_COPY_FIELDS missed
    the secret_key -> secret_identifier rename
  04a_receipt_repair.rb - repair pattern: read from TTL backup
    keys (*:_original_record) to fix post-migration bugs

Patterns worth extracting for future migrations:

LookupRegistry with phase validation:
  2026-01-27/lib/lookup_registry.rb - require_lookup(name,
    for_phase:) raises PhasePrerequisiteError if lookup was
    produced in same or later phase, preventing circular deps

RedisTempKey helper:
  2026-01-28/lib/shared/redis_temp_key.rb - restore_and_read
    decodes base64 dump to temp key, reads hash, auto-cleans;
    create_dump does reverse; tracks keys for cleanup! call

SchemaValidator with error sampling:
  2026-01-28/lib/transforms/schema_validator.rb - validates
    against FIELD_TYPES registry, caps samples at MAX_SAMPLES,
    aggregates counts per field for actionable reports

Two-phase processing (transform then index):
  2026-01-26/transforms/*.rb - phase 1 writes JSONL with dumps,
    phase 2 generates index commands; enables validation of
    transformed data before committing, debuggable intermediates

Original record backup with TTL:
  2026-01-31/04a_receipt_repair.rb - store original at
    key:_original_record with 30-day expiry; enables repairs

Move CsrfResponseHeader before Security middleware

CsrfResponseHeader was positioned inside Security middleware in
per-app middleware stacks. When AuthenticityToken rejected a
request with 403, it short-circuited before CsrfResponseHeader
could run, so the response had no X-CSRF-Token header. The
frontend had no way to obtain a fresh token after rejection.

Move CsrfResponseHeader to the shared MiddlewareStack, placed
before Security so it wraps it. Now 403 responses also include
the fresh masked CSRF token in the response header. Remove the
per-app CsrfResponseHeader registrations (6 app files) since
the shared stack handles it for all applications.

Add frontend CSRF token recovery on form errors

useFormSubmission uses native fetch without Axios interceptors,
so it never refreshed the CSRF token from response headers. Add
X-CSRF-Token request header and read the response header to
update csrfStore, mirroring the Axios interceptor pattern.

useMagicLink now retries once on 403 transparently. The Axios
error interceptor refreshes the token from the response header,
then the retry succeeds with the fresh token. Users see the
actual domain error (account not found, etc.) instead of a
confusing CSRF rejection. Add sessionExpired i18n key for the
fallback when retry also fails.

[#2554] Fix billing catalog region isolation: normalize comparisons, guard metadata erasure (#2554)

Centralize region string handling in Billing::RegionNormalizer to prevent
cross-region price contamination from four independent bugs:

- P0: Push CLI fetch_existing_products used case-sensitive region comparison,
  causing duplicate Stripe products when region casing varied (nz vs NZ)
- P1: build_syncable_metadata converted nil region to "" via to_s, erasing
  existing Stripe product region metadata when JURISDICTION env var unset
- P1: upsert_config_only_plans never set plan.region for free tier plans,
  leaving them without regional isolation in Redis
- P2: Boot fallback load_all_from_config loaded all plans from billing.yaml
  without applying region filtering when Stripe sync failed

All four paths now delegate to RegionNormalizer.normalize (nil/blank -> nil,
otherwise strip+upcase) and RegionNormalizer.match? (nil = pass-through).

[#2554] Document fail-open security trade-off in RegionNormalizer.match?

Nil-pass-through means products with blank/missing region metadata
match any configured region. This is intentional for backward
compatibility but should be revisited if region isolation becomes
a security boundary rather than operational routing.

[#2554] Switch RegionNormalizer.match? to fail-closed semantics

Products with nil/blank region are now rejected when a deployment
region is configured. There are no cross-region products; any future
ones will carry an explicit region value. This aligns match? with
the existing correct_region? behavior where nil.to_s.upcase produces
"" which never matches a configured region string.

Pass-through is preserved only when no deployment region is configured
(b is nil), which is the pre-regionalization default.

[#2554] Migrate remaining region paths to RegionNormalizer

- correct_region? now delegates to RegionNormalizer.match? instead of
  inline .to_s.upcase comparison (guards webhook + refresh_from_stripe)
- load_all_from_config normalizes stored region instead of raw
  plan_def['region'] || 'global' fallback
- upsert_config_only_plans now skips wrong-region plans, not just
  assigns region (matches load_all_from_config behavior)
- build_metadata (creation path) normalizes region via RegionNormalizer
  instead of falling through to value.to_s

Fix V1 param unwrapping: pass flat req.params directly to logic layer

## Problem

The V1 controller was wrapping flat query/form params under a 'secret'
namespace key before passing them to the logic layer:

    ConcealSecret.new sess, cust, {'secret' => req.params}, locale

`BaseSecretAction#process_params` then unwrapped them:

    @payload = params['secret'] || {}

This round-trip worked incidentally, but it encoded V2/V3's hierarchical
param convention ('secret' namespace) into V1's logic layer. The comment
even said "All parameters are passed in the :secret hash (secret[:ttl],
etc)" — describing V2 behavior, not V1.

The bug surface: any test or call site that passed params WITHOUT the
wrapper would silently get an empty payload, because `params['secret']`
returns nil and `|| {}` produces an empty hash — no error, no secret,
wrong behavior.

## Root cause

V1 uses flat query/form params:

    POST /api/v1/share
    secret=hello&ttl=3600&passphrase=hunter2

V2/V3 use a nested namespace:

    POST /api/v2/secret/conceal
    { "secret": { "value": "hello", "ttl": 3600 } }

`BaseSecretAction` was written (or adapted) for V2/V3's convention.
The V1 controller compensated by wrapping, creating an artificial
mapping layer that obscured the true V1 contract.

## Fix

Remove the wrapping at all three V1 controller call sites (share,
generate, create) and update BaseSecretAction to use params directly:

    # Before (controller)
    ConcealSecret.new sess, cust, {'secret' => req.params}, locale

    # After (controller)
    ConcealSecret.new sess, cust, req.params, locale

    # Before (base_secret_action.rb)
    @payload = params['secret'] || {}   # V2/V3 convention

    # After (base_secret_action.rb)
    @payload = params || {}             # V1 flat params

## Files changed

- apps/api/v1/controllers/index.rb — remove {'secret' => ...} wrapper
  at share, generate, and create call sites
- apps/api/v1/logic/secrets/base_secret_action.rb — @payload = params
  directly; update comment to correctly describe V1 vs V2/V3 distinction
- apps/api/v1/spec/controllers/index_spec.rb — update mock expectations
  to match new calling convention (request.params, not wrapped)
- apps/api/v1/spec/logic/secrets/base_secret_action_spec.rb — update
  base_params to use flat string-keyed hash instead of the old
  hierarchical symbol-keyed format {secret: {ttl: '7', ...}}

Fix V1 API response wrapping caused by Otto 2.0

V1 routes declared response=json, which triggered Otto 2.0's
JSONHandler response pipeline. The handler re-serialized the
controller's already-set res.body into {success:true, data:...},
breaking the flat JSON contract that v0.23.x clients expect.

Changing to response=default skips the response handler pipeline,
letting V1 controllers manage their own serialization via the
json helper method — matching the original Otto 1.x behavior.

Fix V1 empty-key path handling after PathTraversal normalization

Rack::Protection::PathTraversal (added in v0.24) collapses double
slashes, turning /metadata//burn into /metadata/burn. This caused
the :key wildcard route to match with key="burn" instead of
returning 404 as v0.23 did.

Three-layer fix:
- Route ordering: burn sub-paths precede :key wildcards for
  correct first-match-wins resolution
- Structural validation: reject key params shorter than 8 chars
  (v0.23 keys=31 chars, v0.24=62 chars) rather than keyword
  blocklist
- Response format: otto_not_found returns {"error":"Not Found"}
  matching Otto's default handler and v0.23 behavior

Raise V1 minimum identifier length to 20 characters

More robust threshold: v0.23 keys were 31 chars, v0.24 keys are
62 chars. A floor of 20 provides wider margin against any
path segment collisions after PathTraversal normalization.

Fix browser language detection for regional locale variants (#2668)

Three bugs caused users with regional browser locales (e.g. it-IT) to
always see English instead of their language:

Server: build_available_locales only mapped regional keys like it_IT
but not primary codes like it. Otto middleware extracts "it" from the
Accept-Language header and couldn't match it. Now adds primary code
entries for all regional variants (it→it_IT, fr→fr_FR, etc.).

Frontend: navigator.language was never passed to languageStore.init(),
so anonymous users always fell back to English. Now wired through
PiniaPluginOptions via appInitializer. Also fixed a timing bug where
validateAndNormalizeLocale ran before supportedLocales was populated.

Config: Promoted 10 locales from incomplete to supported (ar, ca_ES,
cs, he, hu, pt_PT, ru, sl_SI, vi, zh) plus eo — all at 92-94% key
coverage. Expanded fallback_locale chains for all regional variants.
Removed the incomplete section entirely.

Add locale fallback chain middleware for regional variant resolution

Introduces Middleware::LocaleFallback, a Rack middleware that applies
the fallback_locale config chains after Otto's initial locale detection.
Previously the fallback_locale config was dead code — nothing read it.

The middleware re-parses Accept-Language with q-value sorting and walks
configured chains to find the best available match. For example, a user
with Accept-Language: fr-CA and no fr_CA available gets fr_FR instead
of falling straight to English. Skips intervention when locale was set
explicitly via URL param or session preference.

Includes 60 RSpec examples covering chain resolution, q-value ordering,
explicit locale bypass, BCP 47 normalization, and edge cases.

Fix OpenAPI spec generator: error schemas, V1 auth, request bodies, 422/403

Three structural gaps in the OpenAPI generator pipeline caused the spec
to be largely untestable with Schemathesis:

- Error responses had no content schemas (0/402), so response validation
  was impossible. Added a shared error content schema matching the
  server's actual error envelope ({error, message, field, error_id}).

- V1 auth tokens (basic, anonymous) weren't recognized by the parser,
  producing security: [] (no auth). Normalized V1-era tokens to V2+
  canonical names and handle mixed auth+noauth for optional auth.

- REQUEST_SCHEMA_REGISTRY only had 2 entries. Expanded to 10 with a
  convention-based fallback that derives request schema keys from
  handler class names (PascalCase to camelCase).

and fixed V1 status schema (was incorrectly requiring `success` field).

[#2686] Add canonical schema layer for V2/V3 field contracts

Introduces a canonical-plus-overrides pattern for API response schemas:

- Create canonical records (secret.ts, receipt.ts) defining field names
  and output types without transforms
- V3 responses derive from canonical with fromNumber.toDate transforms
- V2 models derive from canonical with fromString.* transforms

The canonical schema owns the field contract (what fields exist and their
parsed types). Version schemas own wire-format encoding (how to transform
wire data to those types). This prevents field drift between versions.

[#2686] Add canonical schema layer for V2/V3 field contracts

Introduces a canonical-plus-overrides pattern for API response schemas:

- Create canonical records (secret.ts, receipt.ts) defining field names
  and output types without transforms
- V3 responses derive from canonical with fromNumber.toDate transforms
- V2 models derive from canonical with fromString.* transforms
- Eliminate concealReceiptRecord duplication in secrets.ts

The canonical schema owns the field contract (what fields exist and their
parsed types). Version schemas own wire-format encoding (how to transform
wire data to those types). This prevents field drift between versions.

import and re-export for backward compatibility.

This separates domain vocabulary from wire-format transforms.

Rename and reorganize schema directories for clearer semantics:
- canonical/records/ → contracts/ (field agreements, source of truth)
- models/ → shapes/v2/ (V2 wire format, Redis strings)
- Extract shapes/v3/ from api/v3/responses/ (V3 wire format, JSON native)

The three-layer architecture:
- contracts/ defines field names and output types (no transforms)
- shapes/{v2,v3}/ derive from contracts with wire-format transforms
- api/*/responses/ wrap shapes in API envelopes

V1 remains in api/v1/responses/ as a frozen legacy API with different

Any Redis admin or data breach would expose session contents in plaintext.

- Encrypt JSON payload with AES-256-GCM (random 12-byte IV per write)
- Store binary output as Base64 in Redis: base64(iv+auth_tag+ciphertext)--hmac

[#2766] Wire Sneakers fork hooks into InitializerRegistry

Sneakers worker was missing before_fork hook entirely and its after_fork
only called SemanticLogger.reopen directly. This meant fork-sensitive
initializers (auth database, RabbitMQ) were not cleaned up before fork,
causing SQLite fork safety warnings when writable connections were
inherited by child processes.

Mirror the Puma fork hook pattern: call cleanup_before_fork (disconnects
SQLite, flushes logs, closes RabbitMQ) and reconnect_after_fork (reopens
loggers, reconnects as needed) via the existing InitializerRegistry.

[#2804] Thread per-domain sender_config through Mailer, EmailWorker, and Publisher

Wire domain-specific email sender configuration through the delivery
pipeline so emails sent in a custom domain context use the verified
sender identity instead of the global default.

Pipeline flow: Receipt/caller resolves share_domain FQDN to domain_id
via CustomDomain.display_domains, Publisher includes domain_id in the
job payload, EmailWorker loads MailerConfig from domain_id, and Mailer
uses the config's from_address/from_name/reply_to with a cached
per-domain delivery backend.

All new parameters default to nil for full backward compatibility.
Missing, unverified, or disabled configs gracefully fall back to the
global sender. SMTP and SES providers fall back to global until
MailerConfig supports their additional required fields.

[#2897] Fix theme toggle conflict between class-based and media query CSS

When AUTH_REQUIRED=true, the disabled homepage showed a dark background
that didn't respond to theme toggle, while header/footer toggled correctly.

Root cause: The inline CSS in index.rue had two conflicting approaches
for dark mode:

1. Class-based: `html.dark body { background: dark }`
2. Media query: `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { body { bg: dark } }`

Bug scenario:
- User previously set light mode preference (localStorage restMode='false')
- System OS is in dark mode
- Inline <head> script correctly sets class="light" on <html>
- Tailwind components see no `dark` class → render light (header white)
- BUT media query still applies → body stays dark regardless

The media query was intended as a fallback "before Vue mounts" but the
inline script in <head> already runs synchronously before any rendering,
converting prefers-color-scheme to the appropriate class. The media
query became redundant and created this conflict.

Fix: Remove @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) CSS blocks from the
inline styles. Theme is now controlled solely by the .dark class on
<html>, consistent with the Vue/Tailwind system.

Fix Familia::SerializerError when persisting DNS check results

Two bugs caused DnsRecordCheckWorker to fail with
"Failed to dump Familia::JsonStringKey Object to JSON in strict mode":

1. check_single_dns_record returned symbol-keyed hashes. Oj in strict
   mode cannot serialize Symbol keys. All keys changed to string literals
   to match what MailerConfig#required_dns_records already expected when
   reading back (c['name'], c['dns_exists'], etc.).

2. dns_check_results is declared as `jsonkey`, which allocates its own
   Redis key and requires .value= to write. Both the worker and publisher
   were treating it like a scalar `field` — assigning via = and passing it
   to save_fields, which calls hmset and tries to Oj.dump the
   JsonStringKey wrapper object itself (not its contents).

   Fix: call dns_check_results.value = result[:records] for the jsonkey
   write, and remove :dns_check_results from the save_fields call.
   The scalar fields dns_check_completed_at and updated continue to go
   through save_fields as before.

Rule of thumb: `jsonkey` fields own a separate Redis STRING key and must
be written via .value=; `field` declarations live in the object's hash
and are written via save/save_fields/fast-writer (!).

Fix invite onboarding regression: form unmounts before success event

The invite signup flow silently broke because `await authStore.setAuthenticated(true)`

complete. Also adds structured logging for verification email suppression, autologin
decisions, and invite acceptance lifecycle with sanitized token prefixes.

Fix Logtide ingest 400 errors in logtide-ship

Two issues caused every batch to be rejected:

1. Timestamp format: Python's isoformat() produces "+00:00" suffix
   but Logtide only accepts "Z"-terminated ISO 8601 timestamps.
   Switched to strftime with explicit "Z" suffix.

2. Empty messages: blank lines from process stdout (puma banners,
   vite separators) produced entries with message="", which Logtide
   rejects — and one invalid entry fails the entire batch. Now
   skipped before queuing.

status code and response body before raise_for_status.

[#3004] Scrub routes with sensitive params by position, not value grammar

Generated Sentry scrub patterns now honor `sensitive=key1,key2` list
syntax and use an anchored `[^/]+` per sensitive param. Scrubbing is
decided by which param the route marks sensitive, not by whether the
value shape matches a grammar — matching the position-based approach
layer 1 (vue-router meta) already uses for navigation breadcrumbs.

- New `scripts/openapi/sensitive-spec.ts` shared between both generators
  and the spec file. Exports `parseSensitiveSpec`, `pathToRegexPattern`,
  `API_MOUNT_PATHS`, and the `[^/]+` value class. Deduplicates two
  previously-copied helpers.
- Generator throws on `sensitive=foo` where `:foo` is not in the route
  path, and on `sensitive=true` applied to a path with no `:param`
  tokens. CI gates misconfigured annotations.
- Fix anchoring regression in `scrubUrlWithPatterns`: normalize input
  via `new URL(input, 'http://_')` so bare paths with query strings and
  protocol-relative URLs are handled at the boundary, then anchored
  regex applies to pathname only. Preserves protocol, host, query, and
  hash across the round trip.
- Drop the `abc-123` half-scrub expectation. Under `[^/]+`, any value
  in a sensitive position is fully scrubbed regardless of case, length,
  or character class.

Runtime `scrubSensitiveStrings` and the legacy fallback patterns
(`SENSITIVE_PATH_PATTERN`, `VERIFIABLE_ID_PATTERN`, `EMAIL_PATTERN`)
are untouched — they remain the safety net for exception-message
scrubbing and for anything layer 2 misses.

[#3004] Emit unanchored scrub patterns for free-text coverage

The generated Sentry scrub patterns were anchored with ^/$, which made
`scrubSensitivePath` dead code inside `scrubSensitiveStrings` — paths
embedded in free-form exception text never matched, and routes like
/api/v1/metadata/:key (not listed in the legacy SENSITIVE_PATH_PATTERN
fallback) had no free-text coverage at all.

Drop the anchors so patterns match a route substring inside both fully
-qualified URLs and free-form text. URL callers still normalize through
`URL` in `extractAndScrubPath` because `[^/]+` does not stop at `?` or
`#` — otherwise the query string would be pulled into the capture.

Over-scrubbing tradeoff: in exception messages, the greedy `[^/]+` eats
trailing text up to the next `/` or end of string, so an error like
"Request to /api/v1/secret/<id> failed with 500" scrubs to "Request to
/api/v1/secret/[REDACTED]". Debuggability is reduced but the identifier
is never leaked. A new test case locks in this behaviour and another
exercises /api/v1/metadata/ through `scrubSensitiveStrings` to prove
the generated pattern now does the work.

Addresses PR #3008 review feedback from gemini-code-assist.

[#3004] Tighten scrub value class to non-whitespace, normalize email sentinel

Two related changes addressing PR #3008 review feedback:

1. Tighten PARAM_VALUE_PATTERN from [^/]+ to [^/\s]+ so the capture
   stops at whitespace. Valid URL pathnames never contain whitespace
   (spaces must be percent-encoded), so URL scrubbing via the URL
   parser is behaviourally unchanged. In free-form text, scrubbing
   now preserves trailing log context ("failed with 500", stack
   frames, next log line) instead of greedily eating everything up
   to end-of-string. Any query string or fragment attached to a URL
   embedded in free text goes down with the path identifier — a
   fail-safe: a sensitive value leaking into a query param gets
   scrubbed along with the rest of the URL tail.

2. Rename the email sentinel from "[EMAIL REDACTED]" to
   "[EMAIL_REDACTED]". The literal space in the old form interacted
   badly with the tighter path class: EMAIL_PATTERN runs before
   scrubSensitivePath in scrubSensitiveStrings, and a whitespace
   -bearing sentinel caused the path regex to split its capture
   mid-sentinel ("[REDACTED] REDACTED]"). Data was still scrubbed
   but the output was cosmetically corrupted. Normalizing every
   sentinel to the shape /^\[[A-Z_]+\]$/ restores clean atomic
   replacement. A new sentinel-invariant test block in
   scrubbers.spec.ts locks the rule in place so future scrubbers
   cannot reintroduce whitespace.

Also adds a 12-case table-driven test in sentry-scrub-patterns.spec
covering query params, fragments, multi-line stack frames, tab
-delimited log columns, multiple URLs per line, and sensitive-email
-in-query-string — each exercising a distinct boundary behaviour of
the whitespace-excluding value class.

[#3025] Use atomic_write for orphan domain claim, fixing blind unique-index guard

`CustomDomain.claim_orphaned_domain` called `save` inside a raw
`dbclient.multi` block. Familia's unique-index guard (invoked by `save`)
issues HGETs against index hashes — inside MULTI those return QUEUED
instead of real identifiers, making the guard blind. Under concurrent
orphan claims the method could raise a spurious `RecordExistsError` or
silently bypass validation.

Switch to Familia 2.6.0's `atomic_write`, which runs `prepare_for_save`
(and therefore `guard_unique_indexes!`) outside the transaction with real
reads, then wraps the scalar HMSET, index bookkeeping, and collection
mutations (`add_to_organization_domains`, `owners.put`) into a single
MULTI/EXEC. `atomic_write` returns `true`/`false` rather than nil on
WATCH-abort, so the failure check widens to `result == false || result.nil?`.

For the orphan-claim path the guard check is a defensive pass
(self-reference: `display_domain_index` already points to the orphan's
own identifier), but re-arming it with real reads closes the window for
any future code path that reaches this method with a different claim
scenario.

Independent of #3020 — same surface symptom (`RecordExistsError` under
concurrent claims) but different root cause. #3020 was migration-caused
index corruption; this is a structural bug in the MULTI block.

[#3025] Pin pool connection across WATCH+MULTI; decode hget org_id via JSON.parse

claim_orphaned_domain's outer WATCH landed on one pool connection while
the nested atomic_write's MULTI resolved to another -- each Familia.dbclient
call re-enters connection_provider, which returns a released pool.with
checkout. WATCH never pairs with EXEC under that model, so races go
undetected.

Add Onetime.with_pinned_dbclient: pushes a single pool.with checkout onto
a fiber-local stack that connection_provider consults first. While pinned,
every Familia.dbclient call on the fiber resolves to the held conn. Helper
is reentrant, ensure-safe, and leaves the unpinned fallback byte-identical
for the many single-command call sites. Wrap claim_orphaned_domain in the
pin; rewrite dbclient.watch/unwatch as conn.watch/unwatch for clarity.

Also decode the JSON-wrapped hget(:org_id) so the same-org idempotent
short-circuit actually matches -- Familia v2 JSON-encodes scalar fields,
and the raw compare against bare org_id never hit, making concurrent
same-org retries raise "Domain is registered to another organization".

Consistency decision: kept Phase 2 in upgrade.sh as

command and continued. WRONGTYPE, NOAUTH, READONLY, LOADING, CLUSTERDOWN,
MISCONF, OOM, and corrupt DUMP payloads now abort the run immediately with
exit code 2. These represent environment misconfiguration or structural
data conflict where continuing compounds damage or amounts to retry-spam
against a broken target. Per-record soft errors (Base64, JSON, single-key
issues outside the hard list) still collect-and-continue so all surface in
one pass; exit code 1 is preserved for that path.

Also clarifies the dry-run default contract scope. run_pipeline.sh's
"must default to execute" rule applies to Phase 2 callees only;
enrich_with_original_record.rb is a Phase 4 callee invoked directly by
upgrade.sh with inverted flag semantics. Adds receipt and secret validators
to the --redis-url consistency pattern in run_pipeline.sh, and adds banner
comments to dump_keys.rb and enrich_with_original_record.rb pointing at
the relevant orchestrator contract.

transform.rb and generate.rb behind OTS_MIGRATION_PIPELINE so an
operator can opt in without changing default behavior.

  error tracking and HardLoadError fail-fast on WRONGTYPE, NOAUTH,
  READONLY, LOADING, CLUSTERDOWN, MISCONF, OOM, and corrupt DUMP.
  Default off; "1"/"true"/"yes"/"on" -> batch 500; positive integer ->
  that batch size.
- transform.rb: collapse RESTORE+HGETALL, HMSET+DUMP, and the per-customer
  counter SET+DUMP fan-out. Counter DEL pipeline lives in ensure so a
  mid-batch failure does not leak temp keys.
- generate.rb: collapse RESTORE+HGETALL, organization HMSET+DUMP, and
  membership HMSET+DUMP. DEL stays in ensure on every path.

Truthy parsing is shared across all three: empty / 0 / false / no / off
disables. Memoized so ENV is read once per run.

[#3041] Add customer migration enqueuer skeleton

Structural blueprint for the upstream side of the queue-driven
migration. Builds a sorted set of v1 customer keys scored by updated
timestamp (via ZsetIndexer), iterates lowest-score-first, filters out
records already current in target Valkey DB 0, and publishes filtered
batches of N (default 500) onto a RabbitMQ queue.

Filter decision tree (should_enqueue?) is a pure function fully
covered by 16 passing tryouts. Inputs: (v1_score, v2_status,
v2_migrated_at). Outputs: :enqueue | :skip | :stale_warning.

  - missing v2 record → enqueue (first migration)
  - completed AND migrated_at >= v1 score → skip (current)
  - completed AND migrated_at < v1 score  → enqueue (delta sync)
  - failed                                → enqueue (retry)
  - migrating recent (<5 min)             → skip with warning
  - migrating stale (>5 min)              → enqueue (assume crash)

Known/intentional limitations:
- ZsetIndexer integration (build_or_reuse_sorted_set) is a TODO with
  the call site sketched. Wiring requires deciding final argument
  shape and whether to clear-or-merge the indexer's output zset.
- publish_batch raises NotImplementedError; pending decision on
  app-boot vs standalone Bunny client. Project has Sneakers + a
  BaseWorker pattern but no example publisher in scripts/.
- update_cursor checkpoint storage is sketched; resumability of
  partial enqueuer runs needs a final location decision (source
  Redis vs target Valkey vs file).
- Concurrent enqueuer instances would race on cursor + double-publish.
  Single-instance assumption documented in class header; advisory
  lock TODO if parallel runs become a requirement.
- migration_status comparison uses the actual stored constants
  (completed/migrating from WithMigrationFields::MIGRATION_STATUS),
  not the brief's legacy strings. migrated_at is compared numerically
  as float-seconds.
- Float::EPSILON arithmetic at unix-timestamp scale is a no-op
  (epsilon ≈ 2.2e-16, well below ULP at ~1e9). Tryouts use 1.0s
  deltas instead — relevant if any future cursor logic does score-
  epsilon arithmetic.
- Customer-scoped only. Sister scripts for custom_domain / receipt /
  secret follow the same pattern but live in separate files.

[#3067] Recover parseable Content-Type for malformed/duplicate headers

Some clients (notably the OneTimeSecret PHP client) send two
Content-Type headers: text/html first, application/x-www-form-urlencoded
second. After integrating Rack::Parser in afc519b26, requests in this
shape stop parsing the body, causing V1 POSTs (/api/v1/share, etc.) to
return 404 "You did not provide anything to share".

Add Onetime::Middleware::NormalizeContentType in front of Rack::Parser
to (a) prefer a parseable type when servers comma-join duplicate
Content-Type headers, and (b) sniff the body on POST/PUT/PATCH when the
declared Content-Type is unparseable but the body unambiguously looks
like form-urlencoded or JSON. The body is rewound after sniffing so
downstream consumers see it unchanged.

[#3072] Replace prepend Coercion with Familia BooleanFieldType

The previous Coercion module overrode `verified=` and `verified!` on
the host class via prepend. It worked, but it sat above the model
boundary — pure-Ruby module composition rather than a Familia construct
— and the same pattern would have to be reinvented for the next field
needing canonical string storage.

Introduce Onetime::Familia::BooleanFieldType, a subclass of
::Familia::FieldType that mirrors the upstream EncryptedFieldType
pattern. It overrides:

  * define_setter   — canonicalize input on direct assignment
  * serialize       — canonicalize on database write (covers the
                      fast-writer path, which previously bypassed the
                      setter and reached hset directly)
  * deserialize     — canonicalize on database read, so legacy '1' /
                      '0' values self-heal on next load

A companion BooleanFieldMacro module exposes the field-level
declaration via `boolean_field :name`, registered through Familia's
`register_field_type`. The Status feature now extends the macro and
declares `boolean_field :verified` alongside the regular `field`
declarations; Customer#verified? simplifies to `verified == 'true'`
because the stored form is now guaranteed canonical.

TRUTHY = %w[true 1 yes].freeze documents the accepted truthy aliases
(case-insensitive). Anything else — nil, '', 0, 'false', 'no',
arbitrary strings — canonicalizes to 'false'.

Tryouts coverage in try/unit/familia/boolean_field_type_try.rb
exercises canonicalize/1 across every documented input, the setter
path, the constructor path (Customer.create!(verified: …)), the fast
writer, the legacy-data self-heal, and Customer#verified? predicate
alignment. The file is documented as the reference implementation for
adding type-level value coercion to Familia models in this repo;
future custom field types should follow the same shape.

[#3113] Coerce Familia::Counter to Integer in colonel JSON responses

Familia 2.8.0 added `include Enumerable` on Familia::DataType (the
parent class of Counter), but Counter doesn't implement #each. When
the colonel API endpoints embed counter readers directly in their
response hashes (e.g. secrets_created: cust.secrets_created), the
subsequent JSON serialization triggers ActiveSupport's
Enumerable#as_json, which calls .to_a, which calls .each, which
raises NoMethodError. Every /api/colonel/users* endpoint that surfaced
counters 500'd.

This regression surfaced in CI as 6 admin_interface_spec failures
(Full Mode SQLite job) after the familia 2.7.0 → 2.8.0 bump in
9bcb8d622 (housekeeping needs do_chore! which only exists in 2.8+).

Fix is local and minimal: call .to_i before stuffing counters into
the response hash. Counter#to_i returns the current integer value,
which is what every caller already expected from the field.

The safe_dump_field path already handles counters correctly (via the
counter_field_handler lambda in customer/features/safe_dump_fields.rb
that calls .to_s); only these three colonel logic files accessed
counters bare.

Touched:
  - apps/api/colonel/logic/colonel/list_users.rb (secrets_created,
    secrets_shared)
  - apps/api/colonel/logic/colonel/get_user_details.rb (secrets_created,
    secrets_shared, emails_sent)
  - apps/api/colonel/logic/colonel/get_colonel_info.rb (secrets_created,
    secrets_shared, emails_sent)

(RACK_ENV=test AUTHENTICATION_MODE=full AUTH_DATABASE_URL=sqlite::memory:).

fix(ip): resolve client IP behind RFC-1918 proxy chains (#3107)

Rack's request.ip falls back to REMOTE_ADDR when every hop in
X-Forwarded-For is a private address — the normal case in Kubernetes
where both ingress and client may be RFC 1918. This caused the Colonel
"Banned IPs" page to display the ingress pod IP instead of the real
visitor address, and meant IP bans could never match the right address.

Two root causes fixed:

1. list_banned_ips read metadata[:ip] but IdentityResolution writes
   metadata[:ip_address] — the Colonel page silently fell through to
   'unknown' on every request.

2. All IP-sensitive paths (ban enforcement, session storage, identity
   resolution, audit logging) called request.ip directly, ignoring any
   proxy chain.

Introduces Onetime::ClientIpHelpers with a site-wide TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH
(default 0, preserves existing behaviour) and TRUSTED_IP_HEADER setting.
Set TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH=1 for a standard single-proxy deployment (nginx,
Caddy, Traefik). The helper does not reject private IPs after extraction,
so all-RFC-1918 chains work correctly.

All request.ip / req.ip callers replaced with request.trusted_client_ip
via a Rack::Request mixin loaded at boot. Homepage mode detection retains
its existing private-IP rejection on top for CIDR matching semantics.

Closes #3107

[#3135] Refactor Plan model to family-keyed with nested prices

Plans are now keyed by family ID (e.g., `identity_plus_v1`) instead of
the suffixed form (`identity_plus_v1_monthly`). Per-interval price data
moves into a new `prices` hashkey, with one entry per interval (month,
year). Family-scoped fields (entitlements, features, limits) stay at
the top level.

Drops the redundant scalar fields that encoded a single price:
`stripe_price_id`, `interval`, `amount`, `billing_scheme`, `usage_type`,
`trial_period_days`, `nickname`. Each is now nested inside the per-
interval price hash.

Public surface changes:
- New `prices_hash`, `price_for(interval)`, `available_intervals`,
  `all_stripe_price_ids` helpers replace the dropped scalar accessors.
- `monthly_equivalent_amount` reads from the nested prices.
- `collect_stripe_plans` merges multiple prices for the same product
  into a single family entry.
- `load_all_from_config` creates one Plan per plan_key with nested
  prices, instead of one Plan per (plan_key, interval).
- `build_stripe_price_id_cache` indexes every price_id across all
  intervals to the family record.
- `load_from_config` accepts both family IDs and legacy suffixed IDs
  for backward compatibility.

Companion changes (callers, specs, frontend, docs) follow in subsequent
commits.

[#3107] fix(middleware): use require_relative for ClientIpHelpers in middleware_stack

The bare `require 'onetime/helpers/client_ip_helpers'` only resolved
because config.ru unshifts `lib/` onto $LOAD_PATH before loading the
app. Subprocesses that boot the stack without that setup (e.g. the
Puma fork-registry integration test's rackup) hit LoadError, trip the
rackup's rescue-and-exit-27 path, and never bind a port — surfacing
as "connection refused" rather than the real failure.

Switch to `require_relative '../helpers/client_ip_helpers'`, matching
the loader pattern already used in lib/onetime/middleware.rb:6. No
behavior change in the normal boot path; restores boot under bare
$LOAD_PATH.

Fixes the T3 puma_fork_registry_workflow integration spec.

[#3107] Add Rack-native trusted proxy configuration

Introduce ConfigureTrustedProxy initializer that configures Rack's
built-in IP resolution mechanisms instead of monkeypatching.

Uses Rack::Request.forwarded_priority to control header parsing:
- depth=0: forwarded_priority=[] disables header trust entirely
- depth>0: enables RFC 7239 Forwarded and X-Forwarded-For parsing

Uses Rack::Request.ip_filter to extend trusted proxy ranges:
- Rack's default filter handles RFC 1918 private ranges
- trusted_proxy_cidrs config adds custom ranges (e.g., CDN IPs)

This approach delegates to Rack's well-tested IP resolution rather
than reimplementing header parsing in application code.

[#3107] Simplify ClientIpHelpers to RFC 7239 parsing utilities

Remove the Rack::Request monkeypatch and depth-based extraction logic.
Retain only the header parsing methods needed by HomepageModeHelpers:

fix(cli): surface fatal boot errors instead of "OT.conf is nil" (#3189)

CLI commands previously masked config errors (e.g. deprecated keys) behind
a misleading "Boot failed: OT.conf is nil" warning, then continued past
boot and crashed on Redis. boot! swallowed OT::Problem in :cli mode to
keep REPL sessions alive, which made sense for transient errors but
hid fatal config issues that leave OT.conf unusable.

Introduces a FatalBootError marker module included in ConfigError. boot!
now re-raises any OT::Problem carrying that marker even in CLI mode, so
bin/ots can present the actual error (matching bin/dev's behaviour).
Non-fatal OT::Problem in CLI mode still passes through for REPL debugging.

fix(#3114): preserve validated domain_id for tenant-SSO org join

The before_omniauth_callback_route hook in omniauth_tenant.rb consumed
session[:omniauth_tenant_domain_id] via session.delete for cross-tenant
validation, but two downstream hooks needed to read it:

  - after_omniauth_create_account (omniauth.rb)
  - after_login (login.rb)

Both guarded with `if domain_id`, so JoinDomainOrganization was never
invoked. Tenant-SSO users only got a Default Workspace; OrganizationLoader
fell back to the personal workspace because no tenant org membership existed.

Fix separates "pending validation" from "validated" state by re-storing the
identifier under :validated_omniauth_domain_id after the mismatch check passes.
Downstream hooks now read the validated key; after_login deletes it as the
single point of cleanup once login completes. Cross-tenant validation still
works because the original :omniauth_tenant_domain_id is still consumed
before the comparison, and the validated key is set only on the success path.

exactly once per SSO login:

[#3026] Revert destroy!-as-rollback; explicit per-step rescue instead

The destroy!-based rollback (commit 14c527f) was nominally cleaner but
introduced fragility the new rollback test caught: destroy! transitively
touches helpers (organization_instances enumeration, scoped_memberships
cascade, Familia super) any of which can raise mid-rollback when the
original failure was infrastructure-related. A secondary raise inside
destroy! aborted the cascade and left partial state — every cleanup
step after the raise point was skipped, including the main domain hash
DEL that Gemini originally flagged.

The explicit per-step rollback is more verbose but stable: each step
gets its own rescue StandardError, so one failure can't block the
others. Steps:

  - display_domains.remove (the hsetnx claim)
  - obj.remove_from_class_display_domain_index (Familia auto-index)
  - instances.remove (manual class index)
  - owners.remove (manual class index)
  - HomepageConfig.delete_for_domain! (sibling cleanup)
  - ApiConfig.delete_for_domain! (sibling cleanup)
  - Familia.dbclient.del(obj.dbkey)  ← the orphan fix Gemini caught
  - organization_instances.each { remove_from_organization_domains } —
    uses the in-memory participation set, NOT Organization.load, so
    safe even when the original failure was org-lookup related

The trade-off versus destroy!: we duplicate the cleanup logic (it also
lives in destroy! for the normal-lifecycle path) but gain
defense-in-depth for the error path. If a future write is added to the
create! begin block, the rollback list must be updated alongside —
that's the maintenance cost of explicit-over-magical.

[#3026] Fix S5 setup: missing trailing assertion + S6: raw ZSCORE check

Verified hypotheses about Familia 2.9.1 by writing a probe script
(tested against actual familia gem at the project's pinned version,
Ruby 3.3.6). Key findings:

  - Familia.dbclient.exists? returns boolean (not integer)
  - Horreum dbkey format IS "prefix:identifier:object"
  - Class.instances IS memoized (same object across calls)
  - sorted_set#member? AND #score both work correctly
  - Familia sorted_set instances are FROZEN — define_singleton_method
    on them raises FrozenError. (This is what broke the earlier S5
    attempt that tried to stub instances.remove. The current S5 stubs
    a class method, ApiConfig.delete_for_domain!, which works fine.)

So the actual bug in S5 wasn't a Familia behavior I'd misunderstood —
it was a Tryouts framework requirement: every testcase needs an
`#=>` (or `#=~>`) assertion, otherwise the body code is treated as
bare code between testcases and is skipped. S1-S4 each end their
setup testcase with `@sX_exception_message  #=~> /.../`; S5 didn't.
The setup body never ran, so @s5_captured and @s5_exception_message
were both nil, which cascaded into every downstream NoMethodError.

exact pattern S1-S4 use), with an inline comment explaining the
requirement so this isn't accidentally regressed by a future edit.

with a raw `Familia.dbclient.zscore` lookup against the sorted-set
dbkey directly. The check now tries both `obj.identifier` and

the question of which representation participates_in uses internally.

Fix to_s/message divergence on Problem and Forbidden + cover gemini gaps

gemini-code-assist on PR #3208 flagged that error_resolver_spec only
asserts error.message after resolution and not error.to_s. The instinct
was right — testing revealed a real production bug, not just a coverage
gap.

Onetime::Problem and Onetime::Forbidden both declare attr_accessor
:message, which shadows Exception#message but does not touch Exception's
C-level internal message slot that #to_s reads from. So after
ErrorResolver.resolve! mutates error.message via the accessor:

  error.message  # => "localized text"  (accessor: from @message)
  error.to_s     # => "original text"   (Exception#to_s: from C-level slot)

Anywhere in the request lifecycle that falls through to #to_s — including
SemanticLogger's default error rendering, Exception#inspect, and any
rescue-and-log code — would see the un-localized text. The to_h handler
escapes this because it reads error.message via the accessor, but
log/trace surfaces don't.

Fix is a small to_s override on each base class that delegates to
@message when set, falling back to super (Exception#to_s) otherwise.
Both bases get the same shape; the override is inherited by every
subclass (RecordNotFound, MissingSecret, FormError, EntitlementRequired,
LimitExceeded, GuestRoutesDisabled, GuestRoutesDisabled).

Tests:

- error_resolver_spec.rb: existing "error_key present" test now asserts
  error.to_s alongside error.message so the override stays in place.
- error_resolver_spec.rb: new "preserves an existing non-empty message
  when I18n.t fails" example covering the rescue branch's else path —
  the original gemini comment correctly noted this branch had no
  coverage. The previous test only exercised the empty-message →
  fall-back-to-error_key path.
- errors_spec.rb: new describe block locking down the to_s override
  on one subclass per base (Forbidden + FormError); the behavior is
  inherited, so every leaf class would be redundant.

No production code paths other than errors.rb change; only the to_s
return value is corrected for mutated instances.

fix(#3053): align config schema with shipped YAML shape

The integration spec added in 16dc77a flagged two real schema/YAML
mismatches in the CI run. Both are addressed in this commit (and stay
fixed going forward thanks to the spec).

1. `features.domains.acme.port` accepts string | number.

   The shipped YAML uses `<%= ENV['ACME_PORT'] || '12020' %>`. ERB
   outputs `12020` (bareword), and YAML's implicit-typing rule coerces
   that to an integer at parse time. Schema previously required string;
   port is the same TCP port either way, so widening the type is the
   honest fix.

2. Validator normalizes Ruby Symbols to Strings before JSON Schema
   validation.

   `mail.truemail.default_validation_type: :regex` is a YAML symbol on
   purpose — Truemail (the consuming Ruby gem) expects a Symbol at
   runtime. JSON Schema has no symbol type, so the validator
   round-trips the loaded hash through a Symbol→String transform that
   is scoped to validation only and does not affect what Ruby sees at
   boot. Fix is in `Validate#load_config` / `#stringify_symbols`.

With both fixes the integration spec passes against the real
etc/defaults/config.defaults.yaml.

refactor(#3212): introduce augment helper and remove duplication from config shapes

The first pass at the contract/shape split (commit 45dd88b) restated each
contract's nested structure in the shape file because `.extend()` is shallow
— to put a default on `secret_options.passphrase.minimum_length` you had to
re-declare every sibling under `secret_options`. The shape files came out
~the same length as the contracts they augmented, which is the duplication
the entity-contract convention is supposed to avoid.

This commit adds `src/schemas/utils/augment.ts`, a ~135-line recursive
walker that takes the contract and a tree of overrides where each leaf is
a `(field) => field.someChain()` transform. Unmentioned fields pass
through verbatim, nested objects recurse, and structural wrappers
(.optional / .nullable / .default) are unwrapped before the leaf runs and
re-wrapped around sub-trees. Object-level qualifiers — .catchall(),
z.strictObject, z.looseObject — are preserved by reading the contract's
def.catchall and re-applying it after the spread.

Per-field defaults on partial-override consumers (the deferred PR #3206
suggestion for jobs workers) are now a single-line edit in the augment
tree rather than a contract-side change. The TODO in
shapes/config/section/jobs.ts records this.

Design decisions:

- The leaf receives the *unwrapped* inner type, not the wrapped field, so
  `(n) => n.int().min(0).max(256).default(4)` works on a contract field
  declared `z.number().optional()`. If the shape wants to preserve a
  wrapper around a leaf (rare — `default` already makes a field
  input-optional), the leaf re-applies it explicitly:
  `default_ttl: (n) => n.int().positive().nullable().optional()`.

- Sub-tree entries recurse into a nested ZodObject. The helper unwraps,
  recurses, and re-wraps so `secret_options: z.object({...}).optional()`
  stays optional after augmentation without the tree author touching it.

- Unknown keys throw at construction time with a useful error message
  listing the contract's known keys. This catches typos on the next test
  run / CLI validation with no type-system gymnastics — the alternative
  (recursive conditional generics keyed off the contract's `.shape`) was
  considered and rejected as gold-plating for the marginal value over a
  three-line runtime guard.

- Leaf parameter is `any` because TypeScript can't narrow across the
  tree boundary; the leaf body is written against the field the contract
  declares, and TS catches mis-chained methods inside the leaf.

Hybrids where augment doesn't apply:

- `LimitValueSchema` is `z.union(...)` — reconstructed manually in the
  shape.
- `BillingConfig.entitlements` / `plans` are `z.record(...)` whose value
  schemas need to reference the *shape* versions of EntitlementDefinition
  / PlanDefinition, so those record fields are reconstructed via leaf
  transforms that return a fresh `z.record(..., XxxShape)`.
- `secretOptionsSchema` is a top-level `z.record(...)`, so augment runs
  on `secretOptionBoundariesSchema` and the shape file rewraps it.

JSON Schema generation output is byte-identical to the previous commit
(verified by diffing generated/schemas/config/{static,billing}.schema.json
pre- vs post-refactor — empty diff). All 5458 tests still pass, including
the existing public.spec / sections.spec / billing.spec shape tests that
exercise the defaults and bounds end-to-end.

Tests:
- New src/tests/schemas/utils/augment.spec.ts (17 cases) covering leaf
  overrides, sub-tree recursion, wrapper unwrap/rewrap (optional /
  nullable / nullish), runtime unknown-key guard, and
  catchall/strict/loose preservation.

test(#3212): cover .strict() / .passthrough() / strip in augment helper

In response to gemini-code-assist's suggestion on PR #3223 to copy
`def.unknownKeys` from the contract into the augmented object: that's a
Zod v3 mechanism. In Zod v4, all unknown-key behavior is encoded via
`def.catchall`:

  z.strictObject(...)           catchall: z.never()
  z.looseObject(...)            catchall: z.unknown()
  z.object(...).strict()        catchall: z.never()
  z.object(...).passthrough()   catchall: z.unknown()
  z.object(...)                 no catchall (strip — default)

The helper already preserves catchall, so strict / loose / passthrough /
strip all round-trip correctly. Adding explicit tests for the method
forms (.strict(), .passthrough()) and the strip default to make the
coverage exhaustive.

  - allowed_signup_domains: omit to preserve; provide [] to clear;

  - enabled: optional, preserves existing if omitted

Previously the omniauth callback ran Customer.create! then performed

second write was redundant and, in the existing-customer branch,

[#3221] Apply ADR-013 error wire format to Otto router fallbacks

BaseJSONAPI and V2 still configured router.not_found / router.server_error
with the pre-ADR shape:

  base_json_api.rb: { message: "Not Found", code: "NOT_FOUND" }
                    { message: "Internal Server Error", code: "SERVER_ERROR" }
  v2/application.rb: { error: "Not Found" }
                     { error: "Internal Server Error" } (no error_type)

Bring both into line with ADR-013:

  { error: "<user-facing message>", error_type: "NotFound" | "ServerError" }

`code:` drops since ADR reserves it for per-operation discriminators not
redundant with `error_type` (only GuestRoutesDisabled qualifies today).
`NotFound` / `ServerError` are enumerated in the ADR as legitimate
`error_type` values for router fallbacks.

V1 (apps/api/v1/application.rb) and the web apps' plain-text fallbacks are
out of scope per ADR §"Out of Scope". TypeScript apiErrorResponseSchema
deadwood in src/schemas/api/base.ts is deferred to a separate change.

feat: route build_metadata IP through Rack::Request#ip

The auth strategies' build_metadata helper read env['REMOTE_ADDR']
directly, bypassing the trusted-proxy initializer that rebinds
Rack::Request#ip to honor X-Forwarded-For / RFC1918 filtering /
custom CIDRs / depth-based hop counting. The result: every
metadata[:ip] consumer (audit loggers, banned-IP panel, the new
feedback rate limiter) saw the proxy's IP instead of the real
client whenever the app sat behind Cloudflare or k8s ingress.

Switch the single line to Rack::Request.new(env).ip. When the
trusted-proxy initializer is disabled, Rack falls back to
REMOTE_ADDR — so deployments that haven't opted in see no
behavior change.

skipped before the cascade ran, leaving member entitlements stale even
though the operator explicitly asked for the cascade. Memberships can
drift independently of the org's entitlement set (role changes, invite
acceptance race conditions, partial cascade failures from prior runs),

useful.

idempotent write + cascade — and were not worth the consistency hole.

reach the wire and the status reflects the exception class.
