[#3240] Use explicit rescue clause to propagate OT::Problem

Replaces `raise if ex.is_a?(OT::Problem)` inside the StandardError
catch-all with a dedicated `rescue OT::Problem; raise` clause placed
before it.

Why: Ruby's rescue list is order-sensitive, so a typed rescue listed
first short-circuits the broader StandardError clause without needing
imperative type checks inside the rescue body. The new form makes the
intent obvious — "OT::Problem propagates to the centralized OttoHooks
handler per ADR-013; only truly unexpected errors get logged and
flattened to 500" — and is robust to future contributors adding code
in the StandardError block without remembering the type guard.

Comment in each location names the centralization target so the
"why" survives future refactors.

[#3240] Convert load_organization to raise Onetime::Forbidden

PR #3261 (the PR-1 work) does not register an OT::Problem handler in
OttoHooks; the design is strict typed-only, with unknown exceptions
falling to a generic 500 ('ServerError'). Without conversion, the
three OT::Problem raises in load_organization would have hit that
fallback after the rescue removal, regressing the spec assertions
that expect 403 + 'Access denied' / 'Organization not found' /
'Owner access required'.

Convert all three to Onetime::Forbidden, which is already registered
in OttoHooks (status 403, log_level :warn). Class-specific fields
(error_type: 'Forbidden') now reach the wire per ADR-013, satisfying
the stated PR-2 goal.

Status semantics: all three conditions remain 403 by design. Returning
404 for 'Organization not found' would let an unauthenticated probe
distinguish real extids from random ones; the existing behaviour hides
that signal and is preserved here.

Tighten the propagate clauses from `rescue OT::Problem` to
`rescue Onetime::Forbidden`. OT::Problem from any inner call now
falls through to the StandardError catch-all (still 500, now with
controller-context logging) rather than being silently routed to
Otto's no-context 500 fallback. Bare OT::Problem in inner code is a
PR-4 concern (typed-subclass introduction).

test(auth): harden Auth::Config namespace shim against boot collision

Auth config/unit specs stubbed Auth::Config with plain `module Config` or
`class Config` (no superclass) so production hook/feature/email modules could
load in isolation. If such a file shares an RSpec process with a full app boot,
the registry reopens `class Config < Rodauth::Auth`, and the wrong-typed
constant raises TypeError ("Config is not a class" / "superclass mismatch"),
marking boot permanently not-ready for every later spec.

Replace each stub with the canonical top-level shim
(`Auth.const_set(:Config, Class.new(Rodauth::Auth)) unless defined?`), which is
superclass-compatible with the real definition in both load orders. Move the
production `require_relative` to top level and drop the in-block module/class
definitions.

Integration full-mode admin_interface_spec failed with 19 identical
"Familia::EncryptionError: Key version cannot be nil" errors when creating
encrypted secrets via Receipt.spawn_pair.

Root cause: Familia's encryption key version is a process-global, populated
only by the ConfigureFamilia boot initializer. After the connect_to_db skip

stayed nil and any encrypted-field write raised. admin_interface_spec is the
only full-mode spec that creates encrypted secrets, so it was the only one
that surfaced the missing config.

`force: true`, resetting boot state so the full initializer chain (including
ConfigureFamilia) always runs once for the suite. The encryption key version
is then set globally for the whole run regardless of spec ordering.

fix: reject guest cross-domain share_domain explicitly; allow same-domain (#3311)

Replace the silent ingestion guard with an explicit boundary check, and let
guests create links on the custom domain they are actually visiting (the /guest
endpoints on a branded domain).

A guest may keep a requested share_domain only when they are on that exact
custom domain (case-insensitive match against the Host header / display_domain).
Any other custom domain — a guest on the canonical domain naming a custom one,
or a guest on one custom domain naming a different one — is a cross-domain
smuggle and is now rejected outright (V2: Onetime::Forbidden; V1: FormError),
before the domain is resolved or looked up.

    Guest is on…    | POST body share_domain | Result
    ----------------+------------------------+------------------------------
    custom domain X | X (or omitted)         | allowed — link on X
    custom domain X | a different domain Y    | rejected
    canonical       | any custom domain       | rejected
    canonical       | omitted / canonical     | allowed — link on canonical

The check lives in validate_share_domain (new validate_anonymous_share_domain),
not process_share_domain, because the comparison needs display_domain — and V1
logic objects don't receive domain context until the controller applies it
after construction (controllers/base.rb#apply_domain_context), i.e. only by
raise_concerns. validate_share_domain is the one point where the context is
available in both V1 and V2, so this is also what gives the two versions parity.
process_share_domain reverts to plain ingestion (records the requested domain);
determine_share_domain keeps its anonymous pin as a defensive second layer.

Harden heap dump file handling against secret leakage (#3366)

ObjectSpace.dump_all serializes live String values, so a heap dump from a
secrets product contains plaintext secrets and key material. Write the dump

clobber or follow a pre-planted symlink in a shared /tmp. Document the
sensitivity in the initializer, the analysis script, and .env.reference, and

A heap dump serializes live String values, so it is a memory-disclosure

ptrace restriction. Make it opt-in via should_skip? — the SIGUSR2 trap is only
installed when HEAP_DUMP_ENABLED is truthy, so a disabled deploy carries zero

tmpfs, where a large dump consumes RAM (counting against MemoryMax) and is lost
on restart; /var/tmp is disk-backed and persistent. Document both vars under
DEVELOPMENT ONLY in .env.reference and add should_skip? specs.

Fix #3427: give IP privacy middleware a trusted-proxy config

The IP privacy middleware was mounted with no security config, so Otto's
resolve_client_ip returned REMOTE_ADDR (the proxy hop) without reading
X-Forwarded-For, then overwrote the forwarded headers with the masked
value. Behind a proxy the real client IP was gone before any later
middleware or auth strategy called request.ip, defeating the
site.network.trusted_proxy mechanism from #3116.

Build an Otto::Security::Config that trusts RFC1918/loopback proxy hops
when site.network.trusted_proxy is enabled, and hand it to the middleware
so it resolves the client from the forwarded headers before masking. When
trusted proxy is disabled the helper returns nil and behaviour is
unchanged.

Add reproduction tests isolating the #3424 V3 numeric type mismatch

Issue #3424 (follow-up to #3268): recipients see "no longer available"
immediately because GET /api/v3/.../secret/:id returns lifespan,
secret_ttl, created and updated as JSON strings, which the strict
z.number() V3 schema rejects; gracefulParse throws and UnknownSecret
renders even though the secret was never consumed.

The new tryouts file checks types at every boundary against a real
database (at-rest bytes -> hydrated getters -> safe_dump -> rendered
JSON) and isolates the mechanism:

1. The default write path is fully typed: spawn_pair stores lifespan as
   a bare JSON integer, prepare_for_save stores created/updated as bare
   JSON floats, and safe_dump emits native numbers. This is why the bug
   does not reproduce in a clean environment.

2. Bare numeric bytes at rest are not the mechanism: Oj :strict parses
   unquoted "604800" / "1735142814.123456" back to Integer/Float, ruling
   out v1-era raw values and the floats-stored-as-strings hypothesis
   from the issue thread.

3. The only at-rest state that produces the reported payload is a
   JSON-QUOTED numeric string ('"604800"'). Familia v2 serialization is
   type-preserving by contract, so any writer that assigns a Ruby String
   (unconverted param/config value, console session, raw hset - compare
   issue #3016) poisons the record permanently: it hydrates as String on
   every load, safe_dump has no cast at the boundary, and previewed!
   (save_fields(:state)) never rewrites the poisoned fields. A full
   save() heals updated but never created or lifespan, which gives
   poisoned records a recognizable String-created/Float-updated
   signature.

   no-op for healthy ones (not applied to the model here).

Make the global auth kill switch authoritative over per-domain configs

The runtime gates Core::Controllers::Base#signin_enabled? / #signup_enabled?
(which guard POST /signin and POST /signup) used REPLACE semantics:

    return config.signin_enabled? if config&.enabled?

So an enabled per-domain SigninConfig/SignupConfig could re-enable sign-in
or sign-up even when the operator had disabled it globally (AUTH_ENABLED /
AUTH_SIGNIN / AUTH_SIGNUP) — e.g. during a maintenance or incident lock-down,
a custom domain with enabled=true, signin_enabled=true would keep accepting
logins. Meanwhile the DISPLAY gate (ConfigSerializer#resolve_signin) used AND
semantics, and its own docstring claimed the runtime gate "consults the same
SigninConfig state" — but it did not, so the rendered page and the POST
handler could disagree.

Introduce a single source of truth — SigninConfig.resolve_signin_enabled and
SignupConfig.resolve_signup_enabled — that AND-combines the install-level
capability with the per-domain override (a domain may only narrow, never
widen). Wire the runtime gates and the display serializer through it so they
cannot diverge again.

switch property for both resolvers. The existing resolve_signin display-gate
assertions in try/integration/domain_auth_enforcement_try.rb are preserved.

Security hardening: session deserialization, CSP, shell-exec, YAML loaders

Addresses the four hardening items in #3498.

1. Marshal.load on Redis-sourced session bytes (Medium)
   Marshal.load runs its object graph before it can raise, so the
   rescue -> JSON.parse fallback offered no protection against a crafted
   payload planted at a session key. Session data is JSON-serializable, so
   parse it with JSON.parse directly in both the session CLI
   (lib/onetime/cli/session_command.rb) and the debug middleware
   (lib/middleware/session_debugger.rb). Updated the CLI spec to serialize
   fixtures as JSON instead of Marshal.

2. CSP script-src weakened by 'unsafe-inline' (Medium)
   CSP Level 1 agents ignore nonces and honor 'unsafe-inline', defeating the
   per-request nonce. Removed 'unsafe-inline' from script-src on both the
   development and production policies and rely on the nonce, which the view
   layer (Rhales, sanitizer, vite_manifest) already attaches to inline and
   module scripts. style-src 'unsafe-inline' is intentional (Vite) and left
   as-is.

3. Shell command injection in test_trigger_webhook CLI (Medium)
   Interpolating args into a single-string system() call routes through
   /bin/sh -c, so shell metacharacters execute. Switched to array-form
   system(*cmd), which bypasses the shell entirely.

4. YAML.load -> YAML.safe_load (Low, defense-in-depth / consistency)
   Replaced bare YAML.load in the config loader, logger loader, and the two
   deep-clone round-trips with YAML.safe_load(permitted_classes: [Symbol]),
   matching the existing convention used elsewhere (billing/config.rb,
   operations/config/validate.rb). The deep-clone round-trips additionally
   pass aliases: true because the input is our own YAML.dump output (shared
   object references emit anchors/aliases) — kept the YAML round-trip rather
   than reverting to Marshal per the documented singleton/gibbler issue.

[#3436] Bump otto to ~> 2.3 for upstream IP/trusted-proxy resolution

otto 2.3.0 absorbs the IP and trusted_proxy resolution this app used
to maintain in parallel: a real IPAddr CIDR matcher in
Otto::Security::Config, count-based depth mode (trusted_proxy_depth),
a canonical env['otto.client_ip'] resolved once, and an idempotent
IPPrivacyMiddleware. This bump unblocks deleting our parallel copy.

Upstream work shipped in otto 2.3.0:
  delano/otto#145 - CIDR matcher, canonical client_ip, idempotent
                    privacy middleware, secure? via otto.via_trusted_proxy
  delano/otto#146 - Otto::Utils.resolve_client_ip + IPv6-aware private_ip?
  delano/otto#149 - count-based depth mode + proto-trust decoupled
                    from depth (faithful port of this app's logic)

Residual upstream follow-up tracked at delano/otto#150 (RFC7239
Forwarded header in depth mode); see the header-handling note in the
MiddlewareStack change.

[#3436] Centralize trusted-proxy config in MiddlewareStack

Make ip_privacy_security_config the single place that translates
site.network.trusted_proxy YAML into an Otto::Security::Config, so the
universal IPPrivacyMiddleware mount resolves the client IP once for the
whole stack. Replaces the scattered, parallel trust lists.

  - filter mode: add_trusted_proxy(PRIVATE_PROXY_RANGES) plus each
    operator-configured cidrs entry (otto now does real IPAddr CIDR
    containment, so public CDN ranges work; see delano/otto#145).
  - depth mode: trusted_proxy_depth = depth + 1. otto's chain is
    XFF + [REMOTE_ADDR], one hop longer than our historical XFF-only
    count, so +1 resolves the same client. Remap documented in the
    gem's docs/migrating/v2.3.0.md (delano/otto#149, delano/otto#151).
  - full IP privacy: mask_private_ips = true, preserving what the
    per-router enable_full_ip_privacy! calls provided before they are
    removed.
  - header: Forwarded|Both is logged and degraded to X-Forwarded-For.
    otto 2.3.0 depth/CIDR-walk is XFF-only; RFC7239 support is tracked
    upstream at delano/otto#150 and returns here for free once it lands.

Extends middleware_stack_spec with cidrs, depth +1 remap, header-warn,
and full-masking coverage.

[#3436] Resolve auth-event IP from canonical otto.client_ip

AuthStrategies::Helpers#build_metadata resolved the auth-event IP with
a bare Rack::Request.new(env).ip. That worked only because the
ConfigureTrustedProxy initializer monkeypatched Rack::Request#ip to do
trusted-proxy resolution. With that monkeypatch being removed, the bare
call would silently return an unresolved (and privacy-masked) REMOTE_ADDR
instead of the real client, mislabeling the IP on sign-in/auth events.

Read env['otto.client_ip'] instead — the value the universal
IPPrivacyMiddleware resolves once per request (delano/otto#145). Fall
back to Otto::Utils.resolve_client_ip when the middleware has not run
(standalone strategy invocation in unit tests), then to Rack's #ip as a
last resort, so the trusted-proxy contract holds with or without the
full stack.

Surfaced during the issue #3436 harmonization review; this method was
the one live consumer still depending on the deleted monkeypatch rather
than the canonical key.

[#3436] Mount IP privacy once via the universal stack

Otto 2.3.0's IPPrivacyMiddleware is idempotent: a second pass yields if
env['otto.client_ip'] is already resolved (delano/otto#145). That makes
the per-router mounts redundant now that the universal MiddlewareStack
mount carries the full trust + masking config.

  - Drop router.enable_full_ip_privacy! from all five Otto apps
    (web/core, web/billing, api/base_json_api, api/v1, api/v2). Private-
    IP masking is now provided once by the universal mount
    (mask_private_ips = true in ip_privacy_security_config).
  - Remove OttoHooks#configure_otto_trusted_proxies and its call. It
    mirrored a second, partial trust list (PRIVATE_PROXY_RANGES only)
    onto each router's security config; the single MiddlewareStack
    config now owns trust resolution, so this defense-in-depth mirror is
    dead weight and a divergence risk.
  - Refresh the Base#build_router docstring example accordingly.

One mount, one trust list, one resolution — no app can land with an
inconsistent or missing IP-privacy configuration.

[#3436] Remove ConfigureTrustedProxy Rack monkeypatch

This initializer monkeypatched Rack::Request#ip, #ip_filter, and
forwarded_priority to do trusted-proxy resolution, and in depth mode
overrode #ip to call ClientIpHelpers.extract. otto 2.3.0 now owns that
resolution end to end via Otto::Security::Config + the canonical
env['otto.client_ip'] (delano/otto#145, delano/otto#149), and its YAML
translation moved into MiddlewareStack.ip_privacy_security_config.

With config and consumers migrated to the canonical key, the monkeypatch
is dead. Delete the initializer, its boot-registry require, and its spec.
No Rack::Request IP behavior is patched anywhere after this.

[#3436] Remove ClientIpHelpers; depth resolution now upstream

ClientIpHelpers re-implemented forwarded-header parsing and position-
based (depth) client-IP extraction. otto 2.3.0 hosts this faithfully:
Otto::Utils.resolve_client_ip_by_depth with the same right-to-left hop
counting and proto-trust decoupled from depth (delano/otto#149). Its
sole runtime caller was the ConfigureTrustedProxy depth path, removed in
the previous commit.

  - Delete the helper, its spec, and its tryout.
  - Drop the now-dead require in web/core controllers base.
  - Refresh the HomepageModeHelpers comment: it resolves the client via

Note: otto depth mode is X-Forwarded-For only, whereas ClientIpHelpers

[#I18N] Make the freshness timestamp deterministic across git versions

The SPEC §2.4 gate regenerates de_AT and diffs it byte-for-byte against the
committed artifact. Both the vendor step (sync-resolved.sh) and the gate
(resolved-freshness.yml) derived _meta.generated_at from `git show --format=%cI`,
which renders a UTC commit as "+00:00" on git <2.54 but "Z" on git >=2.54. The
artifacts were vendored on git 2.43 ("+00:00") while the CI runner is on git
2.54 ("Z"), so the gate red-failed on the timestamp line alone for an otherwise
identical instant — the first time it ever actually checked de_AT (PR #3507).

Derive the timestamp identically in BOTH call-sites with
`TZ=UTC ... --date=format-local:'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S+00:00' --format=%cd`: force
UTC and a literal +00:00 offset so the value is a pure function of the commit on
every git version. The committed de_AT.json is already "+00:00", so no re-vendor
is needed; verified byte-identical.

Correlate API error responses with logs via request_id

Backend JSON API errors (e.g. a v3 404 RecordNotFound) returned an Otto-minted
`error_id` in the payload, but that id is a poor support handle: Otto only adds
it to the body in development, and it is logged on the separate 'Otto' logger
whose context carries no request_id. So in production an API consumer's error
payload held no id that appears in our request log, and even in development no
single log line linked the error to the request_id. Meanwhile RequestLogger
already logs request_id (x-request-id) for every request but never recorded
what failed.

Lean into request_id as the one correlation id:

- OttoHooks: every typed error handler now echoes the request's x-request-id
  into the JSON error body and stashes the error_type into env
  (with_error_correlation, nil-safe for the handler unit-test path).
- RequestLogger: include error_type in the request-log payload when an error
  handler ran, so the single line that carries request_id also names what
  failed (e.g. RecordNotFound), regardless of capture mode.
- Document the request_id correlation field in ADR-013 and the OpenAPI error
  schema.

An API consumer can now quote the request_id from the error body (or the
x-request-id header) and we can grep it straight out of the request log, which
also tells us the error_type.

Fix Rack::Lint error from nil-valued HTTP_REFERER in dev

Otto's IPPrivacyMiddleware clears privacy-sensitive request headers
(HTTP_REFERER, HTTP_USER_AGENT) by assigning their anonymized value
"even if nil, to clear original sensitive data". When a request arrives
without a Referer header, this leaves env['HTTP_REFERER'] = nil.

The Rack spec requires CGI-style env keys (those without a period) to
hold String values. A nil is harmless in production, but ViteProxy
enables Rack::Lint in development, which rejects the request:

    Rack::Lint::LintError: env variable HTTP_REFERER has non-string value nil

Add Onetime::Middleware::NormalizeEnv, wired immediately after
IPPrivacyMiddleware, to delete nil-valued CGI keys. This is the
spec-compliant equivalent of the clear the privacy middleware intended
and keeps Rack::Lint useful for catching real middleware bugs.

When jobs are disabled (the default) or RabbitMQ is unavailable,
Publisher#enqueue_email(..., fallback: :sync) delivered synchronously but
unrescued: an unreachable SMTP host raised out of the publisher and the
request returned HTTP 500 - even though the domain record (invitation,
email-change request, etc.) was already persisted before the email step.

Make :sync honour its documented contract ("block and deliver") as distinct
from :raise ("raise on failure"): send_synchronously now rescues delivery

of propagating. This fixes the contract in one place and benefits every
fallback: :sync caller (org invitation create/resend, password reset,
request/resend email change, and the Rodauth delivery hook) - each of which
has a resend or retry path, so the operation degrades gracefully.

same log/report helper for consistent observability.

fix(security): harden CSP precedence and permit Date/Time in config YAML (#3498)

Follow-up to the #3498 hardening, addressing two latent issues surfaced by
the security review.

1. CSP hardened policy is now authoritative when enabled
   apps/api/v1/controllers/helpers.rb#add_response_headers previously returned
   early if a content-security-policy header was already present — BEFORE the
   enabled check — so a weaker policy set by upstream middleware could silently
   bypass the hardened nonce-only policy. The method now returns early only when
   CSP is disabled (leaving any pre-existing header untouched), and when enabled
   it overrides any pre-existing/upstream policy (logging the override via
   OT.lw). Nothing else in the app emits a CSP header, so no legitimate
   per-endpoint policy is clobbered.

   any unquoted date/time in a deployment's config or logging YAML raise
   Psych::DisallowedClass and fail to boot. Widened to [Symbol, Date, Time] at
   all four symmetric sites — config loader (config.rb), logger loader
   (setup_loggers.rb), deep_clone (enumerables.rb), and the config validator
   (operations/config/validate.rb) — so a config that validates also boots.
   Arbitrary Ruby objects (!ruby/object) remain rejected.

[#3547] feat(auth): self-service resend of verification email

Stuck "Unverified" accounts (status_id=1) had no self-service recovery when
their verification link was lost or believed expired: login,
reset-password-request, and email-login-request all reject unverified
accounts via rodauth's open_account? status check (403/401), and the verify
screen only offered "contact support".

Add POST /api/account/resend-verification-email (auth=noauth), a custom Otto
endpoint wrapping rodauth's built-in verify_account_resend internal request.
It returns a uniform 200 {sent:true} for EVERY account state (nonexistent /
verified / unverified / throttled / internal error / feature-disabled) so it
cannot enumerate accounts; outcomes differ only in server-side audit-log
events. Resending reuses rodauth's existing verification-key row and its 300s
throttle, regenerating a current-HMAC link (recovers from secret rotation).
A defined?(Auth::Logging) guard keeps the endpoint safe in non-full
('simple') auth mode where the auth boot chain is not loaded. /api/ paths are
CSRF-exempt by design, which this cold/sessionless recovery flow requires.

Frontend: useAuth.resendVerificationEmail(), a zod response schema, and a
"Resend verification email" sub-form on the verify-account error screen that
always shows the same neutral confirmation (UI-layer anti-enumeration).

Out of scope (documented as future options): reset_password_verifies_account
(needs rodauth >= 2.43.0) and verify_account_grace_period.

contract across account states + a rodauth internal-request guard spec;

[#3486] fix(security): prevent account enumeration in password-reset request (CWE-204)

ResetPasswordRequest leaked account existence: raise_concerns returned for a
registered address but raised "Invalid email address" for an unregistered one,
so an attacker could probe which emails are registered (valid -> generic
success, invalid -> error).

Mirror the existing CreateAccount (#1831) enumeration-prevention pattern:
raise_concerns now validates only the email FORMAT, and process handles
existence uniformly — a well-formed but unregistered address gets the same
generic success response, with no reset secret created and no email sent.
Existing, pending and verified accounts all return the same response, so the
result no longer reveals whether an account exists. The pending branch now
returns the same generic success_data instead of a no-op message.

The response timing still differs (a real account does more work) and is a
weaker residual channel not addressed here.

Adds unit coverage: raise_concerns rejects only malformed addresses and never
queries existence; process returns the generic success with no side effects for
an unregistered email.

Extract shared Onetime::Application::ErrorCorrelation from OttoHooks

OttoHooks#with_error_correlation echoes the request's x-request-id into a
JSON error body and stashes the error_type into the Rack env so RequestLogger
can name what failed on the line that carries request_id (#3518). That logic
is about to be needed verbatim on the Roda /auth surface, so lift it out of
OttoHooks into a standalone, dependency-free module — the same shape as the
sibling ErrorResolver — that every typed-error edge can call.

- New Onetime::Application::ErrorCorrelation.apply(body, env, exception): the
  one implementation, operating only on the body Hash, the Rack env Hash, and
  any Exception. Owns ENV_ERROR_TYPE ('otto.error_type'), the cross-module
  contract key, as a named constant.
- OttoHooks#with_error_correlation becomes a thin adapter: it extracts env
  from the Otto/Rack request (preserving the original nil-/duck-typing safety)
  and delegates. All handler call sites are unchanged.
- RequestLogger reads ErrorCorrelation::ENV_ERROR_TYPE instead of the bare
  'otto.error_type' literal, so writer and reader share one definition.

Pure refactor: no behavior change. The delegation reproduces the previous
return value and env mutations exactly; the existing otto_hooks_spec and
request_logger_spec still cover the Otto path, and a new error_correlation_spec
pins the primitive (request_id echo, error_type stash, nil-safety, class-name
fallback, body-error_type precedence, the contract constants).

Extend request_id error correlation to the Roda /auth surface

Typed errors on the Roda /auth surface are rendered by Auth::ErrorTranslator
and, unlike the Otto JSON API path, did not echo request_id into the error
body or stash error_type for RequestLogger. So a /auth error body carried
error_type but no request_id while its request-log line carried request_id
but not error_type — neither side of the correlation landed (greptile T-Rex
finding on #3518).

Reuse the shared helper extracted in the previous commit:

- Auth::Router's :error_handler runs the translated body through
  Onetime::Application::ErrorCorrelation.apply(body, request.env, e) — the
  same primitive the Otto hooks use. request.env is the same hash RequestLogger
  reads one frame up the MiddlewareStack, so error_type lands on the log line
  that already carries request_id. Auth::ErrorTranslator stays pure (it gains
  only a doc note): correlation lives in the application layer, where OttoHooks
  sits, not in the translator.
- The router-level 404 fallbacks are returned from routing rather than raised,
  so they bypass the handler and stay request-independent — the x-request-id
  response header still correlates them, matching the Otto static fallbacks.
- ADR-013: the request_id note now covers both surfaces via the one shared
  helper; the resolved #3520 future-consideration caveat is dropped.

describe drives it through a capture frame standing in for RequestLogger,
proving request_id lands in the body and otto.error_type in the shared env

fix(security): emit a CSP on Core web pages so the nonce is enforced (#3498)

The Core web app (apps/web/core) generated a per-request CSP nonce and the
view layer attached it to every <script> tag, but NO Content-Security-Policy
header was ever emitted on web responses: application.rb's
router.enable_csp_with_nonce! only sets an Otto flag, and the one method that
turns it into a header (Otto::Response#send_csp_headers) was never called. So
the nonce was inert and the user-facing HTML pages — where inline scripts
actually execute — had no CSP at all. The #3498 item-2 hardening only covered
the V1 API surface (apps/api/v1/controllers/helpers.rb#add_response_headers,
which runs on every carefully-wrapped V1 response), not the web pages.

Changes:
- Add lib/onetime/security/csp.rb (Onetime::Security::Csp.policy) as the single
  source of truth for the hardened, nonce-only directive list. Refactor the V1
  API helper to use it (output byte-identical; the API stays ENFORCING).
- apps/web/core/middleware/request_setup.rb now emits the policy on HTML
  responses, gated on the existing site.security.csp.enabled flag, using the
  Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header. Report-only is a deliberate first
  step (browsers report, don't block); promotion to the enforcing header is a
  planned follow-up. The nonce in the header is the same env['onetime.nonce']
  the views use, so first-party scripts validate. Defensive: never overwrites a
  pre-existing CSP header; disabled / non-HTML responses are untouched.
- Clarify the misleading application.rb enable_csp_with_nonce! comment and the
  stale Caddyfile-example reference to a non-existent security_headers.rb.
- Add a regression-sensitive spec (spec/unit/web/core/csp_report_only_spec.rb)
  and a changelog fragment.

Follow-up (not in this change): report-only currently sets no report-uri/
report-to, so violations surface only in the browser console; wire a reporting
endpoint before promoting to the enforcing header.

Reviewed by a code reviewer and a security specialist before merge. Security
test surface: 88 examples, 0 failures; rubocop --fail-level warning clean.

- §5.8: the two registries are orthogonal composing axes, not a hierarchy.

  but the relation is partial — some capabilities have no owning feature
  (manage_org/manage_members) and some features need no capability split. Model
  as two registries whose gates AND together only where both apply; the
  "feature owns capabilities" view is documentation grouping, not storage nesting.

- §10: separation is the prerequisite for object-level (per-resource) permissions.
  The capability axis extends (subject, verb) → (subject, verb, object); the
  plan-feature axis stays org-wide. Existing seams (domain_scope_id /

  Stage C's storage shape should not foreclose the RBAC → ReBAC/ABAC path.

fix(web): kill CSP script-src eval violation from Zod's JIT probe

Under the strict production CSP (script-src without 'unsafe-eval') the web
app emitted one `script-src -> eval` violation per page load. The source was
Zod v4's object parser: its JIT fast path builds a validator with
`new Function`, and it probes for that capability via `new Function("")` the
first time an object schema is constructed. The probe throws under CSP and Zod
transparently falls back to its standard parser, so nothing broke — but the
violation polluted CSP reports (now that Otto has a reporting endpoint, that
noise matters).

Set Zod to jitless mode before any schema is constructed. The probe is gated
behind `!jitless && allowsEval.value` and short-circuits, so `new Function`
is never called and no violation is emitted. No-op for correctness (under CSP
Zod already used this path) at a negligible validation-speed cost.

- src/plugins/core/configureZod.ts: sets jitless mode
- src/main.ts: imports it first, before any schema-defining module
- src/tests/plugins/core/configureZod.spec.ts: locks the invariant

Verified in a real browser (Chromium) against the production build with
CSP_ENABLED=true: zero CSP violations across /, /signup, /signin; i18n
renders and locale switching (en<->fr_FR) works; zero console/page errors.

Fix double-reveal race on burn-after-reading secrets

Burn-after-reading is the core product promise: a secret may be revealed
to at most one caller. Secret#revealed! / #burned! guarded the terminal
transition only with an in-memory `state?(:new) || state?(:previewed)`
check. Two concurrent requests each load the secret, both observe an
in-memory state of :new/:previewed, and both pass the check, decrypt, and
destroy in lockstep — handing the plaintext to two clients.

Close the race with an atomic compare-and-set in Redis. A Lua script
(executed atomically by Redis's single-threaded command loop) flips the
persisted `state` field out of a revealable value; of any number of
racing callers exactly one wins and may reveal, the rest get false. This
is the same CAS idiom Familia's Lock#release uses, reached through the
connection resolver via `dbclient`. Comparison operands are produced with
#serialize_value so they match the field's at-rest JSON encoding.

The reveal controllers (v1 ShowSecret, v2 RevealSecret, v2 ShowSecret)
now gate plaintext emission on the boolean return value: a losing request
suppresses secret_value so success_data omits it. On the losing path
revealed! also marks the instance terminal in-memory so a trailing
`previewed! if state?(:new)` cannot resurrect the key the winner just
destroyed (previewed! HSETs state and would recreate a zombie hash).

Adds try/unit/models/secret_double_reveal_race_try.rb reproducing the
race window (two instances that both pass the in-memory check) and
asserting the atomic outcome, including a true multi-threaded reveal.

Make previewed! an atomic non-creating CAS; unify state transitions

previewed! persisted its transition with save_fields(:state), an
unconditional HSET that recreates the key if absent. Two latent bugs
followed from that:

  * Resurrection: a previewed! racing a concurrent reveal/burn that
    destroyed the secret would recreate a partial {state:'previewed'}
    hash (and re-add it to the instances index).
  * Reversion / re-exposure: because the write was unconditional it could
    flip a revealed-but-not-yet-destroyed record back to 'previewed',
    briefly re-opening viewable? while the ciphertext still existed.

It also reset the secret's TTL to the full lifespan on every preview, so a
repeatedly-viewed link never expired on schedule -- contradicting the
method's own comment and undesirable for a burn-after-reading product.

Replace it with the same atomic compare-and-set used by revealed!/burned!,
generalized into one primitive (compare_and_set_state!) that flips state
only from an allowed set of source states. The Lua runs atomically in
Redis, so the transition fails closed: a missing key (destroyed) or an
already-advanced state simply loses -- it can neither resurrect nor revert
a record, and no longer touches the TTL.

Extends the race tryouts with the resurrection and reversion cases.

Add Secret#reveal!; v2 reveal/show enforce the gate by construction

The per-controller "decrypt, then revealed!, then remember to suppress the
plaintext if the claim was lost" pattern kept the burn-after-reading
invariant correct only by every call site remembering to check a boolean.
A future v2 endpoint could reintroduce the leak by forgetting it.

Add Secret#reveal!, the plaintext-returning sibling of #revealed!: it wins
the atomic claim and ONLY then decrypts and returns the plaintext, cascades
the receipt, and destroys the record; a losing caller gets nil and never
computes the plaintext. Because decryption lives inside the won-claim
branch, a caller cannot obtain the plaintext without also winning the one
permitted reveal -- the invariant is enforced by construction. The shared
claim/consume steps are factored into win_reveal_claim!/consume_after_reveal!
so #revealed! (used by verification-consume and the legacy v1 flow) and
#reveal! share one implementation.

The v2 RevealSecret and ShowSecret controllers now reveal via #reveal! and
present the result: no separate decrypt step, and no gate to forget. As a
correctness follow-on, the success log and secrets_shared counters are gated
on actually winning, so a request that lost the race no longer logs success
or inflates the metrics. v1 (legacy) keeps its existing #revealed! + gate.

v2 gate specs now hold viewable? true across the race window so they
exercise the real #reveal! claim (the destroyed key makes viewable? false
otherwise, short-circuiting before the reveal).

fix(ui): never render a silent blank page on a render failure

Diagnosis of the custom-domain "blank sign-in page" report.

## What happens

On a custom domain, once an account becomes a *member* of the domain's
organization (e.g. after being invited), the server's OrganizationLoader
selects the DOMAIN org as the active org (role: member, is_default: false)
instead of the account's personal workspace (role: owner, is_default: true)
— which is why signing in on the canonical site still works. This differ-
ential is confirmed end-to-end (executed against the real backend +
serializers): the server always ships a valid SPA shell with well-formed,
schema-valid bootstrap, and the authenticated workspace renders correctly
for that member/domain-org state.

The user-visible failure is therefore a *client-side* render failure that
degrades to a silent white screen, because the app had no fallback for it:

- The global error handler (src/plugins/core/globalErrorBoundary.ts) only
  logs render/setup errors to Sentry — it renders nothing. When a route
  component throws during setup()/render, Vue tears the subtree down and the
  <router-view> slot is left empty → a blank page instead of an error.
- src/router/index.ts intentionally omits router.onError(), so a failure on
  the initial navigation also leaves the app with no visible state.

## Fixes (defence in depth against the blank-page class)

1. RouteErrorBoundary (new): wraps the active route component. On a thrown
   subtree it renders a visible "something went wrong" panel with a reload/
   home affordance, reports the error to Sentry itself, and resets on
   navigation. A render/setup failure can no longer be a blank screen — and
   the real error is now surfaced (console + Sentry) for pinpoint follow-up.

2. useDisabledConfig / DisabledHomepage: validate the resolved disabled-
   homepage variant against the enum. `??` alone only skips null/undefined,
   so an empty-string or unrecognised store value reached the dispatcher's
   VARIANTS[variant] as an unknown key -> <component :is=undefined> -> a
   blank page. It now falls back to the default variant, with a
   belt-and-suspenders guard in the dispatcher.

Tests: RouteErrorBoundary (throw -> fallback, healthy passthrough, reset on
nav) and two useDisabledConfig cases (empty / unrecognised variant ->
default). Full vitest for the touched areas, vue-tsc, eslint and prettier
all pass.

Fix F7: rate-limit passphrase attempts on burn and v1 show

The audit (F7) and PR review flagged that v1/v2 BurnSecret accept
unlimited passphrase guesses: each wrong guess is a free brute-force
oracle, and a correct guess destroys the secret as a side effect. While
fixing it, the same gap turned up in v1 ShowSecret - only the v2
show/reveal paths included PassphraseRateLimiter.

All three logic classes now use the same limiter as v2 show/reveal:
check_passphrase_rate_limit! before the passphrase comparison (5 failed
attempts per secret in 10 minutes -> 30-minute lockout, surfaced as
HTTP 429 via the existing LimitExceeded translation),
record_failed_passphrase_attempt! on a wrong guess, and
clear_passphrase_rate_limit! on success. In v1 ShowSecret, recording is
gated on a non-empty passphrase so the initial preview of a protected
secret never accrues attempts (matching v2 ShowSecret).

The F7 entry in the DPA audit doc is updated to record the fix and
correct its overstated claim that all show/reveal paths were already
protected.

Verified: 496 rspec examples across apps/api/v1 + v2 (9 new
rate-limiting examples), 12/12 passphrase_rate_limiter tryouts.

Harden HTTP error/exception logging against query-string and param leaks

RequestLogger's per-request access log already defaulted to minimal
capture (method/path/status/duration, no params or headers), matching
Django's django.server logger stance. The gap was on the exception/
error-reporting side: several capture_error/capture_exception call
sites (apps/api/v1/controllers/helpers.rb, apps/web/core/middleware/
error_handling.rb) attached req.url -- the full URL including the
query string -- to Sentry context and, in error_handling.rb's direct
http_logger calls, straight to the application log with no redaction
at all (Sentry's before_send URL scrubbing never runs on that path).

Add Onetime::ErrorHandler.safe_request_context, a shared helper used
by all of those call sites: it always uses path (never the query
string) plus method/ip, and only attaches request params when their
name is on a new opt-in allowlist (logging.http.allowed_error_fields /
LOG_HTTP_ALLOWED_ERROR_FIELDS), empty by default. With nothing
allow-listed, a request that raises an unhandled exception logs
identically to any other request -- mirroring Django's
SafeExceptionReporterFilter stance of hiding request data unless a
view explicitly opts fields in, rather than a blocklist that can lag
behind new sensitive field names.

RequestLogger's :debug capture mode (opt-in via LOG_HTTP_CAPTURE=debug)
is aligned to the same allowlist: its params filter was a small
hardcoded blocklist, and its headers capture had no redaction at all
(Cookie/Authorization included verbatim). Both now gate on the shared
allowlist.

Existing request_id/error_type correlation on error responses is left
untouched -- those are safe, non-sensitive correlation metadata, not
request parameter data, and are already covered by existing tests.

fix(web/csp): make the Content-Type default casing-robust at the Core chokepoint

RequestSetup#finalize_response defaulted the response Content-Type with a
lowercase-only `headers['content-type'] ||=`. A capital-cased 'Content-Type'
from an upstream layer slips past that check, so the default injects a
*second*, lowercase 'content-type: text/html' key — and because Otto's Writer
reads Content-Type case-insensitively, that spurious default can then draw a
CSP onto a response that was really non-HTML.

The bug is dormant today: only the Core app traverses this middleware and Core
emits lowercase header keys throughout (the auth/billing apps that set
canonically-cased headers mount at their own prefixes and never pass through
here). But leaning on that scoping to stay correct is fragile, so harden the
chokepoint itself rather than document around it.

- Extract #ensure_content_type with a case-insensitive presence check, so a
  Content-Type set under any casing counts as "already set" and is never
  double-written.
- Add #call integration specs that drive the full finalize_response path (not
  #emit_csp_header in isolation): a missing Content-Type still defaults to HTML
  and gets a CSP; a canonically-cased Content-Type is neither double-written
  nor, when non-HTML, given a CSP. Both new specs fail against the old ||=
  (verified), so they lock the fix against regression.
- Update the middleware and spec docs to describe the now-robust behavior
  instead of caveating the scoping invariant the previous commit leaned on.

files inject `IDENTIFIER_SECRET=${IDENTIFIER_SECRET:-}` -- an empty string

secret creation after the familia bump (unset), and a docker install would
silently HMAC every identifier under an empty key (blank).

whenever IDENTIFIER_SECRET is absent or blank, using the same HKDF purpose
(:identifier) that init.rake writes to .env -- so booted-from-init and
booted-without-init deployments converge on one key. An explicitly-set value is
used verbatim. This replaces the old passthrough bridge, which propagated the
empty string unchanged.

verified_identifier? yet, so tags minted under any prior fallback/empty key
still resolve. Verified against familia 2.11.0 with IDENTIFIER_SECRET unset:
the API suites boot and pass where they previously raised KeyError.

Tryout covers unset, blank, explicit, and init.rake-convergence paths, guarded
to stay green on both familia 2.10.1 and 2.11+.

history, the Referer header, proxy/CDN access logs and Sentry. Three PR
reviewers flagged this, and it is the same exposure the disclosure matrix
names in finding F6 ("the URL is the bearer secret — and it leaks").

- useAuth.signup() pushes { path: '/check-email', state: { checkEmailAddress } };

  survive a refresh or shared link).

  link, so the page degrades to the generic copy. "Start over" no longer
  forwards the email (correcting a typo means retyping it — and keeps PII
  out of the URL).

  nav breadcrumbs, event.request.url and event.transaction — even on

  VALUE scrubbing only; it no longer disables the email/secret net. This
  covers the grandfathered /signin & /signup ?email= usages too.

- Custom ESLint rule ots/no-pii-in-query flags query: { email } literals.

Add org-scoped audit trail backing the audit_logs entitlement

Organization customers are sold an audit_logs entitlement (admin-tier,
"advanced" plans) that until now had no implementation behind it. This
builds the first functional slice on top of the receipt access timeline
introduced for #3633.

- Organization::Features::AuditTrail: one capped sorted set per org
  (10k newest events, no TTL; orgs are permanent). Events are plain
  hashes (kind, at, receipt/secret shortids, nonce); the nonce keeps
  identical same-second events from silently overwriting each other.
- Fan-out: Receipt#record_org_audit_event mirrors access-timeline events
  (status_get/secret_get) and lifecycle transitions (previewed/revealed/
  burned/expired/orphaned) into the owning org's trail; secret creation
  is recorded where org context is attached (base_secret_action).
  Best-effort by design: a trail failure never breaks or reverts the
  product action, and events carry shortids only - full identifiers are
  capability tokens and must not leak into the trail.
- GET /api/organizations/:extid/audit-events: paginated newest-first
  read, gated by require_entitlement_in!(org, 'audit_logs') so only
  active members whose role/plan intersection grants audit access can
  read it.
- Fidelity fix surfaced by the new specs: Receipt#expired! had no state
  guard (secret_expired? stays true forever), so every later view of an
  expired receipt re-ran the transition - redundant saves, duplicate
  logs, and duplicate audit events. It now fires only from new/previewed,
  matching its sibling transitions.

Specs pin the audit-fidelity contract: completeness (each event exactly
once, guarded transitions can't double-record), accuracy (kind/at/context,
same-second retention, cap evicts oldest only), isolation (right org only;
org-less receipts write nowhere), containment (trail failures swallowed),
non-leakage (no full identifiers), and endpoint authz (entitlement, not
mere membership).

Part of #3633 (PR #3635).

fix(auth): pass post-verification signal via history state, not ?verified=1

verifyAccount() sent users to /signin?verified=1, and Login.vue deliberately
left the param in the URL: stripping it via router.replace would change
fullPath and remount the fullPath-keyed routed component in App.vue,
discarding the success banner. Greptile flagged the leftover flag as a P1 --
the one-shot param was never cleaned up, so a refresh re-triggered the banner,
contradicting the PR's stated contract.

Hand the signal over via router history state (SIGNIN_VERIFIED_STATE_KEY)
instead. Login.vue reads it from window.history.state and clears just that key
immediately after. Because only history state changes -- path and query (and
thus fullPath) are untouched -- the routed component is NOT remounted and the
banner survives, while the flag becomes genuinely one-shot: a manual refresh
re-reads the now-cleared state and does not re-show the banner. The URL stays
clean (/signin), consistent with the same "keep transient state out of the
URL" approach used for the signup email.

Tests seed window.history.state directly (memory history does not touch
window.history) and assert the banner shows once, nothing lands in the URL,
and the flag is cleared after the first render.

fix(receipt): show a generated secret's value exactly once (#3633)

creator-side plaintext preview re-showable: v2 re-revealed it on every

breaks the "one time" guarantee for generated passwords, which are
shown nowhere else.

Both paths now claim the display atomically via a new
secret_value_shown_at field, so a repeated or concurrent load never
re-reveals the value. The claim is taken at display time (at-most-once):
a lost response forfeits the reveal rather than risking a second one,
matching the old state gate. generated_value_display_ttl now bounds only
WHEN the single reveal may occur, not how many times.

The claim primitive (claim_once!) is a single Lua check-and-set:
existence-guarded (never resurrects a destroyed receipt), TTL-neutral
(HSET on an existing hash, safe on a GET), and decided atomically so
simultaneous first-loads cannot both win. HSETNX cannot serve here
because Familia persists every declared field on save, so the field is
never absent; the script instead claims unless the field already holds a
numeric timestamp, which also fails closed if nil serialization changes.

record_receipt_view! reuses the same primitive, so concurrent first
loads of a receipt now record exactly one 'receipt_viewed' audit event
instead of racing to record two.

fix(receipt): guard state transitions with atomic CAS to stop TTL-evicted resurrection (#3625)

Receipt state transitions (revealed!, orphaned!, burned!, expired!)
persisted via `save update_expiration: false`, which issues an
unconditional HMSET. HMSET on a missing key CREATES it, and with the
EXPIRE step suppressed the recreated hash had no TTL. If a receipt's
Redis key was TTL-evicted between load and transition, the in-memory
`state?(:new)` fast-path still passed and the save resurrected the hash
as an immortal (TTL-less) key, re-registering it in receipt:instances.
A stale instance could likewise revert an already-advanced state.

Gate each transition on an atomic compare-and-set on the persisted
`state` field, mirroring the Secret STATE_CAS_SCRIPT from #3615. The

feat(colonel): email deliverability — suppression list, feedback ingest, outbound guard

The console could prove mail was SENT (emails_sent, test send) but showed
nothing of what came BACK — bounces, complaints, suppressions: exactly the
data that diagnoses a transactional-reputation problem. This lane builds the
receiving side, full-stack.

Model (Onetime::EmailSuppression, the AdminAuditEvent capped-storage idiom):
- Suppression list keyed for exact-address O(1) lookup (entries hash +
  created-at index for newest-first pages; oldest trimmed past 100k).
  Entries carry address/reason(bounce|complaint|manual)/source/created.
- Capped bounce/complaint event feed (10k, trimmed on write) + a lifetime
  sends_skipped counter.

Ingestion:
- Asynchronous ESP feedback: Onetime::Operations::Email::IngestFeedback
  behind POST /api/colonel/email/deliverability/events — deliberately NOT a
  public webhook (an unauthenticated bounce receiver is a suppression-
  injection vector); an operator relay (CLI/cron) authenticates as colonel
  and POSTs normalized {email, kind, reason?, source?} records (batch <=500,
  per-record rejection never fails the batch). bounce/complaint => feed
  event + suppression; 'suppression' => import-only. ONE AdminAuditEvent
  per accepting batch (email.deliverability_ingest); zero-accept batches
  audit nothing. Intended flow documented in the endpoint class.
- Synchronous hard bounces: Delivery::Base#deliver records SMTP 5xx
  recipient rejections (Net::SMTPFatalError only — auth/API/config failures
  are sender-side, not bounces) into the feed. Event-only: no
  auto-suppression from a single sync failure.

Outbound guard (the actual reputation protection): Delivery::Base#deliver —
the chokepoint every backend and entry point converges on — checks the
suppression list before perform_delivery. One HEXISTS, FAIL-OPEN twice over
(model + call site): a Redis error can never block sending. Skips are
logged as 'suppressed', counted, and never tick emails_sent.

Colonel API (all sessionauth+role=colonel, both router and logic gates):
- GET  /email/deliverability                        summary counts + window
- GET  /email/deliverability/suppressions           newest-first pages +
                                                    EXACT-address search
- DELETE /email/deliverability/suppressions/:address guarded remove via
  Operations::Email::RemoveSuppression (one email.suppression_remove audit
  event with the lifted reason; :not_found no-op unaudited, 404)
- GET  /email/deliverability/events                 paginated feed

Switch checkout session idempotency keys from deterministic to UUID

Checkout session creation used deterministic time-bucketed idempotency
keys (daily SHA256 in live mode / per-minute in test mode on the API
path; plaintext per-minute on the redirect path). Stripe caches
responses by key, so a same-window retry returned the original -
possibly already-completed - session ("You're all done here"), and
reusing a key with changed session parameters raised
Stripe::IdempotencyError.

Session creation is pre-payment and side-effect free: duplicate
sessions expire unused, and duplicate completions are deduplicated by
the checkout.session.completed webhook handler. Each attempt now sends
a fresh SecureRandom.uuid.

Deterministic keys remain in place where they are correct - mutation
calls whose retries must collapse to one applied change: change_plan
keeps its 5-minute-window SHA256 key, and StripeClient's UUID-based
fallback generator is unchanged.

- Add test asserting two rapid checkout attempts get distinct keys
- Add ADR documenting the session-vs-mutation key strategy
- Document idempotency strategy in stripe-configuration.md

Defer federated subscription claim until email is verified

apply_pending_federation! ran from the standard email/password
after_create_account hook — before the verification email was even sent —
yet its own doc claimed the user had verified their email. Someone who
knew a paying subscriber's email could register that email in another
region and, at account-creation time, claim and destroy the victim's
PendingFederatedSubscription, stealing the federated benefit.

Gate the claim on email verification:
- CreateDefaultWorkspace gains a require_verification: flag. The standard
  signup hook passes verify_account_enabled?, so when verification is on the
  claim is deferred and re-invoked from after_verify_account once the user
  proves email ownership. The default workspace is still created at signup;
  only the federated-subscription claim is gated.
- The gate sits above compute_email_hash!, so a deferred (unverified) org
  gets no indexed email_hash until it verifies and cannot match federated
  webhooks in the meantime.
- Pre-verified/trusted callers keep claiming immediately: SSO (IdP
  verified), invite (never reaches this path), post-payment billing, and
  authenticated lazy creation all use the default require_verification:
  false. When verify_account is disabled there is no verification step to
  defer to, so immediate-claim behavior is preserved.

claim_pending_federation is idempotent and a safe no-op when the customer
is unverified, has no org, or the pending record was already consumed.

Secret Activity: thread actor identity onto revealed/burned events (#3639)

The lifecycle events `revealed` and `burned` previously carried no actor at
all, even though the org audit trail already distinguishes creator vs
third-party fetches. "Who revealed it" is the first question an auditor asks;
this closes the highest-value capture gap in the pipeline.

The emit happens deep inside the atomic consume cascade
(Secret#reveal!/#burned! -> Receipt#revealed!/#burned! ->
record_org_audit_event), which has no request context. Per the ticket's
recommendation, the actor discriminator is computed at the request-scoped
logic layer (where `cust` is in scope) and threaded down through the cascade
as an opaque `actor_context` keyword, preserving the exactly-once guarantee of
the CAS-gated transition (a paired logic-layer event would risk divergence).

- New V2::Logic::Secrets::ActorAttribution#lifecycle_actor_context computes
  creator / authenticated_other / anonymous, mirroring the EXACT ownership
  logic (and anonymous_user? guard) already used for fetch telemetry. The
  guard is load-bearing: a guest link (owner_id nil) revealed by an anonymous
  caller (objid nil) would match nil == nil in Secret#owner? and be
  misattributed to the creator; gating on !anonymous_user? first prevents it.
- reveal_secret / burn_secret / show_secret compute the context before the
  secret is consumed and pass it to reveal!/burned!.
- Secret#reveal!/#revealed!/#burned! and Receipt#revealed!/#burned! take an
  `actor_context:` keyword defaulting to nil, so v1 and account-verification
  paths keep working; a nil/blank actor is recorded as `anonymous`, never
  misattributed to the creator.
- Receipt#record_org_audit_event forwards **event_attrs (shared, additive
  change coordinated with #3640).
- actor_id, when included, is an 8-char shortid of the customer objid
  (mirrors Receipt#shortid) for authenticated actors only -- never an email
  or full custid, and omitted for anonymous.

Fidelity specs extended across the four suites: creator / authenticated_other
/ anonymous for both reveal and burn (end-to-end through the org trail),
exactly-once emission with the actor present, the CAS race-loser recording
nothing, and the anonymous-guest never-misattributed privacy pin.

Capture privacy-safe network context on secret fetch events (#3640)

Fetch events (status_get, secret_get, and the creator_/previewed
variants) now carry the caller's network context in the org audit trail,
recorded only as a reduced, non-reversible representation:

  - net_ip_partial : IPv4 last octet zeroed (IPv6 last 80 bits)
  - net_ua_partial : user agent with version/build identifiers stripped
                     and truncated
  - net_ip_hash    : keyed HMAC-SHA256 over the PARTIAL IP, for
                     correlation without disclosure

The raw dotted-quad IP and the full user-agent string are never stored,
matching the trail's existing "shortids only, no capability tokens"
posture.

New Onetime::Security::RequestContext centralizes the reduction and
re-applies it unconditionally and idempotently, so even if Otto's
edge IPPrivacyMiddleware is disabled or a future change routes a raw
value here, the stored attributes stay masked. The correlation hash is
keyed with the app's global secret (== site.secret), the same root used
for the app's other keyed digests; it is stable across requests
(correlatable) but not reversible. We deliberately avoid Otto's
daily-rotating hash key, whose rotation would break long-horizon
correlation.

Threading: the logic layer reads ip/user_agent from the auth
StrategyResult metadata and passes the reduced context into
record_access_event(kind, context:), which forwards it through
record_org_audit_event(**event_attrs) to the org trail. The
record_org_audit_event change is purely additive (a **event_attrs
splat) so it composes with the sibling actor-identity work (#3639) on
the same seam. The saturation fan-out guard is unchanged.

Privacy decision documented in ADR-022.

Tests: a dedicated RequestContext unit spec plus fetch-path specs assert
the masked partial IP, partial UA, and keyed hash are present and stable,
and -- as the primary safety net -- a no-regression guard asserts no
recorded event attribute can ever contain a raw IPv4/IPv6 or the full UA.

Audit unverified federated claims when verify_account is disabled

The federated-subscription verification gate defers the standard-signup
claim until email verification. But when a deployment disables
verify_account there is no verification step to defer to, so the claim
still runs immediately with no proof of email ownership — an attacker who
knows a subscriber's email could register it here and steal their pending
cross-region subscription. Gating on verified? cannot fix this: without
verify_account the Redis customer.verified flag never becomes true and no
after_verify_account hook exists to re-claim from, so requiring
verification would silently disable federation for that config.

Rather than change happy-path behavior, detect the risky combination
(federation active AND verify_account disabled) at claim time and emit a
loud, structured security-audit log naming the org, email-hash prefix, and
plan, noting the benefit was claimed without email verification. Document
the residual precisely in CreateDefaultWorkspace and the account hooks.

Add a full-stack integration spec that drives the real Rodauth signup hook
(Auth::Config.create_account via internal_request) to prove both branches
end-to-end: verify-enabled defers the claim (then claims once verified),
and verify-disabled claims immediately and emits the audit log. Documents
what is exercised through the real hook vs. replayed, since the one-shot
Auth::Config cannot be reconfigured in-process to fire the real
after_verify_account endpoint.

feat(C10): boot-time SECRET verifier — detect key/data mismatch at boot

QS-6 part 1: nothing bound the running SECRET to the data it encrypted —
a lost .env, regenerated secrets, or a restored dump booted clean while
every pre-rotation ciphertext was silently unrecoverable.

Onetime::SecretVerifier stores an HKDF-derived, purpose-separated
verifier (new KeyDerivation purpose :key_verifier, runtime-only) at
onetime:secret_verifier. The CheckSecretVerifier initializer
(depends_on :familia_config) adopts it on first boot (SET NX), and on
mismatch logs a multi-line error naming the two likely causes and the
fix commands. Policy knob site.secret_verifier_mode /
SECRET_VERIFIER_MODE: warn (default — halting would brick running
deploys on upgrade), enforce (SecretVerifierMismatch, FatalBootError),
off (escape hatch). State cached on Onetime.secret_verifier_state.

Surfacing: /health/advanced gains a secret_verifier sub-check (only a
mismatch degrades; :unavailable maps to not_configured so the keydb
check owns connectivity failures). rake ots:secrets:verify exits
0 ok / 1 mismatch / 2 never adopted / 3 unreachable ('never adopted'
read from the boot state, since boot itself adopts). rake
ots:secrets:adopt re-stamps after an intentional rotation — requires
CONFIRM=yes and prints the live-secret count it would strand. doctor
gains an app-context check that shells the verify task.

Also defines SecretUndecryptable (used by the reveal path, next commit).
Proof: try/unit/boot/check_secret_verifier_try.rb (12 cases) +

feat(C10): non-destructive reveal — roll the claim back on a wrong-key decrypt

QS-6 part 2: Secret#reveal! persisted the atomic reveal claim (CAS
new/previewed -> revealed) BEFORE decrypting, so a wrong-key decrypt
raised Familia::EncryptionError after the claim committed: the request
500'd, the record survived, but state=revealed is terminal — restoring
the correct SECRET could never un-burn it, and each retry on another
secret burned that one too.

reveal! now captures the pre-claim state and, when decryption raises
Familia::EncryptionError, CASes revealed -> prior state (only the claim
holder can be in :revealed, so this cannot race another winner), restores
@state, records a best-effort reveal_failed_undecryptable org-audit
event, and raises SecretUndecryptable. Zero plaintext was produced, so
returning the claim preserves ADR-019's at-most-once display. Race
semantics are unchanged (existing race tryouts still green); revealed!
(consume-without-decrypt) and burn are deliberately untouched, and v1
decrypts before claiming (incidentally non-destructive) — left as is.

SecretUndecryptable maps to HTTP 503 with code secret_undecryptable via
the otto_hooks chokepoint (503 precedent: Billing::CircuitOpenError) and
an i18n message telling the recipient the link is intact and the site
operator must restore the key. The non-2xx makes the UI revert to
click-to-reveal — exactly right, the secret IS still revealable.

Fast-fail: ShowSecret/RevealSecret raise_concerns raises the typed error
before any CAS when the boot verifier flagged a mismatch, gated on the
continue param (reveal intent) so metadata-only requests keep answering.

Proof: try/unit/models/secret_reveal_rollback_try.rb (6 cases: rollback,
survival, recovery, previewed prior-state, in-window race, revealed!
untouched) + 4 RSpec examples in reveal_secret_spec.rb (fast-fail with
no CAS taken, continue gating, rollback through the logic layer).

feat(C10): SECRET_PREVIOUS decrypt-only rotation chain + backup/rotation runbook

QS-6 part 3. ConfigureFamilia.build_encryption_keys (pure, unit-testable)
now derives Familia's encryption_keys map:

- No SECRET_PREVIOUS (the overwhelmingly common case): byte-identical to
  the previous configuration — v1 legacy SHA-256 + v2 HKDF from the
  current SECRET, writes tagged :v2 (asserted by tryout).
- SECRET_PREVIOUS set (comma-separated, oldest first — append the
  outgoing SECRET each rotation): :v1/:v2 map to the OLDEST previous
  secret (every v1/v2 envelope predates the first rotation), every
  previous secret registers decrypt-only under a content-addressed tag
  r<first-8-hex> of its :key_verifier derivation, and the current
  SECRET's content tag becomes the tag for new writes. Content
  addressing makes every generation's tag unambiguous with no rotation
  counter to persist.

The design's implementation checkpoint passed: familia 2.11.2 resolves
envelope key_version with symbol/string fallback (get_master_key), so
arbitrary tags round-trip — proven live in the tryout by decrypting a
pre-rotation :v2 envelope under a rotated mapping and round-tripping a
new envelope written under an r-tag.

fix(ci): swap Caddy TLS issuer to internal CA for the localhost ingress check

full-stack-smoke's Caddyfile-example forces the ACME issuer (correct
for real deployments — no silent fallback to a self-signed cert if
ACME fails), but DOMAIN=localhost here can never qualify for a public
certificate. ACME issuance failed outright at boot ("does not qualify
for a public certificate"), so Caddy never had a cert to present and
the ingress curl got a bare TLS handshake failure (exit 35) — not a
Caddy 2.11.4 regression, this step had never actually passed before
(blocked first by the build, then boot, then the worker).

committed) Caddyfile-example's `tls { issuer acme {...} }` block for
`tls internal` via a brace-depth-counting awk transform, guarded by a
grep check that fails loudly if the block's shape ever changes. curl
already runs --insecure, so it accepts the resulting self-signed cert.

unlike the app image's own Dockerfile (which installs libsodium23 in

leaves RbNaCl partially loaded — RbNaCl::Hash never gets defined — so
any Familia encrypted-field write (e.g. secret.ciphertext=) raises
NameError: uninitialized constant RbNaCl::Hash. Pre-existing failure,
unrelated to today's other CI fixes.

[#3731] Add domains remove Operation + colonel & CLI adapters (P3 of #3731)

Domain removal becomes a reusable Operation in
lib/onetime/operations/domains/remove.rb (mirrors the Transfer op), wrapped by
a colonel DELETE endpoint AND a bin/ots domains remove command — one audited
code path for the toolbox and the UI.

- Remove mirrors DomainsAPI::Logic::Domains::RemoveDomain teardown verbatim
  (delete_vhost -> DeleteSenderDomain before destroy! wipes mailer_config ->
  destroy!); it does NOT call org.remove_domain because CustomDomain#destroy!
  already removes org participation (custom_domain.rb:457-460).
- display_domain_index re-assertion (the crux): CustomDomain#destroy! ends in a
  bare Familia super that UNCONDITIONALLY HDELs display_domain_index[fqdn] keyed
  on the destroyed record's own display_domain. Two live records can't share an
  FQDN (create! HSETNX gate), but a drift-produced shadow can. The op snapshots
  index_owner_id + victim_objid BEFORE destroy!, then re-asserts the survivor's
  pointer ONLY when the index pointed at a DIFFERENT record (reload + confirm
  fqdn match first). Re-assertion is best-effort so it never blocks the audit of
  a destroy that already committed.
- dry_run:true default (safe preview); exactly-one AdminAuditEvent ('domain.remove')
  emitted from the op only (adapters never audit); Result carries reasserts_survivor
  so the preview shows whether removal is a clean clear or a shadow re-assertion.
- Colonel route: DELETE /organizations... -> DELETE /domains/:extid; CLI command
  auto-discovered (apps/*/cli/**/*_command.rb).

Brand packs v2: manifest + etc/branding root + tracked default pack (#3774)

Consolidate branding into a single unit — a "pack" carrying both static
assets and their identity scalars — replacing the two disjoint mechanisms
(BRAND_* identity vars + a separate #3739 asset-overlay dir that nothing
kept in agreement).

Core (lib/onetime.rb):
- brand_pack_roots: two search roots, first existing wins — etc/branding
  (operator space, arrives via mounts/confext) then public/branding
  (vendor space). brand_pack_dir(name) resolves a NAME across them with
  the existing traversal guard.
- resolve_brand_pack_dir: resolution ALWAYS lands on a pack — an unset
  BRAND_PACK, a missing BRAND_ASSETS_DIR, or an unknown name all fall back
  to the tracked `default` pack (and warn). brand_overlay_dir reads OT.conf;
  the resolver itself is pure so it also runs at boot before OT.conf exists.
- brand_asset_path collapses onto the pack path (selected -> default ->
  legacy public/web safety net).

Manifest (lib/onetime/config.rb):
- apply_brand_manifest (run in after_load before normalize_brand)
  safe_load_file's the resolved pack's brand.yaml and fills only the keys
  the operator brand: config left nil. Precedence: built-in < pack
  brand.yaml < operator brand: < BRAND_* env. Keys whitelisted to
  BRAND_MANIFEST_KEYS (== BRAND_ENV) — a pack can never reach site.host/SMTP.

Middleware (static_files.rb):
- Base brand layer serves BRAND_PACK_URLS from the resolved default pack
  (was loose public/web); a selected non-default pack overlays ahead of it
  and partial packs fall through. App assets (/dist,/img,/v3) stay on
  public/web and are never overlaid.

Default pack:
- Move the 8 neutral assets public/web -> public/branding/default (byte
  identical) + a value-free, all-commented brand.yaml. gitignore carve-out
  tracks default/ while other packs stay generator-output-only.
- The default manifest ships NO values, so an unconfigured install keeps
  brand.* nil and the frontend neutral defaults stay the single authority
  for neutral rendering (#3049) — MFA issuer stays "OTS", head tags
  unchanged (verified via full boot).

Generator/build:
- gen:favicons writes the neutral pack to public/branding/default; presets
  emit an active brand.yaml alongside assets. check.mjs reads the default
  pack. Dockerfile bake overlays a selected pack onto default/ so the
  runtime serves it with no env var set.

Doctor (bin/setup):
- doctor_brand_pack: outcome probe reporting which root won, the canonical
  file set present, and loaded brand.yaml keys; pack-not-found lists roots.

Tests:

(fail-fast if unset), the app URL carries the password, the healthcheck
authenticates via REDISCLI_AUTH, and port 6379 is no longer published to
the host (expose only).

[#AUDIT-2026] Default security middleware protections on (M-1)

frame_options, path_traversal, and strict_transport now default to true
(env vars flip to opt-out: set MIDDLEWARE_*=false to disable). Frontend
config schema defaults match. The Security middleware builder logs a
warn-level line when a security-critical protection is switched off, so
an accidental disable is visible; deliberately-off toggles stay quiet.

[#AUDIT-2026] Let session cookie 'secure' default via ssl_enabled? fallback (M-7-A)

Emitting a hard false when the SSL env var is unset pinned the cookie
insecure. Emit nil instead so boot.rb's ssl_enabled? fallback can default
secure=true in production / when site.ssl is on.

[#AUDIT-2026] Require CSRF tokens on session-authenticated API requests (H-1)

The blanket /api/ CSRF bypass let a forged cross-site request ride a
logged-in SPA user's session cookie. The AuthenticityToken allow_if now
discriminates on the actual attack vector: Basic-Auth and cookieless
requests still bypass (no ambient credential to forge), but a
session-cookie-authenticated API request must present X-CSRF-Token. The
SPA already sends it on every request via the axios interceptor.

[#AUDIT-2026] Revoke sessions on password change/reset; consolidate password hooks (M-2)

Rodauth's clear_tokens only gates /auth/* SQL session keys; the app's real
auth gate is the encrypted Redis session blob. Add
Operations::Sessions::RevokeAllForCustomerExceptCurrent (tracked-sidecar
kill plus optional bounded keyspace scan) and invoke it from the password
hooks: reset revokes ALL sessions (user is unauthenticated), change keeps
the current sid and revokes the rest, failing secure (revoke-all) when the
sid can't be resolved. Falls back to the account email when external_id is
absent rather than silently skipping.

Hooks::Password is now intentionally empty: Rodauth hooks don't chain, and
its copies of after_reset_password/after_change_password silently
overwrote Account's richer versions (the #3275 collision pattern). All
password-lifecycle logic lives in Hooks::Account.

[#AUDIT-2026] Refuse OmniAuth email auto-link to existing accounts (H-3)

account_from_omniauth matching an existing account by email let an
attacker who controls an IdP identity emitting the victim's email sign in
as the victim (account takeover). When no (provider, uid) identity row
exists for the matched account, redirect to /signin with an explanatory
error instead of linking; genuinely new emails still JIT-create subject to
the domain checks.

FOLLOW-UP: an authenticated link-SSO-from-settings flow does not exist
yet, so password-first users must keep using their password until it
ships.

[#AUDIT-2026] Add two-tier login rate limiter for simple-mode auth (M-4)

Simple mode has no Rodauth lockout, so credential guessing was unbounded.
New Security::LoginRateLimiter mirrors the passphrase limiter's two-tier
design: a tight per-email+IP gate plus a higher per-email global backstop
that catches IP rotation and nil-IP callers. AuthenticateSession checks
the limit in raise_concerns, counts failures in the single nil-cust
funnel, and clears state once credentials verify.

[#AUDIT-2026] Two-tier passphrase rate limiting keyed on secret+IP (M-8)

Keying the lockout solely on the secret identifier let any link holder
burn a few wrong guesses and DoS the legitimate recipient. The limiter
now gates on a tight per-secret+IP tier (MAX_ATTEMPTS=5) plus a
per-secret global backstop (GLOBAL_MAX_ATTEMPTS=20) that catches
IP-rotating attackers and nil-IP callers without collapsing them into
one shared bucket.

v1/v2 show/reveal/burn logic threads the client IP from strategy_result
metadata (nil in v1, which has no per-request IP plumbing and falls back
to the global tier).

[#AUDIT-2026] Surface per-IP limiter keys in ratelimit inspect/reset ops (RL-1)

The two-tier limiters write keys with a variable {ip} suffix that the
registry's exact key templates cannot name, so a /24-collision-locked
recipient had no operator remedy. The registry now carries glob-escaped
scan_keys patterns (passphrase, and the new login kind), and the
Inspect/Reset operations fold in a subject-scoped cursor SCAN so per-IP
lockouts are visible and resettable. The static-key CLI is unchanged.

[#AUDIT-2026] Block awaiting-MFA sessions from authenticating (M-11)

Defense-in-depth: BaseSessionAuthStrategy now fails any session with
awaiting_mfa=true before the authenticated check, so a session mid-MFA
can never authenticate a request even if a future code path sets
authenticated=true without clearing the flag.

[#AUDIT-2026] Host-allowlist Stripe checkout URLs before navigation (M-9)

checkout_url is API-derived and assigned to window.location, so a
tampered value could drive an open redirect. New isAllowedCheckoutUrl
permits only https://checkout.stripe.com (exact, not *.stripe.com) or
the app's own origin. Enforced at every assignment site in PlanSelector,
in the checkout-session Zod contract, and at the service boundary.
Currency-migration boundary parsing is deferred until its stale spec

[#AUDIT-2026] Gate admin routes on colonel role; harden redirect param check (M-10)

New meta.requiresColonel on every admin-console route, enforced by
handleColonelRequirement as client-side defence-in-depth (backend
role=colonel gate and API 403s remain the authority). Non-colonels are

no /dashboard or /signin route to SPA-redirect to.

The signin ?redirect= param now goes through isValidInternalPath, which
adds a length cap and rejects embedded '://' the ad-hoc slash check
missed.
