[#4063] feat(domains): derive anchor set and link pool from CanonicalHosts

Adds a link_hosts: input to CanonicalHosts.hosts so operator link domains
join the canonical set, and splits out two new readers:

  anchor_hosts / normalized_anchor_hosts - the pre-4063 two-element set
  (default + site.host), which is what anchors generated links and never
  contains a pool member.

  link_pool - nil (unset) resolves to [primary], [] stays [], otherwise the
  operator list stripped and uniq'd. The nil-vs-[] distinction is the whole
  unset/set-but-empty axis and must not be collapsed.

The ordering contract is preserved: primary (default || site.host) stays
element 0. anchor_hosts delegates to hosts(link_hosts: nil) so there is one
normalization implementation and the two sets cannot drift.

Refs #4063

[#4063] feat(config): add LINK_DOMAINS with a set-but-empty boot guard

Renders as an array through ERB so the three states stay distinguishable:

  link_domains: <%= ENV['LINK_DOMAINS']&.split(',')&.map(&:strip) %>

unset yields nil, LINK_DOMAINS="" yields [], and a list yields the parsed
array. The &. is load-bearing; the '|| nil' idiom used by the neighbouring
default: key collapses unset and empty into one value.

link_domains is deliberately absent from Config::DEFAULTS. deep_merge has an
'elsif v2.nil? then v1' arm, so a DEFAULTS entry would restore the default for
unset and make the set-but-empty case undetectable.

validate_link_domains! raises ConfigError naming both the env var and the
config path. It fires from raise_concerns regardless of features.domains.enabled,
since the operator explicitly wrote the setting. This is the opposite polarity
from #4062's allowed_hosts, where empty means canonical-only; the asymmetry is
documented at both definitions.

LINK_DOMAINS is added to the lane scrub explicitly - it has no DOMAINS_ prefix,
so the ${!DOMAINS_@} glob does not catch it and a dev shell would leak it into
every suite.

[#4063] feat(domains): classify link-pool hosts as canonical by exact match

Threads link_hosts through initialize_from_config, gated on domains_enabled.
That gate is a fix, not just plumbing: CanonicalHosts.hosts now defaults
link_hosts: to a config read, so the previous argument-less call site picked up
features.domains.link_domains even when the domains feature was disabled.

Peer/parent and subdomain sweeps now run over anchor hosts only, via a new
@anchor_domains_parsed selected out of the already-parsed canonical set (so no
host can emit a second unparseable-skip line). Pool members participate by exact
match, which already outranks known_custom_domain? - a tenant cannot register an
operator-blessed domain and attach their own brand or signin config to it.

Without that split, blessing go.acme.com would also serve every unregistered
sibling under acme.com, which is the host-passthrough behavior the issue's prior
art explicitly rejects. CustomDomain.overlaps_canonical_domain? makes the same
exact-vs-sweep distinction, so the two now agree.

Also resolves a pre-existing drift that LINK_DOMAINS makes reachable:
canonical_host? compared against raw @canonical_domains strings while
classification compared against the parsed set, so a typo'd entry passed
admission and then classified :invalid. It now reads the parsed set whenever
populated. Unparseable pool entries are skipped and logged via OT.le (promoted
from http_logger.debug, which was invisible in production); domains stay enabled.

[#4063] fix(domains): anchor generated links on the anchor set, not the link pool

default_domain? now reads normalized_anchor_hosts. Without this split the whole
feature is silently inert: process_share_domain returns early when
default_domain? is true, so every pool selection would be discarded and the link
re-anchored on the canonical host - which on a single-tenant install is the
internal platform address LINK_DOMAINS exists to hide. No exception, no log; the
picker looks right and every link is wrong.

overlaps_canonical_domain? splits the same way: the exact arm runs over the full
canonical set (so an operator link domain cannot be registered as a tenant
CustomDomain), while the base-domain sweep runs over anchors only. Sweeping pool
members would forbid customers from registering any sibling under that base
domain - with LINK_DOMAINS=short.example.com, no *.example.com registration at
all. The accepted cost is that a customer may register a sibling of an operator
link domain.

Both predicates carry comments naming the failure a consistency sweep would
reintroduce.

[#4063] feat(secrets): accept link-pool domains at creation, including for guests

An operator link domain has no CustomDomain row by design, so both domain gates
rejected it. Two guards, both required:

validate_domain_access admits pool members before the CustomDomain lookup.
Without it every pool entry 422s with 'Unknown domain' - the picker would offer
a domain that cannot be used.

validate_anonymous_share_domain admits them too. It runs before
validate_domain_access, so the first guard is unreachable for guests. This is
latent rather than visible today: the anonymous form posts canonical_domain,
which default_domain? nils out. But SecretForm.vue watches currentContext and
posts share_domain on every creation including the anonymous homepage - only the
picker UI is hidden, not the watch - so once the frontend falls back to the pool,
every anonymous creation on a LINK_DOMAINS install would 403.

This does not reopen #3311. That rule protects tenant-branded CustomDomains,
which are a phishing surface; pool members have no such record and cannot carry
brand or signin config. The exemption is inert on branded hosts because
determine_share_domain still pins guests to the Host header. Any pool member is
selectable, not just the first - all entries are operator-blessed and equivalent.

Normalization mirrors default_domain? on both sides (display_domain on the input,
extract_hostname on configured hosts), so a mixed-case LINK_DOMAINS entry is not
a dead entry. Unparseable input fails closed to the existing rejection.

Also picks up an unrelated pre-existing Layout/ExtraSpacing correction at :135,
applied automatically by the rubocop pre-commit hook.

[#4063] feat(domains): warn when a link-pool host shadows a registered custom domain

The existing guard covered only features.domains.default. Every pool member
shadows a tenant CustomDomain the same way - the operator's host wins
classification, so the tenant's per-domain brand and signin config silently
stop taking effect - so the warning now runs over the whole pool, one line per
shadowed host.

Reads CanonicalHosts.link_pool rather than DomainStrategy.link_domains:
initialize_from_config runs when the Rack app is built, after every boot
initializer, so the DomainStrategy reader is nil here or stale from a previous
in-process boot. link_pool reads config directly, the same derivation
DomainStrategy feeds from, so the two cannot disagree.

Hosts are normalized before the lookup - the display_domain index is keyed on
the normalized form, so a mixed-case or ported entry would miss its own
registration. Fail-open as before; the set-but-empty boot error stays in
Config.raise_concerns because anything raised here is swallowed.

[#4063] feat(domains): emit the resolved link pool in the bootstrap payload

Adds link_domains beside canonical_domain, unconditionally - the picker still
needs a pool when features.domains.enabled is false, and an absent key would
leave the TS schema's optionality deciding behavior.

The output_template entry is load-bearing, not decoration: SerializerRegistry.run
partitions serializer output against the template and strips undeclared keys, so
an emit without it would silently never reach the payload.

Template default is [] rather than nil because the consuming Zod schema uses
.default([]), which fires only for undefined - a nil-valued key would be a parse
error rather than a default. [] therefore means exactly one thing to the client:
a stale pre-4063 server.

config_serializer's transform_domains deliberately does not carry the field. Its
whole domains subtree is absent when the feature is disabled, which is precisely
when the pool is still needed, and the pool is resolved runtime state rather than
static config.

[#4063] feat(bootstrap): type link_domains and guard the Ruby/TS seam

  link_domains: z.array(z.string()).default([])

Not .nullable(): an explicit null must be a parse error so a serializer
regression is loud rather than silently defaulted. Not .optional(): store state
comes from bootstrapSchema.parse({}), and an optional key would be omitted and
untracked by Pinia.

Declaring it is also the fix for resetForLogout. The prior failure mode was not
a $reset drop - an undeclared field is stripped by Zod at getBootstrapSnapshot()
and never reaches store state at all. Once declared it flows through
SCHEMA_DEFAULTS to state() and resets deterministically.

Deliberately not added to preservedConfig: canonical_domain, site_host,
custom_domains and display_domain are all cleared on logout, so preserving the
pool would leave the picker offering operator domains with no canonical fallback
behind them.

features.ts needs nothing - it mirrors transform_domains, which does not carry
the field.

The serializer-field list is a hand transcription and the Ruby-side specs are
non-exhaustive have_key loops, so this is what actually guards the seam.

[#4063] fix(domains): stop assuming the canonical domain is selectable

With an explicit link pool the canonical host may be excluded from the picker
while still serving the app, so every 'fall back to canonicalDomain' path could
yield a domain setContext silently rejects - dropdown looks right, selection
no-ops, nothing throws.

Seven sites now resolve through one helper, getPoolFallbackDomain (canonical if
it is a pool member, else the pool head, else ''): the currentContext fallback,
resetContext, the domains-disabled branch, and getDomainDisplayName - which was
not an invariant violation but rendered the internal host as the picker label,
the exact string the feature hides.

buildAvailableDomains reads the pool; dedup keeps the custom position so a pool
entry that is also a registered custom domain stays in its slot and retains its
extid. getPreferredDomain discriminates on pool membership rather than equality
with canonical, and every return value is drawn from availableDomains.
resetContext deliberately uses the fallback rather than getPreferredDomain,
which would return the first custom and change long-standing behavior.

persistDomainContext widens to custom_domains union link_domains, so an operator
selection survives reload instead of being dropped. UpdateDomainContext already
admits canonical-set members, and canonical_host? is an exact match, so a
sibling of a pool member is correctly not persisted. Canonical is carved back
out: absent sessionStorage is the canonical/default state, a convention that
predates this change.

setContext is untouched - it remains the invariant.

[#4063] fix(domains): give every link-pool row its own id in the context switcher

The '?? canonical' sentinel collapsed every extid-less row onto one id. That was
safe when the canonical domain was the only extid-less entry; with a multi-entry
pool, selecting the second operator domain silently selected the first and
isCurrent keyed the wrong row.

Row id is now getExtidByDomain(domain) ?? 'link:<hostname>' - two disjoint id
spaces, stable because the hostname is the row's own identity and
availableDomains is deduped. domainForId still inverts by searching idForDomain
rather than stripping the prefix, so the two directions cannot drift and both
stay correct through the window where a custom domain has not yet been assigned
its extid.

disabledReason was unconditionally 'Default domain has no settings page', which
is false for an operator entry; the canonical row keeps that string and other
extid-less rows get their own. Canonical is read for copy only, never for
identity - with the canonical host excluded, every selectable domain reports
isCanonical false, so 'no extid' and 'is canonical' are no longer the same test.

A pool entry that is also a registered custom domain keeps its extid id, its
gear, and its place in customDomainCount.

[#4063] test(domains): cover link-pool classification in the middleware tryouts

24 cases across the two files. The security-relevant ones:

A CustomDomain registration matching a pool entry must not flip it to :custom.
The stub is proven live rather than vacuous - a control case calls the same
registered host against a canonical set that excludes it and gets :custom
(reachable only through known_custom_domain?), then a third case restores the
real lookup and re-runs to prove the restore took.

An unregistered peer of a pool member classifies :invalid while an unregistered
subdomain of an anchor host still classifies :canonical. That asymmetry is the
point of the anchor/pool split.

A middleware.call wiring case guards the call site itself: dropping the
anchor_domains kwarg there would re-widen every real request while every
direct-Chooserator case stayed green.

Also covers unparseable entries (skipped, logged, feature stays enabled), the
serving half of the canonical-excluded case, and the implicit domain-context
override branch, which keys on !canonical_host? and would otherwise read a
blessed host as a dev override.

Every case resets class state explicitly and none mutates OT.conf's domains
config; verified order-independent by running the directory in reverse.

[#4063] test(domains): unit coverage for the link pool, boot guard and guest path

Two new files (CanonicalHosts derivation and ordering; validate_link_domains!
driven directly, since spec/config.test.yaml cannot express set-but-empty) and
five extended in place.

Config is mutated through an around hook that restores key absence rather than
stubbing CanonicalHosts.link_pool - stubbing would skip the config path that
actually broke. The admission examples drive the real
DomainStrategy.initialize_from_config for the same reason.

Non-vacuity was checked by mutation rather than assertion. Dropping link_hosts
from hosts killed 20 examples; removing the guest guard killed 14; removing the
creation-time admission killed 7; putting the pool back into anchor_hosts killed
8. Two results shaped the suite: deleting the validate_link_domains! call from
raise_concerns killed only the wiring block while the direct-call examples
stayed green, which is why both exist; and removing the serializer's
output_template entry was caught only by the registry round-trip, not by the
serialize examples. There is also a mutant for collapsing link_pool's [] into
[primary] - the 'make it match #4062' change this design explicitly rejects.

[#4063] test(domains): vitest suites for the link pool and switcher rows

17 new cases: 12 on the composable, 5 on the switcher. setupBootstrapStore gains
an optional link_domains knob defaulting to [] - the stale-pre-4063 wire shape,
which the composable maps back to [canonicalDomain] - so every pre-existing case
keeps exact prior behavior and needed no edits.

Each new case was proven able to fail by temporarily reverting the production
behavior it covers, then restoring. Ten reverts in total; two were informative.
Reverting resetContext to getPreferredDomain - the naive substitution someone
would reach for - reddens the new pool cases and the pre-existing 'resets to
canonical domain' case together. Reverting the switcher's idForDomain to always
prefix reddens the new shadowed-entry case plus a pre-existing dropdown-close
case, confirming both id spaces are load-bearing.

Order-independence was measured, not assumed: full test- and file-level shuffle
under several seeds after verifying the emitted order actually differed, plus
each suite run alone in both directions.

One behavior change is deliberately left unpinned: getPreferredDomain
discriminates on pool membership, so a custom domain that is also a pool member
is treated as an operator entry and skipped for initial selection. It is only
reachable in the shadowed configuration that ConfigureDomains already warns
about, and pinning it would cement it.

Remove target-blind translation mode

Remove `--all` from the `tasks create` command as catch-up is now the
exclusive mode for generating translation tasks. Argparse will now
reject the deprecated flag.

Protect unexported translations in tasks create

Add an `exported_at` column to the `translation_tasks` table to track
when a level's translations are saved to disk. `tasks create --apply` now
refuses to reopen completed levels with unexported work, exiting with

bin/install shadowed coreutils install(1) inside the image build: the
Dockerfile prepends ${APP_DIR}/bin to PATH, so `install -d -o appuser`
resolved to the wrapper, hit its catch-all arm and failed both source
builds at "Unknown option: -d". Call /usr/bin/install by absolute path in
both stages and say why, in the Dockerfile and in bin/install itself.

bin/install also dispatched on $1 alone and dropped the rest, so
`bin/install --reconcile --help` performed a live reconcile. Reject
trailing arguments (exit 64) rather than silently discarding them.

with a different line range in each and nothing testing either. Replaced
with a usage() heredoc.

tests/lanes/run — four hermeticity gaps, each now covered by
spec/unit/lanes/hermetic_boundary_spec.rb:

  - An imported BASHOPTS=nocasematch made the keep-list `case`
    case-insensitive, so `ci`/`Path`/`Home` (distinct variables as far as
    bash is concerned) were treated as keep-listed and delivered to the
    task process. Added nocasematch and extdebug to the shopt reset.
  - The exported-function scrub piped `declare -F` through awk, so an
    exported function named `awk` WAS the filter: its empty output read
    as "no exported functions" and nothing was scrubbed — including the
    git/bundle/docker shadowing the block exists to stop. Parse with
    builtins instead, and invoke every builtin the scrub runs as
    `builtin <name>` so a shadowing function cannot become the scrub.
  - Environment entries whose names are not valid identifiers
    (`FOO-BAR=x`) are invisible to compgen -e and cannot be unset, yet
    bash forwards them across both execs. Enumerate the real environment
    with `env -0` and add them to the exec-boundary strip.
  - The daemon-addressing snapshot kept DOCKER_CONTEXT but not
    DOCKER_CONFIG (and no podman connection vars), so compose autostart
    looked the context up in the default ~/.docker and failed — a
    regression against main's denylist. Snapshot the full set.

.node-version: the runner, bin/setup --doctor and the boundary spec all
read it there instead of each carrying its own literal, which is how

[#4018] Harden the exec-boundary env(1) call against a shadowing function

The non-identifier-name enumeration added in the previous commit called
`env -0` as an ordinary command word inside a process substitution, so a
function named `env` resolves ahead of coreutils — and the function scrub
cannot clear a readonly one (`unset -f` fails on it; the attribute is
reachable through the caller's BASH_ENV, which is how the boundary spec
already builds its readonly fixture). The function returns nothing, the
loop strips nothing, and the result is indistinguishable from a clean
environment: the same failure shape as the `awk` filter this branch just
fixed one stage earlier. Verified — with a readonly `env() {...}` in
BASH_ENV, `FOO-BAR` and `ORGS.SSO` both reach the task process.

Route both `env -0` calls through `builtin command`. The `exec env` on the
last line needs no such guard: exec's operand is not subject to function
lookup (verified with `env() { :; }; exec env echo x`).

Also probe for `-0` rather than assuming it: busybox env has no such flag,
and an unsupported flag turns the loop into the same silent no-op. On a
shell without it the runner now says so on stderr.

The probe's subshell is load-bearing. `builtin command <external>` loses
errexit's condition-context suppression in bash 5.2, so a bare
`if builtin command env -0 ...` exits the whole runner with status 125 in
exactly the case being probed for, and `|| true` does not rescue it.

spec/unit/lanes/hermetic_boundary_spec.rb grows a readonly `env` function
in its poisoned BASH_ENV and an example asserting the enumeration is
shadow-proof. Against the previous commit it fails with two leaked
non-identifier entries.

[#4063] Address code review of the link-domains pool branch

Seven findings from review, plus seven tests the branch had broken.

Classification
--------------
The exact-match arm ran `equal_to?` over the FULL canonical set, and that
predicate also accepts `www.<registrable-domain>`. With
LINK_DOMAINS=go.acme.com an unrelated `www.acme.com` therefore classified
:canonical ahead of the known_custom_domain? lookup, silently dropping
that tenant's brand/signin config -- the same widening the anchor-only
sweeps exist to prevent, arriving through a different arm. Split it:
`exact_host?` over the full set, `equal_to?` over the anchors only. The
two sets are equal for any caller with no pool, so pre-#4063 behavior is
unchanged.

Admission
---------
`link_pool_host?` in both API versions read features.domains.link_domains
straight out of config, skipping the features.domains.enabled gate and
the parsed-host filter the middleware applies. A pool configured with
domains off -- or holding an unparseable entry -- let guests anchor
secrets on hosts the middleware classifies :invalid and the picker never
offers. Both now delegate to a new
`Middleware::DomainStrategy.link_pool_host?`, so admission and
classification answer from one set.

Boot
----
`resolve_link_domains` fell back to [canonical_domain] when no configured
entry resolved, re-exposing the internal platform host in the picker.
There is no safe fallback for that state, so `validate_link_domains!`
now fails boot when a set pool names no parseable host, echoing the
entries. A mixed list still boots; the bad entry is dropped and logged.

Picker
------
- The canonical domain is no longer offered while browsing a branded
  host, where selecting it was ignored end-to-end and the link anchored
  on the branded host anyway. Pool members stay -- v2 honors those.
- Selecting the canonical domain now writes through to the server.
  Clearing only sessionStorage left sess['domain_context'] naming the
  previous selection, and that value is read first, so the next reload
  reverted the switch. resetContext goes through the same path.
- Host comparisons are normalized on both sides (new
  shared/utils/domain-host.ts). link_domains arrives normalized from the
  server while canonical_domain/site_host do not, so a canonical host
  configured with a port was never recognized as a member of its own pool.

Tests fixed along the way
-------------------------
A formatting pass on this branch split `a == b` across two lines in two
response-header cases, dropped the `status` binding in a third, and
deleted the `result =` capture in three domain-context-override cases so
ENV.delete's return value became the assertion subject. None could pass.
Also one pre-existing case ending on `remove_method`.

Note: the review's fifth finding (UpdateDomainContext persisting
'EXAMPLE.COM:443' verbatim) does not reproduce -- normalize_domain
downcases and DOMAIN_CHAR_PATTERN rejects any port. The real port defect
was its mirror image on the frontend, covered above.

[#4063] Reset the picker to the served host on a branded domain

resetContext landed on '' whenever the offerable pool was empty, which
is the DEFAULT configuration on a tenant-branded host: with LINK_DOMAINS
unset the pool is canonical-only, and getOfferableLinkDomains drops the
canonical entry there. persistDomainContext then took its clearing tail,
dropping sessionStorage while sess['domain_context'] kept naming the
previous selection -- and selectBestDomain reads the server half first,
so the next load silently restored what the user had just reset.

Syncing '' would not have helped: UpdateDomainContext#normalize_domain
maps a blank domain to nil and field_specific_concerns raises before
perform_update, and syncDomainContextToServer swallows the rejection in
its own catch. There is no clear path on that endpoint.

Fall back to the served host instead. It is a value both halves accept
-- it is one of the customer's own custom domains, so valid_domain?
admits it and it is already in availableDomains -- and it is where
determine_share_domain anchors links from that host regardless of what
share_domain asks for. "Reset to canonical" was always fiction on a
branded host.

This restores display_domain to getConfig(), which the previous commit
had dropped as dead; it is live again for exactly this path.

[#4062] Mount AdminNetworkIsolation after Rack::DetectHost

The admin gate mounted six lines above Rack::DetectHost, so
env['rack.detected_host'] was unset when it ran. Harmless while the
gate only consulted the client IP; a prerequisite for consulting the
host.

Moves it below DetectHost while keeping it below IPPrivacyMiddleware
(which supplies otto.client_ip) and above Onetime::Session, so a denied
request still costs no session write.

One consequence: StartupReadiness now precedes the gate, so a request
to /colonel during boot returns 503 rather than 404.

[#4062] Add AdminHostAllowlist, the shared admin-host classifier

Decides which site.admin.allowed_hosts entries can ever match a
request's detected host, and why the others cannot. Side-effect free:
no logging, no raising. Callers decide what their posture does with a
Classification.

Two call sites have to agree exactly — the boot validator that refuses
an unenforceable allowlist, and the middleware that enforces the
surviving hosts — so the judgment lives in neither. If they disagreed,
the app would either boot into a config the middleware then refuses to
serve, or refuse to boot on one it would have served.

Routability is judged with Rack::DetectHost's own predicate rather than
a local copy, so the two cannot drift.

No consumers yet.

[#4062] Add site.admin.allowed_hosts and refuse an unenforceable one

Adds the config key alongside site.admin.allowed_cidrs, and a boot
validator that raises ConfigError when an explicitly set allowlist
names nothing the host gate could ever match — an IP literal, a
`*.example.com` pattern, a non-ASCII entry, or any mix.

Every one of those cases is an operator writing an allowlist in order
to RESTRICT the admin surfaces. Treating them as 'ignore the bad
entries' would leave the gate disabled and serve /colonel on every
hostname, so the config that reads most restrictive would be the one
that exposes most. `*` is how you ask for that deliberately.

Note the polarity is the opposite of #4063's LINK_DOMAINS, where an
empty list is the error. Here empty is the safe default (canonical
only) and non-empty-but-unenforceable is the error. Both land on the
same rule — an operator who typed something gets what they meant or
gets told — through opposite-looking checks. Documented at both sites
so neither gets 'harmonized' into the other.

[#4062] Gate the admin surfaces on the detected host

/colonel and /api/colonel answered on every hostname the app serves,
including tenant custom domains. The only thing keeping the admin
console off a tenant host was incidental: session cookies are mounted
without a domain attribute, and custom-domain signin defaults off. On a
custom domain with signin enabled, a colonel who authenticates there
passes every existing gate.

Adds a host allowlist in front of the CIDR allowlist. Either failure
returns the existing 404, unchanged in shape, so a denial stays
indistinguishable from an absent route.

The host comes from env[Rack::DetectHost.result_field_name] — the host
DetectHost validated, read through the accessor because DETECTED_HOST
can rename the key. Deliberately NOT onetime.domain_strategy, which
honors an O-Domain-Context request header: a header-settable input must
never decide admin reachability.

An unset allowlist falls back to the canonical ANCHOR hosts plus their
www. variants — not CanonicalHosts.hosts, which includes the #4063
link_domains pool. Falling back to that would serve the admin console
on every operator short-link domain, inverting what the pool exists
for.

The gate goes inert when the anchors yield nothing DetectHost could
emit. DetectHost rejects localhost forms and every IP literal, and
site.host defaults to localhost:3000, so enforcing there would 404
/colonel on stock local-dev and bare-IP self-hosted installs that
nobody misconfigured. That inert rule covers the fallback ONLY; an
allowlist the operator wrote is never silently disabled.

Boot logs the effective posture once, including trusted_proxy state:
host_gate 'active' says nothing about whether the host it judges is
trustworthy, and with trusted_proxy off DetectHost will believe any
peer on a private address.

[#4062] Document both admin isolation factors

Retitles the operations doc to cover the host allowlist alongside the
CIDR one, and drops the 'default: no-op' framing that was true of the
middleware before this change and false after it.

Adds the boot-error case, the real boot log payload and WARN strings,
the ops guidance the app cannot enforce itself (serve admin on its own
hostname and 404 the admin paths at the edge on every other vhost),
and the punycode limitation.

Also corrects two claims that were already wrong: the fallback is the
canonical ANCHOR set rather than the canonical set, and the stale
ordering note in the domain-ip-allowlist spec.

[#4062] Cover the admin host gate

Unit tryout for the middleware, config spec for the boot validator, and
full-stack request specs across canonical / www / subdomain / custom /
unknown hosts on both surfaces, authenticated and anonymous.

Includes the spoofing negatives that are the point of the feature: an
O-Domain-Context header cannot make a non-allowlisted host pass, and
neither can X-Forwarded-Host or Apx-Incoming-Host from an untrusted
peer. Enabling domains for those tests goes through
Onetime::Runtime.update_features, not the config hash — DomainStrategy
reads the runtime feature set, so flipping config alone left the whole
override branch dead and the spoofing tests vacuous.

Pins the regression that a link_domains pool member is never admitted
by the anchor fallback, and the four-shape case that caught a
NoMethodError in detected_host: the gate is inert under the default
test config, so nothing else exercises an active gate with a real
detected host.

Every integration example sends a real Host header and sets a routable
anchor, so none of this coverage depends on the inert posture; inertness
is asserted deliberately where it is the subject.

[#4062] Let `*` disable the host gate and stop aborting boot

Two fixes to the allowlist classifier and its boot check.

`Classification#unenforceable?` ignored the wildcard flag, so
ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS="*,10.0.0.5" classified as "nothing enforceable":
boot-fatal at Config and total-deny in the middleware, despite the
operator using the documented escape hatch the error message itself
recommends. An explicit `*` anywhere now disables the gate;
`wildcard_only?` survives only to decide whether to name the ignored
siblings in the WARN.

The boot check no longer raises. It was added when the alternative was
believed to be fail-open, but `configured_host_gate` already returns
[[], true] and denies both admin surfaces for this config, so the raise
was redundant and took the public site down to protect a console that
was already dark. It now warns with the same diagnostic text and the
consequence corrected. The comment records why this is deliberately not
symmetric with validate_link_domains!, which has no runtime backstop.

[#4062] Close two gate bypasses and stop failing open

Both admin gates were defeatable and both could vanish silently.

The surface match compared the raw SCRIPT_NAME+PATH_INFO while the Otto
router dispatches on Otto::Utils.normalize_path, so `/%63olonel` failed
colonel_shell?, skipped both gates, and was then routed to /colonel.
request_path now normalizes first, matching HealthAccessControl and
SessionSkip; an unnormalizable path is judged an admin surface, so the
failure mode is deny rather than bypass.

The host gate trusted whatever Rack::DetectHost produced, and with
site.network.trusted_proxy unset -- the shipped default -- DetectHost
honours a client-supplied forwarded host from any private-IP peer. The
gate now checks provenance BEFORE membership: a forwarded-derived host
is accepted only via a configured trusted proxy, or when the header did
not change the answer. Being on the allowlist is exactly what an
attacker who can set the header would arrange, so membership cannot
rescue an unattributable host. DetectHost itself is left alone (#4024).

Falling back to HTTP_HOST was considered and rejected: under Approximated
ingress, Host is the origin's canonical name and the tenant domain
arrives in Apx-Incoming-Host, so the fallback would admit every tenant
request -- the inverse of the feature.

A config read error returned nil, indistinguishable from "unset", which
degraded a configured gate to the anchor fallback and then to INACTIVE
while the log blamed site.host. It now returns a sentinel and denies.
The CIDR gate had the same shape from main: a list where every entry is
malformed left no ranges, so the gate deactivated and served admin to
every IP. It now stays active and denies, matching the host gate.

Also: the boot posture logged once per mounted app (13 copies of the
lines that say your admin surfaces are unprotected), the path String
was built before the gate-activity check, and the with_www_variants
comment claimed a Chooserator.equal_to? equivalence that does not hold.

[#4062] Document the provenance rule and the fail-closed CIDR change

The boot-error section described an error that no longer aborts the
boot; it is now "When the allowlist cannot be enforced". A new
"Forwarded hosts and the admin gate" section covers the provenance rule
and the recipe for recovering from a 404 caused by it, and the WARN/ERROR
table is corrected with a note that the posture logs once per process,
not once per mounted app.

The changelog fragment gains the three operator-visible contract
changes: forwarded-host provenance, the CIDR gate now denying instead of
deactivating when nothing parses (a change from main's behaviour, which
silently served admin to every IP), and percent-encoded admin paths
being gated.

[#4080] Declare the content entry model once in io.py

Two readers with two different answers to "what is a key" is what
produced #4080: a field-blind flattener compared `<key>.context` as if it
were translatable, and the text-only view collapses `skip: true`, empty
text, and absent-key into one indistinguishable "not there".

Adds the single declaration — TEXT_FIELD, METADATA_FIELDS, a frozen
Entry, read_entries, classify_entry — and rewrites walk_keys as the
derived translatable-text view over it. No behaviour change for existing
callers; the point is that a field added to METADATA_FIELDS can no longer
become translatable in whichever reader happens to be field-blind.

[#4080] Read task entries through the shared entry model

get_source_hashes_from_file and get_target_entries each re-implemented
their own field filtering; get_target_entries handed callers raw dicts
that every consumer had to re-check. Both now go through read_entries,
and get_target_entries returns Entry objects with no policy applied.

classify_key keeps its historical name (it is imported by name elsewhere)
but is now an alias of io.classify_entry, so the classifier lives next to
the entry model it reads instead of drifting from it.

[#4080] Read entries in `validate pr`, and delete flatten_json

flatten_json was field-blind: it flattened `<key>.text`, `<key>.context`
and `<key>.source_hash` into peer keys, so every translated file tripped
the "Extra keys not in English" structure check on metadata the locale
never invented. It is warning-severity, so `passed` stayed true and the
noise went unnoticed — the worst state for a gate to be in, and the same
root cause as #4080. Making that check blocking without this would have
reopened #4080 in the PR gate.

validate_file now reads entries and compares only `text`, and skips any
key whose target entry is not `current` — skipped and missing are
coverage states owned by `tasks next`, not placeholder defects.

Adds the enforcement point for io.METADATA_FIELDS: an entry field nobody
declared is surfaced as a structure warning rather than left for the next
field-blind reader to guess at.

[#4080] Categorize `validate variables` findings and publish `blocking`

Every finding now carries a `category` — variables / format / untranslated
/ error — and `untranslated` is advisory. The JSON report gains a
top-level `blocking` (the sum of every non-advisory category, a deny-list
so a category added later counts by default), `summary[locale]` becomes a
per-category object, and the exit code is the blocking count rather than
the raw finding total.

The load-bearing decision is that untranslated keys do not gate. All 986
current findings — 34 keys × 29 locales, every one genuinely absent, zero
real mismatches — are coverage, and export-all.sh already gates coverage
upstream on `pending: 0`. Counting them at the post-export gate is what
forced a METADATA_FIELDS post-filter in shell; a gate consumers must
post-filter is a gate that gets mis-filtered.

audit_locale reads entries too, so a skip-marked entry (a deliberate
non-translation that KEEPS the source placeholder) is no longer reported
as an "[EMPTY]" translation missing every variable — the failure the
text-only view introduced when it replaced the flattener in 4213484cc.

[#4080] Reflow four over-wrapped statements in validate.py

Formatter-driven line joins in _glossary_handler and _hashes_handler. No
behaviour change; separated so the categorization commit reads clean.

[#4080] Point the shell gates at the report's `blocking` count

export-all.sh reads `blocking` and nothing else — a KeyError on an older
report shape surfaces as an unparseable report, which the caller already
treats as dirty rather than clean. That replaces the shell-side sum over
`summary`, and with it the post-filter that had to re-derive which key
shapes were metadata; re-deriving that policy in shell is how #4080 got
its METADATA_FIELDS list.

review-locale-branches.sh and pr-per-locale.sh prefer `blocking` but keep
the old flat-integer `summary` fallback: both validate OTHER branches'
worktrees, where a CLI predating this field is a real possibility.

Docs updated to match: untranslated keys appear in the report but never
gate — coverage is the `pending: 0` gate's job.

fix(admin): match ADMIN_ALLOWED_CIDRS against the true client IP

env['otto.client_ip'] is privacy-masked before this middleware runs (last
IPv4 octet zeroed, IPv6 to /48), so judging membership against it misjudged
every range finer than the mask in both directions: a single-admin-IP /32
entry could never match its own client, while an entry equal to a masked
network address admitted every neighbour sharing it.

Judge through env['otto.ip_match'] instead -- the verdict-only closure
IPPrivacyMiddleware installs over the resolved PRE-MASK address. Full
/32-/128 precision without the unmasked address ever landing in env, a log,
or this middleware; the denial WARN still reports only the masked value. A
request that never passed the otto mount carries no closure and falls back
to comparing the resolved IP, which in that topology was never masked.
Anything non-callable in the key is judged like an absent one, never called,
and a request with no resolvable IP still fails closed.

feat(config): warn at boot on unparseable ADMIN_ALLOWED_CIDRS entries

check_admin_allowed_cidrs sits beside check_admin_allowed_hosts and names
every site.admin.allowed_cidrs entry that does not parse as a CIDR range,
distinguishing "some entries dropped, the survivors enforce" from "no entry
parses, so both admin surfaces 404 on every request".

WARN, not raise, for the same reason as the host check: the runtime is
already fail-closed -- AdminNetworkIsolation keeps a wholly unparseable list
ACTIVE with an empty range set -- so the over-exposure a raise would prevent
cannot happen, while raising would abort the public site over an admin-only
typo. What fail-closed cannot do is tell the operator, whose first symptom
is otherwise an admin console dark even from inside the range they meant.

Parses and rescues exactly what the middleware does, so it warns about
precisely the entries the middleware will drop; the spec pins that agreement
across the same input table.

fix(admin): qualify the gate WARN remedies so they do not misdirect

Three remedies told operators to do something that either re-opens the hole
the denial closes, or does nothing on their install:

  mode with no explicit CIDRs trusts every private-network peer as a proxy,
  which restores exactly the forwarded-host spoofing the provenance rule
  exists to block. It now demands explicit proxy CIDRs.
- The no-detected-host WARN pointed at the allowlist, which was never
  consulted. The usual field cause is nginx's default proxy_pass rewriting
  Host to an IP literal, so it now names the proxy-side fix

- "Unset ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS to allow the canonical host only" is not a
  hardening step on a localhost or bare-IP install: the canonical-anchor
  fallback has nothing to anchor on there, so unsetting self-disables the
  gate. Both the boot and per-request lines now say so.

load_json_file returns whatever json.load produced and only falls back to
{} on a decode error, so a valid non-object document arrives as a list.

source passed: `key not in source` then tested against list elements
rather than keys, marking every key of the target file an orphan.
`remove-key --orphans --apply` would empty that locale file outright. The
target file was unguarded at both its call sites too, where a non-object
document raised TypeError instead.

Adds _remove_key_document as the single load path: it returns the mapping,
or warns and returns {} for anything else, so a malformed file is skipped
rather than emptied. The handler now loads the target once and threads it
into both helpers, dropping a redundant read and keeping the warning to
one line per file.

The docstring on _remove_key_orphans claimed load_json_file returns {} for
an unparseable source — the premise this bug disproves — and is corrected.

Both tests fail without the guard, each with its own failure mode: the
source-side one deletes three keys, the target-side one raises TypeError.

passkeys get mfa_required with 'webauthn' in mfa_methods, completed by
Rodauth's own POST /auth/webauthn-auth. Each factor only gates a login
when its completion route is actually loaded, so leftover credentials
under a disabled feature never strand anyone.

A login whose FIRST factor was the passkey (webauthn-login) bypasses the
requirement — the presented credential can't also be the pending second
factor (previously: awaiting_mfa with an uncompletable challenge, i.e. a
login loop) — and user-verified passkey logins count as two factors
natively. after_two_factor_authentication moved from Hooks::MFA to a new
Hooks::TwoFactor registered for MFA or WebAuthn, because in a
webauthn-only deployment the session sync it performs never ran: a
passkey completed the challenge Rodauth-side while awaiting_mfa stayed
true forever.

The SSO-linking surfaces (link_sso second-factor prediction, sso-link-
confirm's ConfirmSsoLink call) apply the same rules, closing for
passkey-only accounts the predicted-no-MFA direct-bind path that #3858
closed for OTP. mfa_auth_url now derives from the decision's factor
predicates (a passkey+recovery account no longer gets pointed at an OTP
route) and carries the /auth mount prefix.

fix(mail): treat provider-check errors as indeterminate, never demote verified domains

Sender strategies conflated 'could not determine' with 'provider says
not verified': a rotated API key, 401/5xx, or transport failure returned
verified: false, which DomainValidationWorker persisted as
provider_verified = false — silently flipping a previously verified
custom sender domain to failed on the next scheduled check.

The contract is now tri-state across all four strategies (smtp2go,
lettermint, ses, sendgrid): true = provider confirms, false = provider
authoritatively says no (pending / not_found), nil = indeterminate
(missing credential, provider API error, transport failure).

The worker now distinguishes 'check never ran' (no credentials / smtp:
keep the DNS-result fallback) from 'check ran but was inconclusive'
(leave the stored provider_verified untouched and exclude it from
save_fields, recording a 'Provider check inconclusive' last_error while
still completing the job).

fix(validation): stop optional DNS records from gating sender verification

Hoist the four verbatim copies of required_dns_records (ses, sendgrid,
lettermint, smtp2go) into BaseStrategy, leaving classify_record_purpose
as the per-provider hook, and exclude advisory records ('optional' =>
true) from the gating set — matching the discipline already applied by
BaseSenderStrategy#check_dns_records and MailerConfig. A missing
track.<domain> CNAME can no longer fail all_verified in
ValidateSenderDomain nor poison DomainValidationWorker's
provider_verified fallback.

refactor(mail): derive all provider lists from a single descriptor registry

Adding a provider used to mean touching ~10 independent hashes and case
arms (strategy factories, PROVIDER_TYPES, ProviderConfig::DEFAULTS,
Mailer dispatch/auto-detect, ConfigSummary, ConfigGenerator, feedback
PROVIDERS) which drifted silently — config_summary shipped without a
lettermint arm and nobody noticed.

Onetime::Mail::ProviderRegistry is now the one authoritative source:
each provider is a frozen Data descriptor (required/optional credential
keys, provisioning/feedback capability, strategy/delivery class names
resolved lazily, config-builder method, detect keys, env placeholders,
DNS defaults). Every legacy constant is redefined as a derivation so
external callers keep working, and parity specs pin the derived content
to the exact pre-refactor values.

ConfigSummary.masked_provider_config now dispatches on descriptors and
runs the raw config through the same per-provider builders the delivery
path uses, so a provider can never again be omitted from the summary.

fix(jobs): guard provider checks on required credential keys, not hash emptiness

DomainValidationWorker's guards tested creds && !creds.empty?, which is
blind for smtp2go: Mailer.smtp2go_provider_config bakes in
returnpath/tracking subdomain defaults via ENV.fetch, so the hash is
never empty even with no API key — check_essentials! waved the worker
through at boot and the per-message guard let a doomed API call run
(returning verified: nil under the tri-state contract, but with an
opaque HTTP 401 instead of a legible reason).

Both guards now ask ProviderRegistry.missing_required_credentials and
name the exact missing keys: check_essentials! raises with them, and
the per-message guard skips the provider check and logs them (behaving
as check-never-ran, i.e. the established DNS-fallback degraded mode).
check_essentials! also now scopes to provisioning providers via the
registry instead of the hand-rolled 'not smtp' test.

DnsRecordCheckWorker has no sibling guard (its strategies take
credentials: {} by design), so no change there.

ConfigRegistry's serialize_mailer coerced provider_verified with

comparison and extend the blocked range list to cover NAT64, 6to4,
and Teredo prefixes, which the native IPAddr predicates do not
account for.

Block IPv4-compatible IPv6 in SSRF host checks

blocked_ip? only unwrapped IPv4-mapped IPv6 (::ffff:a.b.c.d), so
IPv4-compatible literals (::a.b.c.d) slipped past every native range
predicate: valid_issuer_host?('https://[::169.254.169.254]') returned
true, reaching the cloud metadata service, with ::127.0.0.1 and
::10.0.0.1 as loopback/private variants. Extend the unwrap to
ipv4_compat? so #native decodes the embedded IPv4 before the range
checks, and add regression rows covering the three vectors.

blocked_ip? passed 0.0.0.0, :: (incl. the ::0.0.0.0 spelling), and
special-use IPv4 ranges the native predicates never matched. 0.0.0.0
and :: connect to localhost as a target, so both were loopback
bypasses. Add a zero-address guard and a BLOCKED_IPV4_RANGES list
(0.0.0.0/8, 100.64.0.0/10, 192.0.0.0/24, 198.18.0.0/15, 240.0.0.0/4)
checked after the IPv4 unwrap, with regression rows for each vector.

Add shared SSRF egress guard for outbound HTTP

Onetime::Http::Guard unifies three divergent per-callsite blocklists
(SafeFetch BLOCKED_V4/V6, SsoConfig::SsrfProtection TRANSITION_RANGES +
BLOCKED_IPV4_RANGES, DispatchNotification's loopback/private/link-local
check) into one deny-by-default range set — the union of all three, which
adds Teredo 2001::/32 (missing from SafeFetch) and multicast/documentation
ranges (missing from the SSO validator). blocked_ip? fails closed on
unparseable input; resolve_and_validate! rejects a host if ANY resolved
address is blocked and returns addresses IPv4-first for pinning via
pinned_address!. Consumers land in follow-up commits.

Delegate SafeFetch and SSO issuer checks to shared Guard

Both validation paths now consume Onetime::Http::Guard's union blocklist
instead of their own diverged copies. SafeFetch keeps its multi-address
connect fallback and BlockedTarget error contract (Guard::Blocked is
translated at the boundary); it picks up Teredo 2001::/32 coverage.
SsoConfig::SsrfProtection keeps its boolean mixin API and picks up
multicast (224.0.0.0/4, ff00::/8) and documentation (2001:db8::/32)
coverage; an unparseable resolver answer now blocks the host instead of
being skipped (fail closed).

The SSO tryout's Resolv stub previously reopened the class inside the
tryouts sandbox module and never intercepted real resolution; it now
stubs ::Resolv's singleton so assertions run hermetically.

Pin webhook and SSO test-connection egress to validated IPs

Both paths validated the target host, then built a fresh Net::HTTP that
re-resolved DNS at connect time — the classic validate-then-reresolve
DNS-rebinding window. Each now resolves once via Guard.pinned_address!
and dials that exact IP with Net::HTTP#ipaddr= while Host, SNI, and
certificate verification keep using the hostname. The explicit nil
p_addr also disables http_proxy environment pickup, which would have
silently bypassed pinning.

Webhook dispatch drops its Addrinfo-based validate_webhook_target!
(loopback/private/link-local only — the weakest of the three blocklists)
in favor of the Guard union; Guard::Blocked propagates to
dispatch_to_channel's per-channel rescue, which classifies it as a
permanent :error the worker never retries. TestConnection's pinning in
fetch_url also covers the Entra path, which never passed through
valid_issuer_host?; a blocked issuer returns a structured blocked_target
result that deliberately omits the resolved IP.

Pin runtime OIDC egress via OpenIDConnect.http_config hook

Tenant-configured issuer URLs are validated when the SSO config is
saved, but discovery, JWKS, and token traffic runs inside the OIDC gems
(openid_connect -> swd/webfinger/rack-oauth2), which re-resolve DNS per
request through their own Faraday connections — no app callsite exists
to wrap. The one supported seam is OpenIDConnect.http_config: install a
:net_http adapter whose per-request config block pins the live Net::HTTP
to Guard.pinned_address! before it dials. Faraday 2's adapter call
replaces each gem's default adapter, and faraday-net_http invokes the
block per connection build, so every request (including redirect hops)
is independently resolved, validated, and pinned.

http_config is set-once per process and propagation skips
already-configured sub-protocols, so install! runs first thing in
Features::OmniAuth.configure — before any provider registers — and the
spec locks in that all four gem modules share the exact block. A
configured forward proxy voids ipaddr pinning, so the hook fails closed
rather than silently un-pinning.

Note for future integration specs driving real OIDC request-phase
traffic: the adapter block does real DNS (WebMock cannot intercept it);
stub Onetime::Http::Guard.pinned_address! in such specs.

method silently widened to standard mode and re-exposed exactly the

Fix NullPointerError when clearing auth database in simple mode

Resolves:
Auth -- [clear_auth_database] Failed to clear auth database: undefined method 'tables' for nil

Treat blank AUTH_DATABASE_URL as unset

An exported-but-empty AUTH_DATABASE_URL is truthy in Ruby, so it won the
`ENV['AUTH_DATABASE_URL'] || <default>` render in the auth config files and
the `full['database_url'] || 'sqlite://data/auth.db'` fallback in
AuthConfig. The empty string then reached Sequel.connect, where
URI.parse('').scheme is nil and adapter_class raises a bare
`NoMethodError: undefined method 'to_sym' for nil` — a fallback that is
defeated by the exact case it exists to cover, reported as a nil crash deep
in Sequel.

Normalize blank to unset in both places: AuthConfig#database_url and
#database_url_migrations (via a private #presence), which covers operator
config files that render the value some other way, and in the ERB of
auth.defaults.yaml and spec/auth.test.yaml so the rendered config is
correct on its own.

Add Auth::Database.available? for reachability checks

Auth::Database.connection returns a LazyConnection proxy that defers the
real connect to first use, so it is ALWAYS truthy in full mode. Callers
that guard with `if db` are therefore asking "is this full mode?" while
believing they asked "is there a usable database?", and the difference
surfaces later as an exception at an arbitrary query.

available? forces the connection behind a rescue and returns a plain
boolean, giving callers that must degrade gracefully (CLI commands,
tryouts without a provisioned database) something honest to branch on.
Not memoized: a database can come up or go away during a process's
lifetime, and tests reset the connection between examples.

Fix close_account_try DB guard and PG migration path

Two setup defects, both of which halted the whole tryouts batch (a global
setup failure sets @setup_failed, which stops every remaining file):

- The `@db = Auth::Database.connection` guard never skipped, because the
  LazyConnection proxy is truthy in full mode regardless of whether a
  database exists. Ask Auth::Database.available? instead.
- Migrations ran as Sequel::Migrator.run(@db, ...) using the application
  credentials. On PostgreSQL that is `permission denied for schema public`
  — DDL needs the elevated database_url_migrations role. Delegate to
  Auth::Migrator.run_if_needed, which already handles the switch.

Verified both paths: full mode against PG (12/12, migrations applied under
the migrator role), full mode with a blank AUTH_DATABASE_URL falling back
to in-memory SQLite (12/12), and simple mode (clean skip).

Fixes the 3 simple-lane and 2 full-lane failures on this branch.

Add tests/lanes/run --only for single-file iteration

A whole lane is minutes, which is too slow to loop on one failing file;
the alternative people reach for is raw rspec, which is exactly what the
hermetic runner exists to prevent. --only <path> (repeatable) runs just
that file inside the lane's environment and skips the lane's tasks file.
Same scrub, same lane env, same exec — the boundary is unchanged.

Runner is chosen by filename: *_try.rb goes to try --agent, everything
else to rspec (path:LINE forwarded, so a single example works). Mixing
the two in one invocation is rejected rather than given an ordering rule.

Documented in tests/lanes/README.md and AGENTS.md, with the caveat that
--only skips the tasks file's setup steps (e.g. locales:sync in the full
lanes), so the whole lane still gates a push.

Walk all validated addresses on connect-level failure

pinned_address! returned only the first validated address, so a
multi-address host whose first IP was unreachable failed webhook
delivery and SSO test-connection even when a sibling validated address
was healthy. SafeFetch already walked its candidate list; extract that
fallback into Guard.try_each_address! and adopt it at both callsites.

Each dial stays pinned to one exact validated IP (Net::HTTP#ipaddr=),
so the walk is a reachability fallback across the already-validated
set, never a widening. Fallback triggers only on connect-level errnos
(now shared as Guard::CONNECT_FALLBACK_ERRNOS, referenced by
SafeFetch); timeouts, TLS, and HTTP errors propagate from the first
dial unchanged.

The OIDC http_config hook keeps single-address pinned_address! by
design: faraday-net_http yields the live Net::HTTP once, pre-dial, and
the seam does not control the request cycle across the four OIDC gems
— documented in oidc_http_pinning.rb. IPv4-first ordering already
covers the dominant broken-dual-stack case there.

Restore tryout result lines dropped by style pass

The rubocop cleanup removed the trailing expressions that four test cases
depended on for their result value:

- custom_domain_destroy_cascade_try.rb: the bare `true` after
  `destroy!` (x2) — destroy! returns Familia::MultiResult, not true.
- custom_domain_destroy_cascade_try.rb: `captured_primary_exists` after
  the begin/ensure — without it the case asserted the destroy! return
  value instead of the ordering fact it exists to prove.
- close_account_try.rb: `@ca_result` — the case asserted the sidecar
  purge count instead of the sweep's deleted-blob count.

Stop Lint/Void from eating tryout result lines

AllCops already excludes try/**/* and apps/**/try/**/*, but RuboCop only
honours AllCops.Exclude for explicitly-named files when --force-exclusion
is passed. The pre-commit hook passes it; an ad-hoc `rubocop -A <file>`
does not, which is how bb9ca4cb9 deleted the trailing expressions four
testcases used as their result value.

Per-cop Exclude is honoured on every invocation path, so pin it there for
the two cops whose autocorrect removes a bare trailing expression.

Disable proxy pickup on the SafeFetch pinned dial

Net::HTTP.new defaults p_addr to :ENV, so an http_proxy in the
environment flips proxy? to true. Net::HTTP#connect only honours
@ipaddr (via conn_address) when proxy? is false; with a proxy it dials
the proxy and sends CONNECT <host>:<port>, letting the proxy re-resolve
the hostname. The IP pin SafeFetch validated is then silently inert —
exactly the rebinding window the guard exists to close.

Note the trigger is http_proxy, not https_proxy: #proxy_uri builds a
hardcoded-http-scheme URI before calling find_proxy, so https_proxy
alone never matches here.

The webhook dispatcher already passes an explicit nil p_addr for this
reason (dispatch_notification.rb, commit a45671f83); this was the one
pinned-dial site that missed it.

Restore Guard.resolve_addresses after the guard tryout

The DNS stub was a bare `def G.resolve_addresses`, which mutates the
Onetime::Http::Guard module singleton for the rest of the process.
Tryouts gives each testcase a fresh Object.new container, not a fresh
process, and tests/lanes/run hands every file to one `bundle exec try`
— so the stub leaked into every file that ran afterwards.

It was already doing real damage: unit/http/ sorts before
unit/operations/, so dispatch_notification_webhook_try.rb's
alias_method captured this stub as "the original" and its own teardown
faithfully restored the stub, permanently.

Switch to the alias/restore pattern that file already uses.

Restore ::Resolv.getaddresses after the SSRF transition tryout

Same leak as the guard tryout, but against stdlib rather than a project
seam: the file replaced ::Resolv.getaddresses with a fixture lookup and
never put it back. tests/lanes/run runs every tryout in one process, so
each later file resolving through that method got [] — a silent
"nothing resolvable", which several guards read as "blocked".

Alias the original away before defining the stub and restore it in a
teardown, matching dispatch_notification_webhook_try.rb.

[#4087] feat(config): add MiddlewareStack.trusted_proxy_mode as the single mode reader

site.network.trusted_proxy.mode had no accessor: ip_privacy_security_config
read `tp['mode'] || 'filter'` inline and branched on `== 'depth'`, so any
unrecognized value silently ran the filter branch.

trusted_proxy_mode owns the 'filter' default (the ERB default in
config.defaults.yaml stays as operator documentation, but no Ruby path depends
on it), canonicalizes case the way the sibling `header` setting already does,
and returns only a value from TRUSTED_PROXY_MODES.

Two independently deduped warnings, neither of which raises — the fallback is
the safer mode, and a boot log line must never be the thing that fails a boot:

- unknown after canonicalization (`dept`) -> filter, warn naming the value
- canonicalization changed the value (`Depth`) -> depth, warn that this is a
  runtime change on upgrade, since the old exact-match branch ran filter

Wires ip_privacy_security_config through the accessor. `tp` still supplies
header, depth and cidrs.

[#4087] refactor(admin): report the trusted-proxy mode actually in force

trusted_proxy_posture echoed the operator's raw `mode` string, so
TRUSTED_PROXY_MODE=Depth produced `trusted_proxy: enabled (mode=Depth)` on a
deployment that was running filter — an untrue statement on the one line the
#4062 changelog tells operators to read to confirm the gate protecting the
admin surfaces.

Both halves of the posture now come from the shared accessors, so the line
reports mode=depth for `Depth` and mode=filter for a typo. Removes the TODO
block that tracked this issue.

[#4087] refactor(security): read trusted_proxy through the shared predicate

Both collapsed-IP hints dug site.network.trusted_proxy.enabled inline. The
hint's whole claim is about how the IP-privacy mount resolved the client
address, so it has to ask the same question that mount asked; four independent
readings of one security-relevant setting is how a default drifts in three
places and not the fourth.

No require_relative and no rescue: both files are reached via `require
'onetime'`, which loads the middleware stack first, so the constant resolves at
call time on every path that can reach a lockout.

[#4087] docs(config): document trusted_proxy.mode canonicalization and the upgrade case

Notes in config.defaults.yaml and .env.reference that the mode is a closed set
matched case-insensitively, that an unrecognized value falls back to filter
with a boot warning, and that the YAML ERB default is documentation rather than
the thing the code relies on.

Changelog fragment calls out the upgrade consequence for operators: a
mixed-case TRUSTED_PROXY_MODE was running filter and now genuinely runs depth,
which still does not record peer trust in otto.via_trusted_proxy pending
delano/otto#226 (the upstream half of #4024), so forwarded host headers are
discarded and custom domains classify as canonical. Remedy is to set filter
explicitly.

[#4087] fix(config): make the canonicalization remedy fit a padded value

`raw != configured` compares against the un-stripped string, so "  depth  "
trips the canonicalization warning — correctly, since the old literal
`== 'depth'` match ran filter for it. But the remedy said "write it in lower
case", which is no help to an operator whose value is already lower case. Name
the exact string to write instead.

[#4087] test(config): pin trusted_proxy_mode canonicalization and rejection

Covers the accessor's whole contract: the closed set, silent resolution for
unset/nil/empty/whitespace and exact-lowercase values, canonicalization of
Depth/DEPTH/FILTER with the warning naming the raw form, rejection of dept and
friends to filter without raising, and warn-once dedup across repeated calls
for both keys independently.

Also asserts the two branches of ip_privacy_security_config honour the
canonicalized mode: mixed-case Depth sets trusted_proxy_depth and registers no
CIDRs, an unrecognized mode lands in the filter branch with RFC1918 trusted.

[#4087] test(admin): pin the trusted_proxy field on the boot posture line

Six examples over the operator-facing string: disabled for enabled:false and
for an absent block, mode=filter verbatim, mode=depth for a mixed-case Depth,
and mode=filter for a typo with an explicit assertion that the operator's `dept`
does not appear anywhere in the line.

Adds capture_admin_gate_infos! beside the existing warn sink (the posture line
is INFO, which that sink swallows) and snapshots site.network in the shared
hook, since a leaked trusted_proxy block changes client-IP resolution for every
later example in the process.

[#4087] test(security): pin the rate-limit hints against the shared predicate

Disabled/absent/enabled hint behaviour was already covered. Adds the one case
that coverage cannot catch: with a STRING 'true' the strict `== true` predicate
is false and the hint still fires — pinning both that the hint now asks
MiddlewareStack rather than digging the config, and that the constant resolves
at call time under a bare tryout boot with no require_relative.

[#4087] docs(config): drop the stale depth-mode forwarded-host claim

The upgrade advisory and the trusted_proxy_mode comment both told operators
that depth mode does not record peer trust in env['otto.via_trusted_proxy'],
so forwarded host headers are discarded and custom domains classify as
canonical. That was true against the otto the claim was written for. It is
not true here: otto is pinned at 2.8 (Gemfile.lock 2.8.0), where depth mode
records via_trusted_proxy from the pre-rewrite peer (delano/otto#226), and
try/integration/middleware/detect_host_ip_privacy_stack_try.rb pins exactly
that as "the deliberate flip of the KNOWN LIMITATION this case used to pin".

This matters more than a doc nit. The bullet is the upgrade advisory for the
one genuine runtime change on this branch — canonicalization making `Depth`
select depth where it previously ran filter — and it was steering operators
toward TRUSTED_PROXY_MODE=filter to avoid custom-domain breakage that no
longer happens. The real hazard in that switch is a TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH that
does not match the proxy topology: depth then resolves a proxy or CDN address
as the client, which is what feeds admin CIDR enforcement and the rate-limit
bucket key. The advisory now names that instead, and the #4024 cross-reference
goes with the claim it was supporting.

docs/specs/domain-ip-allowlist/domain-ip-allowlist.md carries the same
sentence but is a dated gap list whose next clause already annotates it
"Since fixed: otto#226"; left as-is.

Comment-and-prose only, no behaviour change: middleware_stack_spec 57/57,
create_account/reset_request rate-limiter + detect_host_ip_privacy_stack
tryouts 72/72.

[#4087] fix(config): only claim a behaviour change when the mode actually moved

The canonicalization warning fired for any rewritten spelling, but its text
told the operator that upgrading with this value CHANGES how the client IP is
resolved. The pre-existing branch was an exact `== 'depth'` test, so the only
spelling whose runtime behaviour moves on upgrade is one that canonicalizes to
depth without already being exactly `depth`. `FILTER` and `  filter  ` ran
filter before and run filter now — the claim was false for them, and sending
operators to check TRUSTED_PROXY_DEPTH over a non-change is worse than noise.

Sharing one warn_once tag across both cases made it a suppression bug as well:
every Application subclass re-reads this, so a cosmetic rewrite in the first
stack consumed the tag and silenced the real behaviour-change warning in the
next.

Split into two tags. :trusted_proxy_mode_canonicalized keeps the strong text
and now fires only for `raw == 'depth' && configured != 'depth'` — compared
against the unstripped value, since whitespace was significant to the old exact
match and `  depth  ` therefore did change. :trusted_proxy_mode_respelled
covers the rest, still naming both forms so the boot log and the config file
reconcile by eye, but stating that resolution is unchanged.

Specs pin both halves and the tag isolation. Changelog now scopes the
action-required notice to depth spellings.

[#4139] fix(auth): fail closed on unavailable domain restrictions

ADR-024 A3 says a restriction whose backing method cannot run offers
nothing, but availability was only ever asked at global scope. On a
custom host that answer is incomplete: password and email-auth also
require the domain's sign-in opt-in, SSO requires tenant credentials or
the operator's platform fallback, and WebAuthn is not scoped per custom
host at all (#4137). A host inheriting a global restriction to a method
it cannot run resolved :restricted and advertised a sign-in path that
could not complete.

Adds SigninConfig.restriction_available_for_request? as the one place
that rule lives, and routes the runtime gate and the domain settings API
through it. It narrows only, with explicit pass-throughs for canonical
hosts, installs with nothing restricted, and hosts we could not classify
— a false flag must never manufacture a restriction. resolve_restrict_to
applies the same custom-host narrowing to persisted DOMAIN restrictions,
replacing resolve_domain_restrict_to.

Route classification: create_account, verify_account and
verify_account_resend are password routes by default but become WebAuthn
routes when Rodauth's webauthn_verify_account feature is loaded — the
ceremony changes without the route names changing. Classify them by the
loaded feature so a WebAuthn-only signup can complete on a
webauthn-restricted host, and a password-restricted host does not offer
a ceremony that mints a session by another method.

Datastore failures: move the Redis rescue up from domain_id_for, which
could only see the domain lookup, to the resolution path, which sees all
three reads on the custom-host hot path. The degrade now splits on the
global value (in-memory config, so it cannot itself have failed): fail
closed to :unavailable when a restriction is actually in force, stay
:unrestricted when the install restricts nothing — otherwise a transient
blip would take every gated route on every custom domain to 404 on an
install whose correct answer is "no restriction". The degrade path gets
its own restrict_to_domain_lookup_degraded event, since it enforces
nothing and is otherwise silent.

[#4139] fix(auth): expose unavailable sign-in state

features.restrict_to is a string-or-null scalar, so the resolver's
:unavailable state serialized as null — indistinguishable from standard
mode — and the sign-in page rendered every method on a host whose gate
rejects all of them. ADR-024 A4 closes that display-side fail-open.

- ConfigSerializer emits effective_restrict_to ({ state, restrict_to,
  source }) alongside the legacy scalar, which now projects :unavailable
  to null deliberately rather than by omission
- bootstrap contract gains effectiveRestrictToSchema, optional so
  payloads from older backends stay valid
- AuthMethodSelector fails closed on effective_restrict_to.state rather
  than on the scalar, and renders an explicit unavailable branch; the
  nulled scalar reads as "no restriction" and would widen an
  unsatisfiable restriction back into the full method list

The serializer also asks restriction_available_for_request? instead of
global_restriction_available?, so the page cannot answer the
availability question differently from the route gate. It briefly did:
under a global password restriction, a custom host with no enabled
SigninConfig showed a password form whose Rodauth routes the gate had
already taken to 404.

[#4139] fix(invite): offer usable restricted sign-in paths

ShowInvite advertised tenant SSO from the stored sso_config.enabled?
flag alone, but that flag outlives the route: AUTH_ENABLED, provider
support and the domain's SigninConfig each make tenant SSO unusable
without clearing it. On an sso-restricted domain the invite page could
therefore offer exactly one method, and that method dead.

Ask the same runtime ladder the sign-in route asks
(SsoConfig.tenant_sso_available_for?), and when the host permits SSO but
the tenant arm does not (sso_available_for_tenant_host?), fall back to
the operator's platform providers so the invitee still has a way in.

Platform-fallback entries deliberately carry no provider_type: the
platform registry vocabulary (oidc, entra, google, github) is a
different namespace from the tenant PROVIDER_TYPES enum (oidc,
entra_id) that consumers read the field as — 'entra' vs 'entra_id'
collide outright. platform_route_name is carried by both arms and is
what callers should route and branch on.

AcceptInvite.vue and the show-invite response contract follow, and the
magic_link/email_auth naming seam is documented on both sides — it is
the only method whose wire name differs from its restrict_to name, and
comparing the strings directly silently drops it.

[#4139] fix(domains): avoid false SSO lockout warning

The lockout confirmation fired on any `available === false` verdict from
the server, including sso_not_permitted caused solely by the current
SigninConfig having sso_enabled=false. Selecting SSO sets that flag in
the same atomic PUT, so that state is self-healing — warning about it
trains operators to click through the one prompt that does matter.

Guard only when the verdict has some other cause: sso_not_permitted with
SSO already enabled still warns, as do all other reasons, and an absent
verdict still fires nothing.

[#4139] fix(auth): apply host-aware availability in the simple-mode gate

Core::Base#restrict_to_allows? was the fourth consumer of
resolve_restrict_to and had the same gap the other three just closed: it
asked global_restriction_available?, so an inherited global restriction
was never narrowed through the custom host's own capabilities, and this
gate could accept a method the full-mode gate and the /signin page both
treat as dark.

It cannot take the domain id off the SigninConfig — `config&.domain_id`
is nil in exactly the no-config case that matters — so custom_domain_id
is split out of domain_signin_config and memoized, since two gates ask
per request.

Spec fixtures corrected where they pinned pre-A3 behavior: the full-mode
'sso' fixture now stands up tenant SsoConfig credentials (without them
the host resolves :unavailable and 404s the very SSO routes those
examples assert stay reachable), and the ConfigSerializer 'enabled
domain SigninConfig' context stubs AUTH_SIGNIN and the email-auth
feature, which the file-level OT.conf stub does not carry.

docs(security): weekly audit for 2026-08-13

Delta audit against the 2026-08-06 report, covering the 448 commits since
(HEAD ae4a00a0): passkeys/WebAuthn, the shared SSRF egress guard, SMTP2GO,
trusted_proxy mode, admin isolation, domain restrict_to, and the Stripe
currency-migration path.

Three findings:

- HIGH: RABBITMQ_VERIFY_PEER uses `== 'true'` against a default-ON control,
  so any other spelling (TRUE, 1, yes) silently disables AMQPS peer
  verification on a channel whose payloads carry secret retrieval keys.
- LOW: the hand-written /auth/* JSON routes gate on rodauth.logged_in?,
  which is true at first-factor completion, so an MFA-incomplete session can
  purge the victim's other sessions and read account posture. This is the
  half of the 2026-07-06 M-11 finding that 02dd1b21d did not reach.
- LOW: SMTP2GO errors raised inside Smtp2goClient carry the raw provider
  response body into logs and Sentry, bypassing the redact_emails discipline
  the sibling delivery-failure path applies.

The domain restrict_to enforcement gap is recorded as known and tracked
(ADR-024 A1) rather than re-filed.

An unreadable `restrict_to` policy was degrading to the global-only answer
on every host, which silently widens the permitted sign-in methods for a
custom domain whose per-domain restriction lives in the datastore. ADR-024
A3 says a restriction that cannot be honored must fail closed.

Restore unconditional fail-closed, with three changes over the earlier
iteration:

- Answer 503 (`Onetime::SigninPolicyUnavailable`), not the A7 404. A7's 404
  exists to hide policy-gated methods; when the policy is unreadable there
  is nothing to hide, and an honest infrastructure failure is alertable and
  carries retry-after. Translated in both edges (otto_hooks and
  Auth::ErrorTranslator).
- Carve out operator hosts (`:canonical`, `:subdomain`). They have no
  per-domain half to lose — the global restriction is in-memory and fully
  enforceable, so those requests are enforced rather than failed. The test
  is positive, not `!= :custom`: a failing domain-index read classifies a
  real custom domain as `:invalid`.
- Delete the machinery the three-way split needed: `known_restriction`,
  `lookup_failure_resolution`, and the degrade event.

The rule lives in `SigninConfig.resolve_lookup_failure` so the full-mode
gate and the simple-mode gate share it and cannot drift (A2). The
ConfigSerializer keeps its swallow-and-degrade rescue by design; the
asymmetry is documented there.

[#4139] docs(auth): pin what :invalid means to every consumer

`:invalid` reads like a property of the hostname, but DomainStrategy also
answers it when `known_custom_domain?` raises — choose_strategy's blanket
`rescue StandardError` returns nil and `call` resolves that to :invalid. A
datastore blip therefore classifies a real customer domain :invalid, and
the ~10 consumers testing `== :custom` silently hand it operator treatment.

Documents the two ways to reach :invalid at the producer (DomainStrategy's
class doc, with the consumer table), and points the three downstream
readers at it rather than restating it: custom_domain_request?,
OPERATOR_HOST_STRATEGIES, and resolve_lookup_failure.

States the invariant the A3 carve-out rests on, in the only direction that
holds: a failure can never MANUFACTURE :canonical or :subdomain, so
operator_host? may be over-strict during an outage, never over-permissive.
The stronger claim is false — :subdomain's sweeps run after the datastore
read and the rescue wraps the whole chain, so subdomain hosts fail closed
alongside the custom domains while canonical sign-in stays up.

The table is pinned executably in
spec/unit/domain_strategy_classification_contract_spec.rb (47 examples), so
an eleventh consumer with the opposite polarity fails there and not in
review. It also pins the sign-up polarity flip A3 does NOT fix: when the
middleware read fails but the gate read succeeds, no 503 is raised and a
custom domain that never opted into sign-up follows the operator default.
ADR-024 A12 records that as a follow-up — the fix belongs in the resolvers,
since inverting custom_domain_request? would deny branding to genuinely
unplaceable hosts.
