[#4156] Add strict boolean parsing for configuration flags

Introduce `explicit_yes?`, `explicit_no?`, and `strict_bool!` to
ensure operator-supplied boolean flags are explicitly parsed.

`strict_bool!` prevents silent failures on misconfigured flags by
raising an error on unrecognized values, rather than defaulting to false
or true. Added comprehensive unit tests to verify token recognition and
the fail-fast behavior.
[#4156] Add ADR-037 for boolean token vocabulary standardization

[#4156] Harden strict_bool! for consistency and safety

Require Onetime::ConfigError directly to resolve load-order issues.
Normalize inputs once to ensure the empty-check and token tables stay
synchronized.

[#4156] Unify billing config parsing with Onetime::Utils.strict_bool!

Standardize ENV and configuration boolean parsing to use the shared
token vocabulary, ensuring consistent handling of truthy and falsy
values across billing features.

[#4156] Fail loudly on unrecognized RABBITMQ_VERIFY_PEER values

The == 'true' comparison failed open: TRUE, 1, yes, or stray whitespace
all silently disabled AMQPS certificate verification on a default-ON
control. Route through Onetime::Utils.strict_bool! so recognized tokens
resolve correctly and unrecognized ones raise at boot (ADR-033/ADR-037).

AMQP payloads carry secret retrieval keys, so an unverified TLS session
to a managed broker is a real exposure.

[#4156] Fix docstring divergence

The two methods now describe the same rule in the same words:
- ENV overrides config whenever present, including blank (→ false);
- only an absent variable reaches the config key. Dropped "explicitly
  unset," which was the misleading phrase. The automatic_tax? spec
  title and header comment now match enabled?'s wording.

[#4156] Filter strict_bool! error logging

A future caller could pass a credential-adjacent value as raw,
the error message echoes it into logs/Sentry (acknowledged in the inline comment).

[#4156] Never echo rejected boolean values from strict_bool!

strict_bool! is public and its ConfigError message reaches logs, the boot
trace, and Sentry's issue title. A future caller can hand it whatever an
operator put in an env var, including a value misrouted from a credential,
and by-param-name scrubbing cannot reach a string interpolated into the
exception itself. Suppression has to happen at the raise site.

The previous attempt echoed a 32-character truncated head (bool_echo /
MAX_BOOL_ECHO_LENGTH). That caps volume, not sensitivity: most secrets are
shorter than any workable cap, so the truncation was a smaller leak rather
than a fix. Both are removed.

The message now carries the flag name (the actionable part, since the
operator knows where they set it), the character count, the token
vocabularies, and the first 8 hex characters of sha256(normalized value) as
a correlation tag. The tag is deterministic, so two hosts with the same typo
match, and an operator can recompute it locally. For a low-entropy value
like "ture" the tag is brute-forceable, which is acceptable: low-entropy
values are exactly the case that was never sensitive.

Also removes strict_bool! from the mixed-in Onetime::Utils surface
(module_function), so call sites cannot drift back to the shorter name.

Restores the strict_bool! spec block dropped in c7b5eb520 and adds the
non-disclosure sweep: credential-shaped fixtures assert that neither the raw
value, its normalized form, nor any 4-character run of it appears in the
message, inspect, or full_message. A guard pins the absence of bool_echo and
MAX_BOOL_ECHO_LENGTH so the truncation approach cannot return quietly.

Caller assertions that pinned the old value-quoting contract are replaced
per the ADR-037 testing policy, with comments at each site.

**Kept**

- Routine dependency upgrades unless the entry stated a concrete

[#4157] Add request-aware auth resolvers and fail-closed sign-up policy

Operator auth defaults must require positive evidence, not the absence
of :custom. resolve_signin_enabled_for_request /
resolve_signup_enabled_for_request choose their branch on
SigninConfig.operator_host? (:canonical/:subdomain only); the
context-free resolvers keep their semantics for administrative and API
callers. Sign-up reuses sign-in's predicate rather than restating the
classification list, so the two gates cannot drift.

Sign-up also gains the read-failure path sign-in already had:
SignupConfig.resolve_lookup_failure raises SignupPolicyUnavailable on
any host not positively an operator host, and SignupConfigResolution
guards both datastore reads at the read rather than at each gate. The
shared shape lives in a new AuthPolicyUnavailable parent; the
subclasses stay separate so 'sign-up is down' is distinguishable in
both the user message and alert routing.

Otto dispatches error handlers on the exact class name, so the parent
buys the body shape but not the routing -- each subclass gets its own
register_error_handler. The Roda translator walks ancestors, so one
family entry covers both there.

[#4157] Require positive operator evidence on every auth gate

Three widens, not one. The runtime gates (Base#signin_enabled? /
via a new operator_domain?) now go through the request resolvers, so an
:invalid classification -- which DomainStrategy also answers when its
own datastore read raises for a real customer domain -- can no longer
hand that domain the operator's global auth default. The sign-in SSO
carve-out asymmetry is preserved: display passes domain_id, the POST
gate does not.

build_sso_config's platform-fallback guard keyed on == :custom too, so
an :invalid host was offered platform SSO providers the operator had
withheld from tenants -- a working sign-in method, not a rendering
detail. The predicate's two uses are now split: the fallback policy
guard takes the positive test, tenant-vs-platform selection stays keyed
on domain identity.

Both includers of SignupConfigResolution supply the request's
classification, so an unreadable tenant policy fails closed on exactly
the hosts the sign-in side does -- and resolve_autoverify no longer
falls back to the install-wide autoverify setting when a tenant's
config is unreadable.

custom_domain_request? and tenant_domain? are untouched, so branding
and routing for unknown hosts are unchanged; the DomainStrategy
consumer table is regrouped by which test each consumer uses.

[#4157] Pin operator-host classification in specs and tryouts

The classification contract spec now names each consumer by which test
it uses, a parity spec holds the display gate to the runtime gate
across every classification, and a new spec covers the
SignupPolicyUnavailable 503 path. The two auth tryouts gain cases for
:invalid on both gates and for the autoverify read failure.

[#4157] Document A12 fail-closed auth resolution in ADR-024

ADR-024 had only forward references to A12, no stub; it now carries the
decision, the three widens it covers, and the reasoning for leaving the
identity predicates alone. Adds the domain-resolution spec notes and a
Scriv fragment for all three behavior changes.
[#4157] Re-add long-term domain-resolution to spec

[#4157] Close the :invalid classification gap in the domain-ip-allowlist spec

The spec gated enforcement on `env['onetime.domain_strategy'] == :custom`,
inheriting the ambiguity A12 (#4157) just closed for the sign-in and sign-up
gates: DomainStrategy also answers :invalid when its own custom-domain
datastore read raises, so a blip would have stopped the filter enforcing for
every protected domain — a fail-open access-control bypass triggered by load.

A12's remedy does not transfer directly. Its positive operator test works
because sign-in/sign-up have opposite defaults on the two branches; this
feature is default-open on both, so the test alone changes nothing and the
naive fail-closed reading would deny every unknown host. The mechanism
therefore splits: operator_host? for scope, and the AccessConfig read itself
disambiguates the two :invalid cases — no record passes through (default-open
preserved), a raising read fails closed with 503 + Retry-After, not the 403
block page, which would blame the customer's CIDR list for an outage.

Makes the env['onetime.custom_domain'] stash a prerequisite rather than a
free win (it is what keeps the disambiguation off the healthy path), gives
policy-read failures their own counter, and pins both :invalid cases in the
test row.

[#4140] fix(auth): route settings API through the shared restrict_to resolver

The SSO host pin -- a custom domain with no enabled SigninConfig, reachable
only via SSO, inherits restrict_to='sso' because password/email default OFF
there -- existed as two private copies (ConfigSerializer#effective_global_
restrict_to and Auth::RestrictTo.global_restrict_to) and one omission.

The settings API had neither copy: it passed auth_config.restrict_to verbatim
as both the `global` value and the value keyed for restriction_available_for_
request?. For an SSO-only tenant that reported unrestricted/nil while the
request-time gate was enforcing restricted/sso -- the client was told sign-in
was unrestricted for methods that 404 in practice. That is the fail-open
direction ADR-034#degradation-is-fail-closed forbids.

Consolidate rather than add a third copy: SigninConfig.inherited_restrict_to
now owns the policy, and the gate, the display serializer, and the settings
API all call it. Intersection semantics are preserved -- an enabled config
speaks for itself, since an unconditional pin would resolve :conflict and
lock the host out.

Simple-mode Core::Controllers::Base#restrict_to_allows? deliberately keeps no
pin: simple mode serves no SSO route, so pinning 'sso' would darken the only
working method.

Un-pends the parity spec that documented this as a residual gap, and adds
unit coverage for inherited_restrict_to including the subtle case that a
*disabled* config still pins.

Prose across the tree still described the retired behaviour: a restriction

determinable at boot is now a fatal boot error, and host-scoped unavailability

An operator reading the old text would expect a misconfiguration to be
tolerated when it will in fact refuse to boot -- the most costly form of this

adds the fail-closed failure mode to the cannot-log-in runbook (a responder
would otherwise not recognise it), and corrects two frontend comments that
still cited the backend "nilling" an unhonorable restriction.

Two review findings against the initial SigninGate:

- unlock_account / unlock_account_request moved from UNGATED_ROUTES into

  LOGIN route, so a host with signin on and email_auth off would still
  emit links while POST /auth/email-auth-request 404s. Route-level ANDing
  on :login is wrong (dispatch is per-account, not per-route); the shared
  chokepoint is the fix.

already established. This caused a false-negative when platform SSO died

  already proven
- Update inherited_restrict_to to return this struct
- Add already_established: parameter to global_restriction_available? and

  DomainsAPI) to unpack the struct and pass the flag

before computing domain_dead when global_dead is true, avoiding a wasted
SSO datastore probe.

Problem: The simple-mode gate (Core::Controllers::Base#restrict_to_allows?)
used Onetime.auth_config.restrict_to directly, bypassing the SSO host pin
logic in inherited_restrict_to. This caused divergence: display showed
:restricted/sso (from the SSO pin) while the gate resolved :unrestricted.

see the same inherited restriction and the same pin_established flag.

Fix custom-domain 403s from HttpOrigin ignoring resolved display domain (#4170)

Rack::Protection::HttpOrigin resolves the request host via
Rack::Request#host, bypassing DetectHost/DomainStrategy. Behind a proxy
that rewrites Host to the canonical origin, a custom domain's Origin
header never matches, so every unsafe-method request is rejected with
403 — most visibly SSO sign-in through the auth app's production-only
HttpOrigin mount, which also ignores site.middleware.http_origin.

Add Onetime::Middleware::HttpOriginOptions: a shared allow_if that
accepts an Origin exactly matching https://<onetime.display_domain>,
the host DetectHost validates (forwarded headers only behind trusted
infrastructure) and DomainStrategy classifies. Fails closed when
display_domain is absent or empty. Consumed by both the Security stack
component and the auth app's mount so they cannot drift.

Document in .env.reference that the toggle does not govern the auth
app's mount.

fix(auth): set verified on SSO-provisioned customers

Auth::Operations::CreateCustomer hard-coded `verified: false` on every new
Customer, with the comment "needs to be updated in after_verify_account".
For SSO/OmniAuth JIT signups nothing ever updated it.

The call path:

  _handle_omniauth_callback
    -> omniauth_create_account            (rodauth-omniauth 0.6.2)
       -> _omniauth_new_account           stamps account_open_status_value
       -> omniauth_save_account           commits the accounts row (Verified)
       -> after_omniauth_create_account   (config/hooks/omniauth.rb)
          -> Auth::Operations::CreateCustomer  ... verified: false

after_verify_account — the hook that flips the flag — fires only in Rodauth's
emailed verify_account flow, which a JIT SSO user never traverses. So the
Rodauth account sat at status Verified while its Customer mirror stayed
unverified forever. That is not cosmetic: has_system_role?
(lib/onetime/application/authorization_policies.rb) does
`return false unless cust.verified?` BEFORE it reads the role field, so an
SSO-provisioned colonel or admin could not exercise their role even after
`bin/ots customers role promote`.

Changes:

* CreateCustomer takes `verified:` / `verified_by:`, defaulting to the current
  behaviour (false / nil) so no existing caller changes semantics. Both are
  ignored on the existing-customer branch, the same "don't rewrite history"
  rule that already governs provisioning_origin and signup_domain_id, and
  verified_by is dropped when verified is false.

* The OmniAuth hook passes them from a three-part gate: (1) it is inside
  after_omniauth_create_account, so this is SSO JIT provisioning and nothing
  else; (2) the persisted accounts row is already at
  Auth::AccountStatuses::VERIFIED — Rodauth's own decision, committed before
  this hook runs, read rather than assumed, so an install that opens SSO
  accounts unverified or sets skip_status_checks? keeps the old behaviour;
  and (3) the IdP did not explicitly assert `email_verified: false`.

  On (3): most supported IdPs (Entra ID, plain OAuth2 strategies, GitHub)
  never emit the claim, so absence cannot be treated as "unverified" without
  leaving those installs broken, and cannot be treated as a positive signal
  without inventing an assertion the IdP never made. Only an explicit false
  is honoured — the claim can therefore narrow the stamp, never widen it.
  The gate as a whole mirrors a fact the auth store already holds and grants
  nothing the accounts row does not already grant (AGENTS.md: changes that
  widen access require operator approval — this one does not widen).

* 'sso' registered in Doctor::VALID_VERIFIED_BY and in the verified_by field
  comment.

There is deliberately NO login-path reconcile. On login a status_id check
cannot distinguish an SSO user from anyone else: with verify_account disabled
every ordinary password account is Verified too, so such a guard verifies
almost the entire user base. Records that already drifted are handled by a new
`bin/ots customers doctor` check (:sso_customer_unverified) instead, gated on
BOTH real provenance (provisioning_origin == 'sso_jit', written once at
creation) and the accounts row already being Verified. Its repair routes
through SetCustomerVerification with rodauth_already_synced: true (Redis only,
no SQL write) and preserves any existing verified_by rather than relabelling
an email- or stripe-verified record as 'sso'. It shares one memoized accounts
read with the existing :auth_email_drift check, so a `--all` sweep still costs
one SQL round trip per customer.

Tests: omniauth_jit_verified_spec.rb drives the real Rodauth callback and
asserts a JIT SSO sign-in yields verified?/verified_by == 'sso', that a
non-SSO CreateCustomer with a Verified accounts row does not, and that an
explicit email_verified: false vetoes; omniauth_account_creation_spec.rb pins
the new parameter contract including the negative and existing-customer cases;
doctor_sso_verified_spec.rb covers the doctor check and repair.

Supersedes #4001, whose login-path reconcile guarded only on status_id == 2,
stamped verified_by = 'sso' over existing provenance, wrote the fields by hand
instead of through the canonical operation, used the literal 2, never
registered 'sso', and had no coverage of the headline change.

Resolve datastore index collisions between worktrees (#4168)

The per-worktree index is a checksum of the repo root mapped onto 1023
slots, so two worktrees can derive the same one. A collision was silent,
and a silent collision reproduces exactly the fixture contamination the
isolation exists to prevent.

Make the derived index a starting point rather than the answer: claim it
in a registry under ~/.cache/onetime-lanes/db/, one file per index naming
the repo root that owns it, and walk to the next free index when a live
checkout already holds that one.

Claims are atomic (noclobber, so worktrees starting together cannot both
win an index), sticky (a worktree keeps its index and its data across
runs), and reclaimable (a claim whose repo root no longer exists is stale
and gets taken over, so the registry does not accumulate). An empty read
counts as taken rather than stale: it means the winner of a race has not
finished writing, and reclaiming it would undo the race the atomic create
just resolved. If HOME is unwritable the derived index stands, which is
no worse than having no registry.

A file rather than a key in valkey because the index has to be settled
before the service preflight, which probes the database it names, and has
to survive `pnpm clean:db` flushing that database.

Add spec/unit/lanes/datastore_claim_spec.rb, which drives the real runner
and reads the index out of the environment the task process received.

fix(secret): make branded instructions "Show More" toggle deterministic

The toggle over the instructions text on the recipient page appeared and
disappeared between otherwise identical renders, failing visual checks.

Two independent sources of nondeterminism:

The clamp in force was decided by stylesheet injection order. The
paragraph used Tailwind's `line-clamp-6`, but SecretConfirmationForm
re-declared `.line-clamp-6` at three lines from a *global* (unscoped)
style block. Same specificity, so whichever stylesheet landed last won,
and that varies with chunk load order. SecretPreview carried the same
override behind `scoped`, where it never matched the child component's
paragraph at all. The clamp now lives in BaseSecretDisplay as its own
scoped `instructions-clamp` class, named for its role so callers are not
tempted to re-declare a utility to change it; both overrides are gone.

The toggle's visibility was decided by a line count re-derived from
line-height (`scrollHeight > lineHeight * 4`) that matched neither clamp,
measured by removing and re-adding the clamp class behind Vue's back,
against an element whose bottom padding grew when the toggle appeared —
so the measurement's own outcome fed back into the next measurement. It
now asks the clamped element whether it is actually overflowing, in the
layout the reader sees. The padding the toggle overlays moved to the
wrapper, so nothing about the toggle's presence perturbs the measurement
that decides it.

Also: skip re-measuring while expanded (no clamp means no overflow to
read, which retracted the toggle mid-use), coalesce resize measurements
through rAF, observe the paragraph with a ResizeObserver so container and
font-swap reflows are caught, stop leaking the paragraph's clamp and
padding classes onto the button element, and give the button an explicit
type and aria-expanded.

fix(auth): join active sessions on the key Rodauth actually stores

The account active-sessions list rendered no ip_address, user_agent or
geo_country for any session. It joined Rodauth's
account_active_session_keys rows to the SessionMetadata sidecar with
compute_hmac(sidecar.session_id) — a digest of the Onetime Rack sid.
Rodauth stores HMAC(active_session_id), where active_session_id is a
random token it mints itself in add_active_session and never derives
from the Rack sid. Both sides produce well-formed, non-nil digests of
different inputs, so the lookup missed every time and every metadata
field came back nil.

Nothing surfaced the failure: created_at and last_activity_at fall back
to the Rodauth row's own columns, so the list kept looking healthy.
is_current was never affected — it already compared against Rodauth's
token rather than the sid, which is exactly the asymmetry that made the
join wrong.

The sidecar now stores the digest Rodauth stores. It is computed in an
update_session override, because compute_hmac needs the Rodauth
instance and TrackMetadata has none, and because update_session is the
one seam every token-minting path crosses — after_login would miss the
remember-cookie login and the create_account, reset_password and
verify_account autologins, none of which fire it.

The raw token is deliberately not carried: the sidecar is not encrypted
at rest and Rodauth itself persists only the digest. The new field is
an internal join key and is kept off the safe_dump allow-list, so the
exact-key-set assertion on that allow-list is unchanged.

Rejected the alternative of listing from the sidecar instead: the
delete route passes its id straight to remove_active_session, which
matches on Rodauth's column, so plain sids would silently revoke
nothing — and the sidecar's liveness probe only prunes on blob absence,
which would leave Rodauth-revoked sessions listed as active.

Sessions predating the stamp simply do not join and keep today's
behaviour until their next sign-in. No backfill.

fix(api): stop leaking colleagues' secret bearer tokens from org receipts

Closes H-1 of the 2026-08-14 appsec review.

GET /receipt/recent?scope=org returned every organization member's receipts,
each carrying a live `secret_identifier`. In this product that identifier IS
the capability: the reveal path performs no ownership check by design, so any
member could read the plaintext of a colleague's unread secret, or burn it via
the receipt `identifier`. The surface was gated only at `api_access`, a
member-level entitlement.

Two independent controls, either of which alone leaves the finding partly open:

1. Redaction (the load-bearing one). For scope=org and scope=domain, records
   the caller does not own now come back with `secret_identifier` nulled and
   `identifier`/`key` collapsed to the receipt shortid. Shortids are already
   this codebase's safe form for cross-member surfaces -- ListSecretActivity
   emits "receipt/secret shortids only, never full identifiers, which are
   capability tokens". The default (own receipts) scope is untouched, so the
   personal dashboard is byte-identical.

   The withheld values must stay Strings: the V3 contract types identifier and
   key as required, non-nullable strings inside a strict array, and one failing
   record blanks the entire response. secret_identifier is nullish there, so
   null is the correct withheld value for it. Redaction happens before
   records.partition, so details.revealed_receipts / pending_receipts -- which
   alias the same hashes -- are covered too.

2. Entitlement. scope=org is raised to `audit_logs`, matching the sibling
   org-wide surface. The pre-existing unconditional api_access gate is
   unchanged, so the personal dashboard keeps working.

OPERATOR ACTION, billing-enabled deployments only: entitlements are the plan
catalog intersected with the role, and the shipped example catalog defines
audit_logs without granting it in any plan -- so scope=org will 403 for every
role until a plan grants it. Standalone installs are unaffected
(STANDALONE_ENTITLEMENTS already includes audit_logs). This mirrors the
precondition ListSecretActivity already carries and fails closed. Grant
audit_logs, or drop that single guarded line: the redaction closes the
confidentiality break independently of the gate.

Known cosmetic gap: no shipped UI requests scope=org, but a client that did
would render dead receipt/burn links for redacted rows, since it builds routes
from `identifier` without an ownership guard.

Closes H-2 of the 2026-08-14 appsec review.

GET /billing/portal resolved the caller's default organization and minted a

cust.default_org_id at the shared tenant organization when a pre-existing

entitlements are the plan catalog intersected with the role, and no shipped
catalog grants manage_billing, so an entitlement gate here would deny every
caller including legitimate owners. Ownership is the same test every mutating
sibling endpoint already applies via load_organization(require_owner: true).

response=, so Otto content-negotiates the error and a browser navigation would
render a bare text/plain 403.

fix(auth): enforce tenant SSO allowed_domains on create and login

Closes H-3 of the 2026-08-14 appsec review.

CustomDomain::SsoConfig#allowed_domains is plumbed through the API, rendered in
the UI, and described by the provider metadata as the way to restrict a generic
OIDC IdP ('oidc' declares requires_domain_filter: true) -- but the method had
zero production callers. An operator who restricted their tenant to @corp.com
had no restriction at all: any identity the IdP would authenticate could sign
in. The only domain gate that ran consulted a different object entirely
(CustomDomain::SignupConfig / the global allowed_signup_domains).

Enforcement goes in before_omniauth_callback_route, which is the first
statement of rodauth-omniauth's _handle_omniauth_callback and therefore runs on
EVERY callback -- JIT creation and every subsequent sign-in -- before the gem
branches on whether a (provider, issuer, uid) identity row exists. That
placement is the fix for the review's secondary finding too: the existing gate
lived in before_omniauth_create_account, which the gem skips once that row
exists, so a create-only check let a user keep signing in indefinitely after
their domain was removed from the allowlist.

Edited in place rather than added as a second hook: Rodauth hooks do not chain,
so a new registration would have silently clobbered the tenant-mismatch
validation this file owns. The check sits after that validation (so the
allowlist consulted belongs to the domain that actually initiated the flow) and
before the validated-domain stamp (so a rejected callback leaves nothing behind
for the org-join hooks).

Fails closed on every branch it can -- missing config, unreadable allowlist,
and absent/malformed asserted email are all denials. An EMPTY allowlist still
means allow-all: that is the documented, spec-asserted state and the correct
one for Entra ID, where the IdP controls access via app assignment.

Two supporting pieces:

- SsoConfig#allowed_domains_corrupt?. allowed_domains swallows
  JSON::ParserError and returns [], which valid_email_domain? reads as
  allow-all. Harmless for display, an inversion of intent on the auth path, so
  authentication callers deny when a present value is unreadable.

- A structural email check before the domain comparison. This is load-bearing,
  not hygiene: valid_email_domain? takes the segment after the LAST '@', so for
  an allowlist of ['example.com'] the asserted address
  attacker@evil.com@example.com resolves to example.com and the allowlist alone
  returns true. The regression test asserts that bypass explicitly, and carries
  a note that the mirror-image ordering proves nothing.

Rejections reuse auth_error=domain_not_allowed, already localized in Login.vue
and deliberately silent about which domains are configured; the audit event is
distinct (:omniauth_tenant_domain_rejected) so operators can tell it apart from
the signup-domain denial. The asserted address is obscured in logs.

Follow-up worth tracking: the workspace SSO form hardcodes its allowlist editor
hidden (showDomainFilter is always false) while re-sending the stored value on
every save, so a populated allowlist is now enforceable but not editable from
the UI. Operators can still clear it through the API.

[#4190] fix(mail): forward configured SMTP2GO fastaccept to delivery backend

Mailer.smtp2go_provider_config omitted fastaccept, so Delivery::Smtp2go
always fell back to its own default and CUSTOM_MAIL_SMTP2GO_FASTACCEPT had
no effect on ordinary sends — only the test-email path, which passes the
flag explicitly, honoured it.

Resolve it through Utils::Strings.strict_bool! (provider section wins, ENV
fallback, default false) so an unrecognized token raises instead of quietly
resolving to false, which would look like working accounting. The value is
always a real boolean so .compact cannot drop an explicit false.

Records why fastaccept stays in dns_defaults rather than config_env_sources:
the latter declares verbatim string passthroughs the parity spec round-trips
through ENV, and this key's template coerces to a boolean.

[#4190] fix(mail): read SMTP2GO fastaccept from stringified config, coerce strictly

Smtp2go#initialize read the raw constructor argument while Base#initialize
stringifies keys into @config, so a symbol-keyed fastaccept: true silently
resolved to false. Read @config instead, and coerce the value: SMTP2GO
expects a JSON boolean, and a string "false" from ENV or a hand-built hash
would be truthy on their side, switching off the per-recipient accounting
this backend depends on.

Prefers the canonical strict_bool!, with the same token set kept locally for
standalone mail-lib loads where Onetime::Utils is absent — mirroring the
existing EMAIL_PATTERN twin-constant arrangement.

Both the code comment and the defaults template prose claimed fastaccept
defaulted to true for backward compatibility; the default is false, which is
the point of the change — synchronous accounting so a failed recipient is
reported rather than dropped.

Prepend a normalized geo_country reader on SessionMetadata so Otto's
'**' unknown sentinel can never cross a serialization path: safe_dump,
to_h, and to_h_for_storage all read through the public getter, so the

perf(sessions): batch session metadata sidecar reads with load_multi

ListSessions#attach_geo_country and ListForCustomer each did a serial
SessionMetadata.load per row (EXISTS + HGETALL, ~200 round trips per
100-row colonel page) to read sidecar fields. Familia 2.12's load_multi
pipelines all HGETALLs into one round trip, position-aligned with nil
for missing keys — the same per-position nil tolerance the serial loads
had.

load_multi materializes the whole batch in one call, so any failure
inside it raises for the entire page; both call sites degrade to the
legacy per-row loads on batch failure. In ListForCustomer a per-row
fallback failure maps to a private SIDECAR_READ_FAILED marker distinct
from nil, so a transient read error skips only its row and never
triggers the self-heal ZREM that absence (nil) legitimately does.

The '**' unknown sentinel is now normalized to null server-side at the
SessionMetadata model boundary, so the API never emits it. Remove the
three duplicated frontend checks (AdminSessions, AdminCustomerSessions-

zod schema doc comments to state the contract, and drop the specs that

fix(domains): store CustomDomain booleans natively, surface resolving

`verified`, `resolving` and `favicon_fetched` were plain fields, so each
row stored whatever spelling the caller handed it — true, 'true', '1',
nil — and the nine sites that read them each re-implemented the
comparison. `.to_s == 'true'` is a silent false negative against a row
written as a native boolean, and the `field!` fast writer (the path
VerifyDomain uses) bypassed coercion entirely.

Declare them `boolean_field ..., storage: :native`. BooleanFieldType
gains a storage encoding: :native coerces to a real boolean and preserves
nil as "never determined"; :string keeps its grandfathered 'true'/'false'
and stays the default, so Customer's verified/suspended rows are
untouched. Coercion moves onto the setter and the fast writer — the two
paths that actually reach the value. Familia 2.12 declares #serialize /
#deserialize on FieldType but never calls them, so those overrides went
away; reads self-heal because the load path assigns through the setter.

Also adds `resolving` to the domain safe-dump. It was never in the API
payload, so the frontend could not tell a domain whose DNS resolves from
one that does not and fell back to reading vhost.status.

try/unit/models/custom_domain_boolean_fields_try.rb is the regression
surface: it asserts the persisted bytes via hmget on both write paths,
and that rows hset directly as '"true"' / '1' / '"garbage"' coerce on
load.
Allow native boolean fields in raw-read guard

fix(fields): coerce only genuine fast-writer writes

The boolean fast-writer wrapper decided whether to coerce by inspecting the
argument value (skip when empty or nil). That diverged from what Familia
actually treats as a write: it collapsed a two-argument `field!` call to one
argument, swallowing the ArgumentError Familia raises on bad arity and
persisting a value instead.

Extract the decision into `BooleanFieldType#fast_write?`, mirroring Familia
2.12's own guard: more than one argument, an absent/nil argument, or a
Redis::Future placeholder are all non-writes and are forwarded verbatim.
`Redis::Future` is matched with `===` because it subclasses BasicObject, so
calling `.nil?` on one raises.

Confirms the review question on this hunk: Familia does not distinguish
`field!` from `field!(nil)` — both return hget — so leaving nil uncoerced is
correct for :string storage too. Coercing it there would turn a documented
read into a silent overwrite with 'false'.

Adds spec/unit/onetime/field_types/boolean_field_type_fast_writer_spec.rb:
24 examples running the same shared group against :native and :string
storage, pinning the persisted bytes and the read/arity/Future passthroughs.

test(fields): correct raw-read guard diagnostic for native storage

The guard's failure message asserted that every boolean_field reader returns
the strings 'true'/'false', which stopped being true when :native storage
landed — a native reader returns a real boolean and a bare read of it is
correct, not a bug. A future offense on a native field would have shown a
diagnostic pointing at the wrong fix.

Split the message by declared storage and document the
`# boolean_field native` marker the guard already honours. The scan is
name-based and cannot tell the two encodings apart, so a correct native read
still needs the marker. Detection logic is unchanged.

feat(jobs): add nightly entitlement re-materialization job

Adds EntitlementMaterializeJob to the maintenance family (#4203). Org
entitlements are materialized from the Redis plan cache, and nothing
converged them on a schedule: after a plan definition change, an org's
snapshot only self-healed on its next Stripe webhook — weeks away for
monthly subscriptions, never for orgs with no billing events.

The job runs the existing idempotent batch op
Billing::Operations::MaterializePlans (include_memberships: true) on a
nightly cron. It refreshes the plan catalog in-job first and aborts if
the pull fails, so it can never materialize from a stale cache — the
ordering trap behind the 2026-07/08 truncated-snapshot incident.
Standalone installs (no Stripe key) skip gracefully. Result counts are
logged as one structured JSON line at INFO; per-org failures at ERROR.

Config-gated and default off: requires both jobs.maintenance.enabled
and jobs.maintenance.entitlement_materialize.enabled.

feat(cli): org doctor check 6 — stripe_customer_id index drift (#4205)

Organization claims its class-level stripe_customer_id unique index on
every full save, so an entry mapping an org's Stripe customer id to a
different objid makes every later full save raise "Key already exists".
Stripe webhook updates, org reconcile and entitlement materialization all
take that path, so the org is silently locked out until something happens
to write. `org doctor` had no coverage for the defect class.

Check 6 names the three drift states:

  missing entry  the field was written without claiming the index (a fast
                 write, or a write inside MULTI). No lockout yet, but the
                 id reads as unclaimed so another org can take it.
  stale entry    the entry points at a deleted org, or at one that has
                 since moved to a different Stripe customer.
  duplicate      another live org carries the same Stripe customer id.

--repair handles the two mechanical states: it claims a missing entry and
repoints a stale one. A live duplicate is report-only — picking the
canonical org means reading which one the Stripe subscription actually
references — and the finding carries both sides' extid, plan,
subscription status and obscured owner so an operator can adjudicate.

The duplicate test runs first and does not depend on where the index
points. An entry aimed at a third, deleted objid while two live orgs
carry the id would otherwise read as a plain stale entry, and --repair
would award the customer to whichever org the scan reached first; #call
therefore builds the claim map over every org before checking any of
them.

--all additionally sweeps organization:stripe_customer_id_index for
entries no live org carries. Those are invisible to a per-org check (the
org that would report them is gone) and each one blocks whichever org
tries to claim that customer id next; --repair removes them. Entries a
live org still contests are left to the per-org check, so the sweep can
never delete a claim check 6 just repaired.

Index values are read through Familia's legacy JSON-encoding strip before
being compared, and index fields are keyed on the field value verbatim —
an unstripped comparison would read as a conflict, and a trimmed lookup
would miss the real entry and write a second one.

Also extends the shared org_doctor_issues spec helper with the narrow
form of the invariant, so ops that produce an organization assert it too.

[#4173] refactor(csp): resolve tenant extras on the way out, keyed on display_domain

Three defects in the request-phase shape:

  static assets, JSON, 404s, health checks, and every request when CSP
  is disabled — pay 3-4 Valkey round-trips whose result otto discards

  cheapest-first (CSP enabled, HTML media type, display_domain present)

- The :custom domain-strategy gate skewed against the SSO button's
  serializer, which keys purely on display_domain: DomainStrategy

a String value is a whitespace-separated token list (Array() would wrap

The 'override on both surfaces' advice was wrong and harmful: tenant

fix(cli): make org doctor check 6 index writes compare-and-set (#4205)

Review feedback on #4208. Three defects, all in the window between
reading the index and writing it.

Repair wrote the index with a blind HSET, and the sweep deleted by
field name alone. Diagnosis and repair are separate round trips, and
the ids involved are exactly the ones a Stripe webhook or an
`org reconcile` is free to claim in between — an orphan is by
definition an id nobody holds. A blind write there erases a valid,
seconds-old claim, leaves the billed org unindexed, and re-opens the
lockout the check exists to close.

Every write is now a compare-and-set against the value the diagnosis
was read from, and every sweep deletion a compare-and-delete against
the value seen when the entry was classified, both as Lua run by
Redis — the shape Customers::ChangeEmail and the :state_cas feature
already use. An entry that moved is left as found and reported. That
means the expected value has to be the bytes Redis holds, so index
reads for these paths go through the raw client: Familia 2.10.1
strips a legacy JSON-encoded value on the way out, and a CAS stating
the stripped form could never match a legacy entry.

Check 6 also classified from whatever claim map it happened to have.
On a single-org run that is a map of one, which cannot tell a missing
entry apart from two orgs contesting an unclaimed id — and --repair
would then award the customer to whichever org was named on the
command line, auto-repairing a live duplicate it promises never to
touch. The map is now completed before anything is reported or
repaired, lazily: an org already holding its own entry returns first,
so the scan is paid only where a wrong answer would reach Redis.

The shared spec helper compared the index holder without stripping
legacy JSON encoding, so on a dataset still carrying the 2.9 format
it would fail every billed org for a check-6 violation that is not
one.

Tryouts: scenario 21 now asserts the duplicate is detected with no
pre-pass at all; 25 covers the compare-and-set primitives in both
directions; 26 races a claim against the sweep and asserts it
survives.

fix(billing): gate re-materialization on a verified catalog, not pull success

Catalog::Pull reports success for a run that synced nothing. When Stripe
matches no products — wrong region filter, unpublished products, no active
recurring prices — sync_from_stripe returns early, before pruning stale
plans, rebuilding the price-id cache, and stamping the sync timestamp, so
the previously cached plans stay in Redis untouched.

EntitlementMaterializeJob treated that success as proof of freshness and
would have materialized every org from the stale cache: the exact incident
the job exists to prevent. MaterializePlans does not catch it either — a
missing plan fails the org, but a stale plan is found and applied.

Add a catalog_verified signal to Pull::Result, true only when the run
persisted at least one plan from the live catalog and completed the
prune/rebuild/timestamp path, and gate the job on that instead of success.
An unverified pull now aborts with catalog_pull_unverified rather than
materializing. Leaving entitlements untouched is always safer than
rewriting them from plans we did not just confirm.

success semantics are unchanged, so the catalog CLI, the catalog-updated
webhook handler, and PlanCacheRefreshJob are unaffected; the new field is
keyword-defaulted and nothing constructs Result positionally.

Also point the spec's run instructions at the lane runner instead of a raw
rspec invocation, which bypasses the isolated lane environment and can
inherit ambient service credentials.

GET /api/v2/version and GET /api/v3/version returned the exact build
version to anonymous callers. That version string is the primary input to
fingerprinting an install and matching it against known CVEs, so it now
requires auth=sessionauth,basicauth like the rest of the authenticated

This is a deliberate breaking change to the public API. Both endpoints
previously answered 200 for anonymous requests and now answer 401.
Nothing in this repository consumed them: the frontend has schemas and
contract tests for the response shape but never issues the request, and
no script, healthcheck or container probe calls them. External
integrations that polled the version anonymously will need credentials.

The sibling meta endpoints are unchanged and stay public — /status
reports operational state and /supported-locales reports locale config;
neither discloses build information.

That path sits ahead of r.rodauth in the Roda tree, so it answers
anonymous callers, and a service-identification response is no place to
volunteer the build. /auth/health still reports it and remains restricted
to loopback/RFC1918 by HealthAccessControl.

Note for operators running with site.authentication.enabled = false: the
sessionauth and basicauth strategies are not registered in that mode, so
these endpoints become unreachable rather than merely gated. That is the
same behaviour the authenticated secrets API already has on such installs,
and withholding the version from an install with no accounts is the
intended outcome.

[#4196] Elect one workspace creator via the Stripe customer claim

Two checkout-completion surfaces -- the browser redirect and the webhook

Both read the participation set before either writes, so both create a
workspace. The customer ends up with two default workspaces, and only one
can hold the Stripe customer: the loser raises Onetime::Problem on its
subscription write, which the redirect surface does not rescue, so a
customer who just paid gets a 500.

the org's save takes the unique index's server-side CAS. The checkout's
Stripe customer is the one identifier both surfaces provably share before
either writes, and the index already treats it as authoritative -- it
gives a permanent election with no TTL to tune, unlike a lock spanning
the web process and the Sneakers worker.

rather than falling through to a second create if that fails. It sits
outside the OrganizationExists retry so a claim lost on either attempt is
adopted. stripe_claim_fields returns an empty hash for blank or
non-Stripe values, so the field is never written as a literal null.

[#4196] Normalize the checkout session's Stripe customer to an id

ProcessCheckoutSession retrieved the session with expand: [subscription,
customer], so checkout_session.customer was a Stripe::Customer object,
and that object was handed to CheckoutTargetResolver as
stripe_customer_id. The resolver's contract is strict — is_a?(String)
then start_with?('cus_') — so step 2 silently never matched on the
redirect path and the workspace it created held no stripe claim. That
disables replay resolution, the unique-index concurrency claim shared
with the webhook twin, and redirect/webhook agreement on which workspace
a checkout lands in.

boundary, and pass that string to both resolver entry points. The
extractor returns nil for anything that is neither a String nor a

invalid claim instead of failing.

subscription is legitimately nil for one-time payments, so validating in
raise_concerns would turn every one of those redirects into a form error.

one, which is exactly the boundary the check is meant to hold.

which Stripe never expands, so that surface always holds a cus_ string
and already passes it correctly. The resolver's String contract is what
surfaced this and is left strict.

[#4196] Guard organization deletion against drifted domain records

The org-delete rewrite (65d2109381) and the #4196 review follow-up landed the
same verb from the same base, independently. Main's shape wins: the teardown
belongs in Onetime::Operations::Org::Delete, shared by the CLI, the colonel
endpoint and the customer API. What only the follow-up had was domain-drift
handling, and it moves into the op as a guardrail rather than staying at the
adapter, where two of the three surfaces could not reach it.

A CustomDomain can fall out of its org's domains collection while
CustomDomain.owners still attributes it to that org. The domain then vanishes
from the owner's domain list, and the :has_domains guard — which counts the
collection — has nothing to refuse on, so the delete proceeds and leaves the
record pointing at an org that no longer exists.

The op now probes for that drift in the snapshot phase, before any mutation,
and on the applied path repairs the affected domains back into the collection
through Operations::Domains::Repair, the single audited repair implementation.
Repair puts them back in view, the re-read count then trips :has_domains, and
the customer gets an actionable "remove your domains first". Repair-then-refuse,
never repair-then-delete. A dry run repairs nothing and reports the drift as-is.

What repair cannot restore gets its own :drifted_domains refusal. Previously
this shape reached Organization#destroy!, whose guard raises a bare
Onetime::Problem — a 500 on the API, and on the operator surfaces a raise
landing AFTER the instances-zset removal, i.e. mid-teardown. No org: is passed
to the repair op, so the orphaned shape (owners names this org, the record's
own org_id is blank) returns :needs_org and mutates nothing: inferring
ownership from a stale denormalized index as a side effect of a delete would be
guessing. All three adapters name the domains and route to
`bin/ots domains doctor --repair`.

Also drops the adapter-side domain_count pre-check the merge left behind as a
dangling call. It duplicated the op's guard with a different message and would
have short-circuited the self-heal — telling the customer to remove domains
they cannot see.

Model-side: Organization#destroy!'s drift guard stays as defense-in-depth, and
archive! warns rather than refuses (the domain SSO login path self-heals by
archiving personal workspaces; raising there turns data drift into login
failures — `bin/ots domains doctor` check #9 is the operator surface).

[#4209] fix(org): gate delete on subscription liveness, not entitlement

The delete guardrail refuses an org whose subscription still bills, but it
read `active_subscription?` — `active`/`trialing` only. A `past_due` org
therefore passed both the server guard and the UI pre-disable, even though
Stripe is still retrying the card and the subscription recovers to `active`
the moment a payment lands. Deleting it strands exactly the billing
relationship the guard exists to protect.

Widening `active_subscription?` was not an option: `paid?` and
`complimentary?` route through it, so that would hand premium entitlements
to delinquent orgs. Split the two questions instead.

`billing_live?` answers "can this charge a card with no further human
action": active, trialing, past_due, unpaid. Excluded are canceled, and
also incomplete/incomplete_expired/paused — all three need a person to
complete a payment or attach a payment method first. That exclusion matters
because the customer-facing delete has no force flag (only colonel and
`bin/ots org delete` do), so every status added here is an unappealable
lockout for an org owner. Accepted residual risk, documented at the
constant: an `incomplete` sub can still reach `active` if 3DS confirms
inside its ~23h window.

The refusal status keeps the name `:active_subscription` — it is a wire
contract across `--force-subscription`, the `delete_active_subscription`
error key, the zod schema and the Vue prop. The CLI plan line now says
LIVE rather than ACTIVE, which is what it now means.

Tests: the delete_spec stubs targeted `active_subscription?` on a verifying
double, so they raised once the op moved off it — repointed, and backed by a
real-datastore layer that asserts which statuses are live rather than
restating the stub. Also fixes two vacuous `clear_billing_fields`
assertions (both twins) that asserted 'canceled' from an already-canceled

[#4209] fix(domains): maintain the owners index wherever org_id changes

Operations::Domains::Transfer reassigned CustomDomain#org_id and moved both
organizations' domain collections, but never updated the CustomDomain.owners
class hashkey. The source organization kept a stale ownership entry forever,
so Organization#destroy! failed its drift guard and Org::Delete refused with
:drifted_domains -- a status with no force override on any surface.

The advertised remediation could not clear it either: doctor check #4 keys off
domain.org_id, which after a transfer correctly names the NEW organization, so
the scan reported nothing to repair. Domains::Repair's orphan-adoption branch
had the same omission.

CustomDomain.record_owner is now the single writer for that index, and the
three existing writers plus Transfer (including its add-failure rollback, which
realigns owners to whatever org_id actually persisted) and Repair route through
it. Doctor gains check #10 in two non-overlapping halves: a per-domain
owners-vs-org_id comparison, and an index sweep that skips entries the
per-domain scan already visits so N problems cannot surface as 2N. The sweep is
what lets `doctor --org <OLD-ORG>` see a domain transferred away, since such a
domain is no longer in that organization's collection for anything else to
reach.

The customer-facing refusal moves to a count-based locale key. A domain that
drifted via a transfer now belongs to a different tenant, so naming it to the
previous owner leaked another tenant's domain. The operator surfaces keep the
full list; the colonel drifted_domains payload shape is unchanged.

Also corrects every live reference to the remediation command. `bin/ots domains
doctor --repair` printed usage and exited 0 without --all, --org, or an FQDN,
so the command three refusal messages advertised did nothing. They now name
`--all --repair`.

[#4209] fix(billing): grant audit_logs so receipt listing is reachable

Gating scope=domain receipt listing on require_entitlement_in!(org,
'audit_logs') was the right call -- it closes the escalation where a member
refused scope=org re-runs as scope=domain against a domain of the same
organization -- but no shipped plan granted that entitlement. Effective
entitlements are plan intersect role, so every caller including the owner got
403. scope=org has been failing the same way on default billing-enabled
installs since f1e54b8632.

audit_logs is launched and tier-gated, not withheld: the maintained catalog
grants it on an active team_plus_v1, and the example lost the grant only
because the entire team-plan block is commented out. Granted here on
identity_plus_v1, the one active paid tier -- it already grants unlimited
custom domains, the domain receipt index exists so domain owners can see
activity on their branded links, and its total_members_per_org cap of 1 means
no cross-member exposure is created.

Restores the operator-action comment the earlier diff dropped, now covering
both scopes. Note this only helps fresh installs: entitlements are materialized
into the Billing::Plan cache from Stripe metadata and billing.yaml is a
fallback for when that cache is empty, so existing deployments must grant it in
their own catalog and run `bin/ots billing catalog sync`.

Also fixes a 500 on the concurrent-creation race in checkout.session.completed.
The handler rescued only Familia::RecordExistsError on the premise that the
stripe_customer_id index elects the creator, but Organization.create! reserves
contact_email via HSETNX before org.save, and the stripe_customer_id CAS only
fires inside that save -- so the loser always sees Onetime::OrganizationExists.

is a plain signup carrying no Stripe customer, so adopt_email_reserved_workspace
falls back to an ownership-checked contact_email lookup. A reservation held by a
foreign organization still resolves to nil, which the caller already handles.

load_by_display_domain, whose blanket rescue reinterpreted a mid-render
datastore failure as 'no tenant config' and left the serializers'
DOMAIN_READ_FAILED handling unreachable.

The failure, not the read, is keyed on DomainStrategy's classification:
operator hosts (:canonical/:subdomain) answer nil on a read failure —
their policy is in-memory config, and DomainStrategy publishes
display_domain unconditionally, so the sentinel there would hide the
password form on canonical /signin. The read itself still runs on every
classification because a per-domain record keyed on an operator host
must keep narrowing both surfaces (ADR-024 parity).

Specs stop stubbing the fail-open loader to raise (a contract it never
had); an integration-level example fails only the datastore seam under
the real finder, and the parity specs leave load_by_display_domain
unstubbed so a regression back to it goes red.

fix: key tenant SSO lookup on public host, not rewritten Host header

Behind a Host-rewriting proxy (Approximated ingress) the browser's custom
domain arrives as `Apx-Incoming-Host` while `Host:` carries the origin
target. The omniauth setup hook keyed its CustomDomain lookup on
`request.host`, so every tenant lookup missed and the SSO POST answered
`302 /signin?auth_error=sso_not_configured` on a domain whose same request
classified as `:custom`.

Add `OmniAuthTenant.public_host(request)`, reading
`env['onetime.display_domain']` (Rack::DetectHost + DomainStrategy) with a
`request.host` fallback for bare-Rack specs. Route the setup hook,
restrict_to enforcement, callback tenant validation, and the auth-event
logs through it — the same source HttpOriginOptions (#4170),
Auth::SigninGate, Auth::RestrictTo and TenantSsoResolution already read, so
the runtime gate and the display gates cannot disagree about which tenant a
request belongs to.

It is also the safer key: Rack 3.2's `request.host` prefers
`X-Forwarded-Host`/`Forwarded` from any client, ungated by proxy trust,
whereas DetectHost accepts a forwarded host only from trusted infrastructure.

Covered by unit specs for `.public_host` and a full-stack integration spec
reproducing the proxy topology.

docs(proxy): document the host seam and stop forwarding client X-Forwarded-Host

The example Caddyfile passed the client's `X-Forwarded-Host` straight to the
app. Rack::DetectHost ranks that header above `Apx-Incoming-Host` and takes
the first syntactically valid hostname without checking whether the domain is
known, so a visitor could inject a header that outranks the one the ingress
set; DomainStrategy then rejects the unknown domain, falls back to canonical,
and that tenant's custom-domain surfaces stop resolving. Strip it instead —
the same block already pins `X-Original-Host` to Caddy's own view of the
request and preserves `Host`, so DetectHost keeps a trustworthy input and
`request.host` stays correct. Matches the rewriting lane in
scripts/host-seam/caddy-approximated-lane.caddy, which already strips it.

Also record what an operator cannot see from the config alone: when a layer in
front rewrites `Host`, `request.host` becomes the origin target for the whole
app including mounted gems (Rodauth's base_url, #4221), which is why Onetime's
own code reads env['onetime.display_domain'] (#4224); and that pinning
X-Forwarded-Host to {http.request.host} is not the fix, since it masks
Apx-Incoming-Host and produces the same failure by another route.

`caddy validate` passes; `caddy fmt` reports no changes.

fix(auth): build SSO redirect_uri from the public host too

Resolving the tenant's credentials was only half the flow. Every absolute URL
the SSO request hands an IdP comes from `OmniAuth::Strategy#full_host`, which
derives from `request.url` — Rack's authority — because `OmniAuth.config
.full_host` was never set. `callback_url` is `full_host + callback_path`
(omniauth-entra-id defines it verbatim, the OAuth2 family inherits the shape),
and the OIDC strategies read a `client_options.redirect_uri` this hook
composes from it.

Behind a Host-rewriting proxy that authority is the origin target, so the
tenant's IdP was handed `redirect_uri=https://<origin target>/auth/sso/
<provider>/callback` — unregistered, so rejected; or honored, landing the
visitor on a host they never authenticated from. Without this, the previous
commit turns `sso_not_configured` into a failure one hop later.

Install a full_host resolver at boot. OmniAuth calls the Proc form per request
with the Rack env, so one process-global assignment stays request-scoped and
covers every strategy at once rather than patching the OIDC branch alone. It
swaps only the hostname — scheme and port still come from the request, and
honor the proxy's X-Forwarded-* exactly as before.

Scoped to display domains outside the canonical set. DomainStrategy pins
display_domain to the canonical host when the domains feature is off or a
detected host fails validation, and honoring that would bounce a local
`localhost:3000` flow to the canonical domain mid-authentication; a host
outside the set can only be DetectHost's validated answer for this request.

Deliberately NOT gated on `domain_strategy == :custom`. Chooserator wraps its
chain in a rescue, so a datastore blip — or an unparseable canonical host,
which is what the integration lane actually has — classifies a real customer
domain :invalid while display_domain stays correct. The first draft gated on
:custom and the new integration example caught it: redirect_uri came back on
the origin target with the tenant resolving fine.

fix(auth): resolve the public host when domains are disabled

Both SSO host resolvers read env['onetime.display_domain'] as the host the
browser used. DomainStrategy pins that to the canonical host whenever the
domains feature is off — it never classifies the request at all — so the
value carries no information about this request, and the request.host
fallback below it was unreachable.

Consequences: every custom-domain lookup missed, so omniauth_setup exited
early, session[:omniauth_tenant_domain_id] was never written, and
before_omniauth_callback_route skipped ALL tenant validation (email-domain
enforcement, identity partitioning, cross-domain mismatch) — a bypass for
operators running domains.enabled: false behind Host forwarding, and the
cause of the red T3 full lanes. full_host_for had the twin failure: it fell
back to the raw Rack authority, so redirect_uri named the origin target.

Both now fall through to DetectHost's result before request.host. That is
the same host DomainStrategy would have classified, already normalized and
validated, and honored from forwarded headers only behind trusted
infrastructure — where Rack 3.2's request.host prefers X-Forwarded-Host
from any client. Local development is unaffected: DetectHost rejects
localhost and 127.0.0.1, so those flows keep OmniAuth's own derivation.

Also moves install_public_host_full_host! after `enable :omniauth`, which
is what requires the omniauth gem — touching ::OmniAuth.config before it is
a cold-boot NameError that specs mask by requiring omniauth in their
helpers.

[#4230] fix(billing): federate customer.subscription.created

Federation ran on subscription updated/deleted/paused/resumed but there
was no handler for customer.subscription.created at all, so the event
fell through to :unhandled. A purchase in region B by someone who
already had an organization in region A never propagated: that org
stayed on the free tier until a later event on the same subscription
happened to fire — the first renewal, a plan change, a pause. In
practice, until the customer wrote in.

Add SubscriptionCreated, mirroring SubscriptionUpdated's two-path match.
The federated path applies the subscription's benefits to orgs sharing
the buyer's email hash; the owner path deliberately writes nothing,
because checkout.session.completed owns that write path in the
purchasing region and compares the STORED subscription id against the
incoming one to catch a replacement that would orphan a live, still-
charging subscription (#2605). Both events fire for the same purchase
with no ordering guarantee, so writing owner fields here would
frequently win the race and make that check compare the new id against
itself. With federation off the handler is a no-op: it returns :skipped
rather than reporting a non-match for every new subscription seconds
before checkout links it.

Also make non-matches visible. A subscription event that matches no
organization means someone's account is not in the state they paid for,
and both paths were effectively silent — the non-federation fallback
logged a bare warning carrying only the subscription id, and the
federated path logged nothing before storing a pending record. Emit a
greppable, alertable federation.no_match warning from both, carrying
region, email hash, Stripe customer, subscription, event type, reason,
and whether a pending record was stored.

The shared federation_enabled? predicate, copy-pasted in four handlers,
moves to the new FederationSupport module alongside the no-match
logging rather than gaining a fifth copy.

fix(ci): actually deliver frontend sourcemaps to Sentry

Frontend stack traces have never symbolicated, on any release built here.
Two independent causes, both of which reported green.

The upload ran `sentry-cli sourcemaps upload ./public/web/dist` on the
runner, but the frontend is compiled inside the image (Dockerfile `build`
stage runs `pnpm run build`) and public/web/dist is gitignored, so that
directory has never existed at that point in the job. sentry-cli treats an
empty directory as a successful upload of zero artifacts. The frontend
project has held zero artifact bundles for every release in its history.

Extract the assets from the image that was just pushed rather than
rebuilding them: vite emits content-hashed filenames, so a second build
would produce artifacts named for files no browser ever requests.

Second cause: dist is a join key. Sentry resolves a bundle only when
release AND dist both match, and this upload has always passed
--dist=frontend while every sampled event carried dist=null. This commit
fixes only CI's half; the frontend half lands with the companion
telemetry-boundary change as `dist: 'frontend'` in enableDiagnostics.ts.
Until it does the preflight reports the mismatch on every run rather than
staying silent. Neither merge order breaks anything that currently works.

Make the delivery observable. continue-on-error is correct here — telemetry
plumbing must never fail a production image build — but it makes each step's
exit code meaningless, so a green check said nothing about whether anything
arrived. Every Sentry step now reports through scripts/ci/sentry-status.sh
as SKIPPED (no credentials, silent, normal on forks), BLOCKED (configured,
precondition failed) or FAILED (configured, command errored), emitting an
annotation and a job-summary row that outlives the log.

Add the checks that were missing: sentry-sourcemap-preflight.sh asserts the
dist tree, .map files, admin bundle, release parity with __SENTRY_RELEASE__
and project/dist agreement before uploading; sentry-verify-artifacts.sh then
asks the server, because input checks and exit codes were both satisfiable
while the project held nothing. Zero artifacts after an upload is FAILED —
the only check that would have caught the original defect.

Remove SENTRY_DIST from .env.reference: nothing in lib/, apps/ or src/ read
it and the preflight never checked it, so it advertised a runtime knob for a
build-time literal, offering no way to actually set it.

[#4221] fix(caddy): strip Apx-Incoming-Host and Forwarded in example config

Apx-Incoming-Host sits at precedence 2 in Rack::DetectHost, above the

shadow the detected host — the same spoof the X-Forwarded-Host strip
closed, one line up. Strip it by default; Approximated-fronted
deployments re-enable via a source-gated request_header matcher
documented inline.

Forwarded (precedence 4) was masked by the always-valid pin at 3, but
that is an ordering accident, not a policy — strip it too. Comment
block no longer claims the precedence-3 pin makes everything above it
trustworthy.

fix(lanes): convert mid-run service loss to one line and exit 69

When a container VM dies mid-run and takes a test service with it, the
suite surfaces the loss as dozens of ordinary-looking spec failures — a
triage session over a failure set that means nothing. The preflight only
proves services were up at the start; nothing distinguished 'tests failed'
from 'the infrastructure vanished underneath them'.

Instead of exec'ing the task command directly, exec a shell that runs it
as a child, and on a nonzero exit re-probes the same ports the preflight
verified, using the pure-bash /dev/tcp probe port_open uses. Any port that
closed since preflight converts the result to a single 'lost mid-run,
results invalid' line and exit 69, matching every other
services-unavailable exit in the runner. Applied to both the tasks exec
and the --only exec.

The epilogue is builtins only (no PATH dependence), defines no functions,
and prints nothing on success; the task runs with the exact argv and
env-u-stripped environment it received before. The only behavioral delta
is one shell level between env and the task. Probing only on nonzero exit
is deliberate: a green run stays byte-identical.

Verified: epilogue unit-checked across success / failure-with-services /
failure-with-lost-port / no-ports; all 45 spec/unit/lanes examples green
run through the modified runner (hermetic boundary spec included, which
drives the selftest lane through the new tasks-path epilogue).

fix(ci): stop publishing secrets and remote markup in Sentry status output

The reporting layer writes to GitHub annotations and the job summary, both
world-readable on this public repo, and GitHub masks secrets by exact value
only.

sanitize() truncated with `cut -c1-700`, which can sever a secret mid-value
and leave a prefix the masker no longer recognises. It now trims at a
whitespace boundary and drops the straddling token whole, so a token is
either wholly present or wholly absent.

render() escaped only pipes, but job summaries render GFM. Details carry
sentry-cli, docker and server output, so a remote could inject a live link
or a Camo-proxied tracking image. Details are now wrapped in a code span
fenced to one more than the longest backtick run inside them. The escape
lives at the render seam rather than in sanitize(): annotations are plain
text and already inert, and stripping markup globally would mangle the TSV
and the step log for every caller.

render also accepts expected component names and synthesizes a BLOCKED row
plus a warning for any that recorded nothing, so a step killed before it
reports can no longer leave the summary claiming every check passed.

fix(ci): make unpinned pulls visible and stop trusting docker's stderr

A missing containerimage.digest silently degraded a digest-pinned pull to a
mutable tag. Two pushes to the same branch both tag edge, so a run that
pulls after another overwrote it uploads the other build's bundles under its
own release SHA, misfiling sourcemaps for both. That now records a warn. The
guard covers BAKE_METADATA being absent entirely as well as missing the key,
since both were equally silent.

Raw docker output no longer reaches the annotation or summary details; it
goes to the step log instead, prefixed at column one. The runner calls
TrimStart() before matching `::`, so an indented prefix would look correct
and still let a registry response forge annotations.

docker create merged stderr into the variable holding the container id, so a
warning on an otherwise successful create produced a malformed reference and
a confidently wrong diagnosis telling the operator to inspect a build that
was fine. Streams are separated, and a hex-only sanity check on the id turns
any future malformation into a named failure. The length is deliberately
unchecked so a short-id format change cannot block extraction outright.

fix(ci): verify the dist join key against the build, not the source

Sentry resolves a bundle only when release and dist both match. The dist
check exempted its own unknown-value sentinels from the mismatch branches,
so execution fell through to an affirmative "dist matches" whenever the
script had no idea what the frontend actually sets. The serializer grep was
also unanchored and matched commented-out lines.

The check now reads the same ground truth the release check already uses: it
greps the built chunks for an inlined dist literal. Source files are
consulted only to explain a mismatch. No path that cannot read the dist off
the build can report ok; unknown reports warn with the reason named.

Reported details no longer carry SENTRY_PROJECTS or the upload project slug,
only counts and text this repo authored. Secret names are kept where they
are the actionable remediation, since naming a secret does not disclose it.

fix(ci): verify sourcemap delivery against what Sentry 26.3.1 actually stores

sentry-cli 3.x uploads only artifact bundles, and the assemble task never
writes ReleaseFile rows, so the two release-file listings return 200 with an
empty array after every successful upload. Each of them was still voting in
the readable tally, which made the UNVERIFIED branch unreachable and turned
any failure of the one meaningful probe into a confident "zero artifacts on
the server". Those listings are now consulted only on negative verdicts, as
context, and never as a vote.

The artifact-bundles query is a disjunction on release or dist, so it could
never confirm the join key: a wrong --dist would have verified as OK while
nothing symbolicated. The authoritative probe is now artifact-lookup, which
filters on release and dist together and is the query symbolication itself
uses. A dist mismatch is reported as its own diagnosis rather than folded
into a generic zero.

An omitted dist on that endpoint means an exact match on the empty string,
not any dist, so without SENTRY_DIST the lookup is skipped entirely rather
than asking a question whose answer is guaranteed wrong.

Release and dist are URL-encoded, the auth token moves off curl's argv, the
instance URL and project slug no longer appear in any reported detail, and
HTTP status codes are surfaced so "could not check" is distinguishable from
itself. Response bodies are never reported.

fix(ci): stop leaking Sentry secrets into the public run page

SENTRY_PROJECTS and SENTRY_PROJECT are repository secrets, and sentry-cli
stderr tails name the org and each project slug individually. A substring of
a space-separated secret is not masked, so those identifiers published on
the run page; on an exact match the row rendered as *** instead, which
defeats the summary. Details now carry counts and text this workflow
authored, and raw CLI output goes to the step log prefixed at column one so
a server response cannot forge workflow commands.

The delivery summary now asserts that the components it expects actually
reported. Previously a step killed before it wrote its output silently
skipped the rest of the chain and the summary still said every check passed.
The sourcemaps expectation is conditioned on the extract having produced
assets, so a fork with no credentials stays quiet; the killed-step case is
still caught, because a killed extract records no row at all and the
unconditional frontend-assets expectation fires.

The zero-upload scrape was unanchored and matched healthy counts like
"Bundled 10 files", and the success notice asserted a delivery count it had
not observed. SENTRY_DIST is hoisted to job scope so the preflight, upload
and verify steps cannot drift apart on the join key.

Four suites, 124 assertions, no services or network:

- render: the two cases where an empty status file means opposite
  things — nothing expected on pull_request (quiet, by design) versus
  a chain killed before it reported (all BLOCKED). Golden-matched, so
  a stray line fails the diff.
- sanitize/md_code: workflow-command forgery, the straddling-token
  drop that keeps secrets maskable, and the code-span fence that

  record, the workflow's expansion stays unquoted, and no script
  records a state outside render's five.

Every suite scrubs the ambient SENTRY_* variables, with a negative

chore(ci): add a shellcheck/actionlint guard with a recorded baseline

Neither tool ran anywhere in this repository, while a growing amount of
CI behaviour lives in shell: scripts/ci/*.sh decide whether telemetry
shipped, .github/scripts/*.sh decide which jobs run at all.

Both tools start with pre-existing findings — 8 and 90 — so the guard
records them and fails only on findings above that baseline. A lane
that lands red teaches everyone to ignore it, which is the same
cry-wolf failure this PR exists to end. A checked-in TSV rather than a
blanket disable, so a reader sees exactly what was accepted, per file
and per rule, and git log shows when each entry appeared. Counts, not
line numbers, which churn on every edit above them.

Findings actionlint gets from running shellcheck over a run: block keep
their SC id rather than the bare [shellcheck] tag, so an unquoted
expansion cannot be traded for a mangling read under one count. Most of
those SC2086s are deliberate list-splitting — one of them is asserted
unquoted by the drift test, and quoting it would silently disable the
missing-component assertion.

scripts/ci and scripts/tests are held to -S style with no baseline:
clean today, and the newest code should stay the tidiest.

ci: run the shell tests and shell lint on pull requests

A separate workflow rather than a tier in ci.yml: that file reports
per-tier timing metrics an unrelated lint job would distort, and this
lane needs no services, no matrix and about thirty seconds. No path
filter, for the reason drift-guards.yml states — a correct filter would
have to enumerate every directory that can hold a .sh file.

shellcheck and actionlint are pinned by version and sha256, verified
before extraction rather than after, and installed into a directory
prepended to PATH because runners ship a shellcheck of their own. A
step re-asserts the pinned versions are the ones actually on PATH; a
baseline recorded under one version is not meaningful under another.

docs: document the shell test suite and lint guard

Both are outside the lane runner, which boots datastores and scrubs

fix(ci): drop the shebang from the sourced assert library

check-shebang-scripts-are-executable rejects a shebang without a +x bit,
and +x would be wrong on a file that is only ever sourced. The
`shellcheck shell=bash` directive carries the dialect instead, which is
all the shebang was doing for the strict lint tier.

fix(ci): score an unrecognised delivery state as degraded

The recap scored a blocklist — failed, blocked, warn — while the table
rendered anything else as UNKNOWN. A row the script had no case for
therefore printed as UNKNOWN with "All Sentry delivery checks passed or
were cleanly skipped" directly beneath it, which is the silent success
this file exists to end.

Unreachable today: record() normalises any unrecognised state to warn
before writing, and nothing else writes the status file. It opens the
moment a sixth state is added to record without a matching change to an
awk a hundred lines away, and the two lists do not look like they are
the same list.

Inverted to "not ok and not skipped", so ok and skipped are named
exemptions rather than the residue of failing to match a blocklist, and
a new state degrades until someone deliberately exempts it. This is the
fail-safe default the missing-row branch a few lines above already
takes, and the same answer Nagios gives: UNKNOWN is a distinct state
and it is not OK.

Tested by writing the row straight to the status file, since record
cannot produce it, plus a negative control asserting skipped still
leaves the recap clean — without it, an awk that degraded every row
would satisfy the new assertions.
