[#4347] Guard useResourceFetch against out-of-order settles

Mirror the requestSeq pattern already in usePaginatedFetch: a slow GET
that settles after a newer request for a different resource must not
overwrite `data`, plant its error, or release `loading`. The drawer
subtitle in WebhookEventsSection binds to the current selection, so a
stale settle previously mislabeled event A's payload as event B's.

Bump the counter inside reset() so an in-flight request whose late
settle would otherwise reconcile onto freshly-reset values is
invalidated too. The RETURN VALUE is unchanged: each caller still
receives (or throws) its own result; only the shared refs are gated.

Tests exercise the race directly (out-of-order deferred promises with
distinguishable payloads) and cover the reset-invalidates-in-flight
case.

[#4347] Fix sync-fallback bookkeeping in billing event publisher

Enqueue_billing_event's sync fallback previously (1) only wrote the
processing_outcome after successful processing — leaving the record
`pending` forever on jobs-disabled deployments — and (2) let a Redis
blip during bookkeeping propagate as a 500, causing Stripe to redeliver
events whose side effects had already been applied.

The sync branch now mirrors the async worker: mark_success! on the
happy path, mark_failed! + re-raise on processing failure, and both
bookkeeping calls wrapped in rescue StandardError so post-side-effects
Redis errors are logged but never bubble to the controller.

Also hardens StripeWebhookEvent#mark_success! so an omitted `outcome:`
kwarg preserves a previously-recorded processing_outcome instead of
silently clearing it (explicit `outcome: nil` still clears).

[#4347] Add write-time index for webhook read views

Both admin listings scanned the object keyspace on every request
(SCAN_COUNT=100 x MAX_SCAN_ROUNDS=100 x MAX_SCAN_ROWS=5_000), which
bounds the keyspace covered per request rather than matched keys and
returns an arbitrary sub-sample with no ordering guarantee on a large
deployment.

Add a class_sorted_set index on each model (scored by first_seen_at /
received_at, member = id, cap = 10_000) written on first insert only
and best-effort on failure. WebhookValidator#initialize_event_record
and PendingFederatedSubscription.store_from_webhook append + trim via
model-owned helpers so a rare index outage cannot fail the webhook
write path (the object row remains the code of record).

[#4347] Rewrite WebhookVisibility to read the index newest-first

Drop the bounded object-key SCAN (identifiers, MAX_SCAN_ROWS, sort,
capped-per-request-scan) and read revrange(0..per_page-1) off each
model's new class_sorted_set. Hydrate only the page slice via
load_multi, lazy-prune any id whose object no longer loads, and add
stale_count to the Page shape (mirroring StripeOrganizations::Result).

capped now means the index itself is at INDEX_MAX_ENTRIES, not that a
per-request scan bailed early — the count is honest again.

[#4347] Cover index-backed read path + write-time index population

[#4451] Extract Onetime::CustomerSessionEvaluator

Introduce a single request-scoped resolver for the customer-session
identity that every protected route, public route, compatibility helper,
and bootstrap serializer will consult. Order is policy and locked here:
session, MFA, authenticated flag, external identity, tenant surface,
customer load, suspension, credential watermark, caller-owned admin
boundary, active-session gate, then impersonation.

The verdict is a frozen value object with typed status/reason. Nothing
in-tree calls it yet; consumers land in subsequent commits.

[#4451] Route auth strategies through CustomerSessionEvaluator

BaseSessionAuthStrategy no longer walks the identity ladder inline; it
delegates to Onetime::CustomerSessionEvaluator and maps the returned
verdict reason to the existing bracketed failure marker. The admin
bound is threaded in as the caller-owned before_active hook so its
env-side effect and precedence relative to the active-session gate are
preserved. The evaluator's Verdict is exposed in strategy metadata as
customer_session_verdict for downstream reuse.

NoAuthStrategy switches to customer_session_verdict for its identity
projection so the shared evaluator produces the same effective customer
on public routes. Helpers#load_user_from_session becomes a compatibility
projection over the same verdict; the inline watermark predicate moves
into the evaluator and is deleted here.

[#4451] Route SessionHelpers through CustomerSessionEvaluator

SessionHelpers#authenticated?, #has_role?, and #load_current_customer
delegate to the shared verdict, so a page render and an API call agree
on identity, surface, watermark, gate, and impersonation once per
request. The per-helper active-session memo becomes the evaluator's
env-level memo through CustomerSessionEvaluator.forget.

The login path drops the newly forgotten verdict after re-stamping
authenticated_at + surface, so the request that just changed identity
does not resolve the previous one from cache.

[#4451] Route views and bootstrap serializer through the evaluator

BaseView and InitializeViewVars stop treating strategy_result as an
independent identity predicate; they extract the session, ask the
CustomerSessionEvaluator, and derive authenticated / cust / awaiting_mfa
from the returned verdict. Organization context is only surfaced when
the verdict is authenticated. The pre-resolved cust argument on
initialize_view_vars becomes vestigial: the evaluator is authoritative
and the memo makes the second call free.

AuthenticationSerializer gains defense in depth: cust is serialized
only when both the authenticated flag and an effective customer are
present, so a stale supplied cust cannot grant identity and an MFA
session leaks neither email nor customer data.

Shared view_test_context is upgraded to a representative authenticated
fixture (authenticated_at, external_id, surface, canonical domain
strategy, non-suspended customer) so the tests exercise the same
predicates the evaluator runs in production.

[#4451] Gate /auth router on CustomerSessionEvaluator reasons

The auth router now resolves the shared verdict before dispatch and
branches on its reason. Definitive rejections (identity_missing,
customer_not_found, account_suspended, stale_credentials,
admin_session_expired) paired with an authenticated Rack flag destroy
the invalid session and answer the established outcomes (logout
succeeds, refused returns session_expired). Surface mismatches keep
their existing warn line and destructive path. active_session_revoked
retains the mid-flow warn and the anonymous-Rodauth continuation.
active_session_unavailable and customer_unavailable both fail closed
but keep the Rack session for recovery.

Since customer predicates can reject before the evaluator's own
active-session boundary, the router still performs its own gate check
in that window: revocation is destructive on this surface and must
not be masked by an earlier customer-store verdict.

MFA-pending sessions are held to the routes that finish the challenge
(otp/recovery/webauthn auth), the anonymous credential/recovery
routes, and logout; anything else is refused with 401. The intact
session lets the ceremony resume after a refused probe.

clear_gated_session also drops the evaluator's env memo so a
destroyed session cannot resurrect a cached identity.

[#4451] Cache-Control private, no-store on personalized HTML and bootstrap

Web Core HTML embeds request- and session-scoped state, including a
masked CSRF token. Core::Middleware::RequestSetup#finalize_response
now applies Cache-Control: private, no-store to every text/html
response as it leaves, replacing any upstream cache directive so
browsers and intermediaries cannot retain the personalized shell.
Non-HTML responses are untouched.

The bootstrap/me route sets the same header explicitly so a caller
mislabelling the response never leaks the JSON snapshot either.

Debug logs are tightened alongside: request_setup logs the request
correlation id instead of the raw nonce prefix, and the bootstrap
route drops session id / key enumerations in favour of the same
correlation id plus boolean state flags.

A shared failure-matrix support helper drives simple- and full-mode
integration specs across every rejection reason and unavailable
outcome. Complementary specs cover:

- the full-mode authenticated continuation baseline,
- the /auth surface's evaluator-driven dispatch,
- the MFA-pending session's allowed and refused Rodauth routes.

These verify end-to-end that the extracted evaluator produces the same
outcome across strategy, helper, view, and router seams.

[#4347] Unindex pending federated subscriptions on destroy

The recent_records sorted set that WebhookVisibility pages through was
only written, never explicitly removed. When EnsureDefaultWorkspace
claimed a pending subscription and called destroy!, the row's Redis
hash went away but its email_hash stayed in recent_records at its
original rank until the 90-day TTL fired.

That left stale ids at arbitrary mid-index ranks. The read-side lazy
prune in WebhookVisibility#list_pending_federated_subscriptions
removed them, but doing so under rank pagination shifted every later
record one slot earlier — an admin paging through would skip one
record at each page boundary the prune touched, until they reloaded
page 1.

to drop the id from recent_records before super, and factor the sorted
set write as unindex_recent(email_hash) that mirrors record_recent_index.
Log-and-swallow keeps this a best-effort read-cache maintenance step
that must not fail the row destroy.

Webhook events (StripeWebhookEvent) don't need the same treatment: all
rows share a 5-day TTL, so stale ids cluster at the old end of the
index where the prune can't shift a valid record across a page
boundary.

[#4451] Constrain session identity resolution to extid lookup

resolve_customer previously fell through Customer.load_by_extid_or_email

the string in session['external_id'] if that field ever held an email
(corruption, hostile write, or a future write path). Session identity
must never cross accounts, so the evaluator now uses find_by_extid
directly. Operator-supplied lookups (impersonation redemption, SSO
linking, basic-auth username) keep the email fallback where it is
intentional.

[#4451] Answer role checks about the acting principal, not the target

has_role? read verdict.customer.role?, i.e. the effective customer, which
is the impersonation target mid-overlay. That silently reversed the

mid-challenge asserted the wrong behavior and now asserts refusal.

cached into env['onetime.customer_session_verdict'] before r.rodauth,

(#4456) are removed and their callers moved.

  longer current is dropped as a unit. Ordinary requests share the one in
  flight. An auth-mutation aborts it and starts again. Local sign-out

committing /signin once will still emit multiple framenavigated events with

therefore failed in CI with three /signin entries — not a Vue bounce, just
normal commit granularity.

[#4497] Preserve session authority through SnapshotOrderingUnavailable 503

A 503 SnapshotOrderingUnavailable is the sidecar counter allocation
failing, not a session verdict. attempt()'s catch block previously
recognised it (recordOrdering 'allocation-failure') but then fell
through to noteFailure(), incrementing failureCount. Under a sustained
outage that crosses MAX_FAILURES within ~10s and calls
bootstrapStore.withholdAuthority('unavailable'), blanking the UI for
every signed-in user.

- Add 'allocation-unavailable' to RefreshOutcome so callers can tell
  it apart from a genuine failed verification. Existing callers (auth
  completion, navigation gates) treat anything other than 'applied'/
  'superseded' as no-advance, which is the correct behaviour here too.
- On isAllocationFailure(error), record ordering, schedule a bounded
  Retry-After-driven retry via a new scheduleAllocationRetry (floored
  at BACKOFF_FLOOR, capped at RETRY_AFTER_CAP, defaulting to 5s), and
  return 'allocation-unavailable'. failureCount is not touched and
  withholdAuthority is not called; the last accepted snapshot stands.
- Reuses the single retryTimer; clearRetry() prevents overlapping
  timers if a subsequent refresh (or noteFailure path) supersedes it.
- VerificationUnavailable.vue treats the new outcome the same as
  'failed' for its retry-failed UX.

Tests: split the shared "no number of failures logs the user out"
outages list (SnapshotOrderingUnavailable no longer belongs — it
never withholds a signed-in user) and add a dedicated describe block
proving 100 consecutive allocation 503s leave authStatus authenticated
with failureCount untouched, that a Retry-After schedules the next
attempt, and that a checking tab does not get withheld by an
allocation 503 the way it would through noteFailure.

[#4451] Make concurrent writers on a SQLite authdb wait instead of failing

Eight parallel POST /auth/create-account against a file-backed SQLite authdb
answered one 200 and seven 500s, each "SQLite3::BusyException: database is
locked" on the accounts INSERT. Two independent causes; four threads that
each read and then insert inside a transaction show three failures under
either fix alone and none under both:

1. Deferred transactions. create-account reads inside its transaction before
   it inserts, so two connections both hold SHARED and both ask to upgrade;
   SQLite refuses the second at once, without the busy handler, because
   waiting would deadlock. transaction_mode = :immediate takes the write
   lock up front, where waiting is safe.
2. Sequel's :timeout calls sqlite3_busy_timeout, which sleeps in C holding
   the GVL. The thread that owns the lock cannot run to release it, so every
   waiter burns the full 5 s and then fails. The sqlite3 gem's
   busy_handler_timeout= does the same wait with the GVL released.

Both live in a new Auth::Database.connect, which the lazy and the immediate
connection now share. PostgreSQL connections are untouched.

No lane saw this because the full-sqlite lane runs on sqlite::memory:, whose
single pooled connection cannot contend with itself. The spec opens a real
file through the production connect. Verified against a running server:
8 of 8 distinct sign-ups 200, and 8 for one login 1x200 + 7x the ordinary
duplicate 403.

Auth: scope the anomaly retry count to one refresh

The coordinator counted anomalous snapshots for the life of the store and
reset the count only when a snapshot applied. A transport failure, a
superseded response or a stale snapshot left it as it was. So one anomaly
whose retry hit the network, followed by hours of failed refreshes, held the
count at 1, and the next unrelated anomaly forced a page load without the
one retry ADR-046 owes it.

The count now lives in run()'s retry loop, where the retry is issued. A
second consecutive anomaly can only be the immediate retry's own answer;
any other outcome ends the path, and a later anomaly begins a new one.
Two anomalies inside one refresh still take the forced page load.

Tests cover the reported sequence (anomaly, failed retries, later anomaly
recovers), the same sequence ending in a second anomaly on the retry, and
the superseded-commit case that previously asserted the count carried over.
ADR-046 rule 4 and the rollout table now say what consecutive means.

[#4450] Add omniauth-saml with ruby-saml pinned exactly

ruby-saml is the XML-signature verifier the SAML trust decision rests on,
and its advisory history is a run of authentication bypasses
(CVE-2024-45409, CVE-2025-25291/25292/25293, CVE-2025-54572). 1.18.1 has
none open. It is pinned with `=` so every bump is a deliberate review of
the gem internals the strategy subclass depends on; the Gemfile comment
lists them as the re-verification checklist.

The lockfile change is the two new gems only. Bundler 4 dropped the
generic `ruby` platform (and the source nokogiri/sqlite3 entries) during
resolution; it was re-added with `bundle lock --add-platform ruby` so
source-built installs keep working.

[#4450] Run bundler-audit on every pull request

An exactly-pinned gem never moves on its own, so something has to say
when it must. Renovate's vulnerabilityAlerts opens the bump PR; this job
makes every other PR red until that bump lands. It reads only
Gemfile.lock, so it needs no bundle install and sits in the
static-analysis workflow beside the other service-free checks.

No ignore list and no baseline: an advisory against an auth-path gem is
not a finding to accept per file.

[#4450] Add SAML assertion replay guard

A SAML Response over the HTTP-POST binding is a bearer document that
travels through the browser. ruby-saml validates signature, audience and
the validity window, none of which stop a second presentation inside the
window; SAML Core requires the SP to keep the set of used assertion IDs
for as long as the assertion would validate.

One atomic SET NX EX keyed on a length-prefixed SHA-256 of
(idp_entity_id, assertion_id). TTL is NotOnOrAfter minus now plus the
clock drift the gem validated with, floored at 1s and capped at one hour
so an IdP-chosen expiry cannot park keys indefinitely. Datastore errors
and blank inputs raise so the caller fails closed.

[#4450] Add request-bound SAML strategy subclass

omniauth-saml and ruby-saml validate the document; they leave binding it
to this login attempt and this IdP to the application, with defaults
that accept rather than refuse. OmniAuth::Strategies::RequestBoundSAML
owns those gates so they run identically on the platform and tenant
surfaces, and a refusal is an ordinary fail! onto the existing
omniauth_on_failure path:

- stores the AuthnRequest id at request phase, consumes it once at
  callback, and refuses when none is pending (the gem treats a nil
  :matches_request_id as "do not check"), so IdP-initiated SSO is
  deliberately unsupported
- refuses a blank idp_entity_id or sp_entity_id in both phases; the gem
  silently skips issuer/audience validation for either
- requires exactly one Issuer value, byte-equal to the configured
  EntityID (the gem's uri_match? folds case and ignores port/fragment)
- refuses a transient NameID unless uid_attribute is set, and a blank uid
- claims the assertion in the replay guard last; datastore errors refuse
- strips every ruby-saml skip_* option before the Response is built
- replaces `extra` so the auth hash never carries response_object (SP
  private key, IdP cert, full XML): scalars plus raw_info as a plain Hash
  without the injected "fingerprint"
- deletes the gem's saml_uid / saml_session_index session keys (SLO off)
- keeps the ACS URL constant by dropping the request query string
- clears RelayState forwarding as a CLASS default: OmniAuth deep-merges
  instance options over defaults, so passing {} at registration is a no-op
- points ruby-saml's STDOUT logger at the Auth logger on load

Specs mount the strategy in a bare Rack stack and drive it with real
signed responses from a runtime-generated test IdP (no key material is
checked in), so the gem's validate path is exercised, not stubbed.

Also switches the replay guard to `extend self` (Style/ModuleFunction)
and corrects the class/path named in its comment and the Gemfile's.

[#4450] Add SAML provider definition and shared hardened-options builder

Registers the platform SAML provider in the SSO registry, configured from
SAML_IDP_SSO_SERVICE_URL / SAML_IDP_ENTITY_ID / SAML_IDP_CERT (+ optional
SAML_SP_ENTITY_ID, SAML_UID_ATTRIBUTE, route/display/trust vars).

Saml.strategy_options_for is the single source of the hardened option set
(full ruby-saml security hash, persistent NameID, clock drift, duplicate
attribute check, SLO off) and validates the IdP trio: https-only SSO URL,
non-blank byte-preserved EntityID, exactly one unexpired PEM certificate.
The tenant arm reuses it next; the strategy spec now runs against it rather
than a fixture copy.

The definition deliberately carries no `issuer:` option: in ruby-saml that
is an alias for our own SP EntityID, and resolve_issuer would key every
identity on it. Invalid config raises from strategy_options (provider
skipped, boot survives) and :vars_valid keeps it unadvertised. Placeholder
options leave the trust anchors blank so the strategy refuses without
tenant injection.

[#4450] Honour an array-wrapped email_verified claim in the SSO verification hold

The SAML strategy hands raw_info over as attribute name => Array<String>,
so an IdP attribute `email_verified` = ["false"] stringified to '["false"]'
and the explicit veto was ignored on that one protocol. Unwrap arrays; any
false among the values holds (the method only ever narrows the stamp).

Specs pin the other direction too: a SAML extra with no such attribute is
not a hold, and is never held as 'claim_unreadable'.

[#4450] Key SAML identities on the validated IdP EntityID, refuse when blank

resolve_issuer gains a SAML branch that is decided first and alone: the
issuer is extra['idp_entity_id'] from RequestBoundSAML (the configured
EntityID, proven byte-equal to the validated response Issuer). None of the
ordinary sources is consulted for a SAML strategy: options[:issuer] is
ruby-saml's alias for our own SP EntityID, raw_info keys are IdP-chosen
attribute names, ENV OIDC_ISSUER is another protocol's, and the '' sentinel
is accepted on the platform surface.

A blank SAML issuer raises SamlIssuerUnresolved, which the identity lookup
turns into an audited sso_failed refusal on both surfaces before any match;
the insert/update hashes can therefore never write '' for SAML. SAML is
identified by the gem's base strategy class, not the route name.

configure_provider now registers the placeholder route when platform config
is present but invalid and org SSO is on, so a platform typo cannot remove
the route tenant SAML configs are injected into.

[#4450] Pin platform SAML IdP origin admission for form-action and POST callback

The SAML HTTP-POST binding is a cross-site POST callback, like Apple's
form_post. Both admitting sets are registry-driven, so the definition's
idp_origin_from (the SSO service URL, never the EntityID) already feeds CSP
form-action and the HttpOrigin callback allowance; these specs pin that:
origin derived from the SSO URL only, callback-path-only and POST-only,
request phase and /metadata, /slo sub-paths still protected, and an
unusable SAML config (bad or expired cert, http URL, blank EntityID)
contributes no origin and is not advertised in sso_providers.

omniauth-saml serves /metadata from whatever options the strategy holds. With the placeholder registration (org-level SSO on, no platform SAML vars) and no tenant resolved, that was a document with a blank entityID. Answer 404 on the same blank-trust-anchor test that already refuses both login phases. Resolves the /metadata open item from the platform stages.

[#4450] Separate SAML certificate structure checks from expiry

cert_problem gains allow_expired: for the tenant record's own validity check, where an expired certificate must not make a stored config impossible to disable or edit. Expiry stays enforced wherever a certificate is accepted or used, including the shared builder. parse_cert exposes the parsed certificate so test_connection can report an expiry date.

[#4450] Add saml as a tenant SSO provider type on CustomDomain::SsoConfig

Three AAD-bound encrypted fields (idp_sso_service_url, idp_entity_id, idp_cert) hold the tenant's IdP trust anchor; none is secret, the domain_id binding is for integrity, so a reveal failure is an error state and never reads as unset. client_id/client_secret become per-provider (CLIENT_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER_TYPES); SAML has no client credential.

to_omniauth_options' saml arm is the platform definition's shared builder plus the record trio. It carries no :issuer, no SP identifiers (derived per request by the tenant hook) and resets uid_attribute so a platform value cannot leak into a tenant flow. An unreadable or unusable trio raises Onetime::Problem. Certificate expiry is not a record invariant, so an expired config stays editable; it is refused where the certificate is used.

BackfillTenantIssuer stamps the revealed idp_entity_id, byte-matching resolve_issuer's SAML branch; blank or unreadable is a Problem.

create! ordering: settled with a real-datastore tryout. Familia 2.12 build_aad does not consult record.exists?, so setting AAD-bound fields before save round-trips for client_id and the new trio alike; MailerConfig.create!'s comment describes an older Familia.

[#4450] Admit a tenant's SAML IdP origin for form-action and the POST callback

AuthConfig replaces the issuer-derived type list with a per-type source-field map (oidc -> issuer, saml -> idp_sso_service_url). The SAML source is an AAD-bound encrypted field, revealed here; an undecryptable value answers no origin. A record-derived type never falls through to the registry, whose saml definition reads the PLATFORM env.

HttpOriginOptions gains the tenant counterpart of the platform IdP allowance: a POST to a callback path is admitted when its Origin equals the request domain's own tenant IdP origin, resolved through the same TenantSsoResolution + tenant_idp_origin pair TenantCspExtras uses, so the form-action set and the HttpOrigin set agree for tenants. Callback-only, POST-only, keyed on display_domain, rescue -> false.

MockAuthConfig's tenant origin delegate called the private Singleton allocate, so tenant_idp_origin raised NoMethodError in every full-mode boot; TenantCspExtras swallowed it. Fixed with send(:allocate).

[#4450] Inject tenant SAML trust anchors and per-request SP identifiers

STRATEGY_CLASS_MAP names the RequestBoundSAML subclass only, so tenant trust anchors can never be injected into a plain omniauth-saml strategy that lacks the gates. After injection the hook derives assertion_consumer_service_url and sp_entity_id from strategy.full_host (the public host), identically on the request phase, the callback and the /metadata sub-path.

A record that cannot produce usable options is refused outright (audited :omniauth_tenant_config_unusable, pending tenant context cleared, sso_not_configured) and never reaches the platform-fallback arm, which would run the tenant's login through the platform IdP with the tenant context still pending.

omniauth-saml runs setup_phase from other_phase, so this hook now fires on /metadata; the tenant context is stored on the request path only, so a bare GET cannot plant a pending tenant flow in a session.

[#4450] Accept and serialize SAML tenant SSO configs in the domains API

PUT/PATCH/test_connection share SamlFields: the platform definition's structural validators plus what is specific to a value arriving over the API (SSRF host check on the SSO URL, certificate expiry, and an outright refusal of idp_cert_fingerprint and its ruby-saml siblings for every provider type). client_id/client_secret are required for the OAuth-family types only.

The SAML trio and the client credentials are mutually exclusive by provider type: the side a type does not use is cleared, never stored as sent, because only the used side is validated.

The serializer returns the trio in plaintext (none is secret), read-only sp_entity_id/acs_url for the admin to register at the IdP, and unreadable_fields naming every encrypted field whose reveal FAILED, so a swapped or corrupted trust anchor is an error state instead of a quiet null.

test_connection's saml arm is local validation only and reports the certificate expiry; it makes no HTTP request.

[#4450] Cover tenant SAML login end to end through real Rodauth

Two tenants with distinct IdPs (runtime keypairs, SamlSpec::TestIdp) drive POST /auth/sso/saml and a signed HTTP-POST callback through the full Rack stack and real Onetime::Session on a custom domain. Asserts the identity row is keyed (saml, IdP EntityID, NameID), a colliding NameID from another tenant IdP gets its own identity and account, a response signed for tenant A is refused on tenant B (honest issuer, forged issuer, replayed valid response), IdP-initiated SSO and assertion replay are refused, SP metadata names the tenant identifiers and is withheld for the placeholder or an unusable record, and HttpOriginOptions admits exactly the tenant IdP origin against real records.

exact ruby-saml pin and bundler-audit on every PR. Documentation: the

[#4450] Correct the SAML signature-algorithm claim in the operator docs

ruby-saml 1.18.1 verifies a response with whatever SignatureMethod and
DigestMethod it declares (xml_security.rb:341, :415); the security hash's
digest_method / signature_method govern only SP-side signing, which this
integration never does. The docs now say SHA-256 is what to configure at
the IdP, not that SHA-1 is rejected.

[#4450] Correct the SECURITY comment: SHA-256 is an SP-side value, not an IdP requirement

digest_method / signature_method feed ruby-saml's sign_document
(xml_security.rb:147), which never runs because no SP key is configured.
The verifier takes the algorithm from the response itself
(xml_security.rb:341, :415), so nothing in SECURITY rejects a SHA1-signed
response. The operator docs were corrected in 1814c3ed9; this brings the
code comment in line so the two do not disagree.

[#4450] Rewrap a comment line in show_invite

A rewording left a two-word orphan line in the middle of the paragraph.

[#4450] Bump sqlite3 to 2.9.6 for GHSA-mwm8-39rw-8826

`bundle update sqlite3 --conservative`; the lockfile diff is sqlite3 only
(2.9.5 -> 2.9.6, every platform entry). The advisory is a use-after-free in
aggregate arguments, fixed in >= 2.9.6. It is unrelated to SAML, but the
bundler-audit job this branch adds reports it and would be red on every
pull request until the bump lands. `bundle-audit check --update` is clean
after the bump; unit, full-sqlite and migrations-sqlite lanes pass.

[#4450] Scope tenant SAML identities to the domain that pinned the certificate

A tenant SAML identity was keyed (route, EntityID, NameID) with the
EntityID taken from the tenant's own record. A SAML EntityID is an
unauthenticated name a tenant admin asserts alongside their own signing
certificate, so tenant B could configure tenant A's EntityID (or the
platform's SAML_IDP_ENTITY_ID) with B's certificate, have B's IdP sign a
response naming it and the victim's NameID, pass every strategy gate and
resolve A's identity row: the victim was logged in on B's surface and
joined into B's organization. Reproduced end to end before this change.

The tenant issuer key is now Saml.tenant_issuer(domain_id, EntityID),
"<domain_id>|<EntityID>". The scope is read through a copy the tenant
hook stamps and nothing consumes, because rodauth-omniauth builds the
identity insert hash after after_omniauth_create_account has consumed
the session copy. The backfill stamps the same value. The platform
surface keeps the bare EntityID, so tenant and platform rows can never
match each other.

[#4450] Refuse SAML responses signed or digested with anything weaker than SHA-256

ruby-saml 1.18.1 verifies with whichever SignatureMethod / DigestMethod
the response declares and maps any URI it does not recognise to SHA-1
(xml_security.rb algorithm), so a SHA-1 signed response validated under
the hardened settings; the SECURITY hash's digest/signature_method are
SP-side signing parameters and cannot change that. Pinned in the spec
against the gem, then gated: after validation the strategy reads every
ds:Signature from the REXML document(s) the verifier used and refuses
anything outside an explicit allowlist (RSA/ECDSA SHA-256/384/512
methods, SHA-256/384/512 digests) as :saml_weak_signature_algorithm,
before the issuer gate so no datastore write is spent.

idp_cert_fingerprint_algorithm is pinned to SHA-256 as well: the gem
matches a certificate embedded in the response against the pinned one
by fingerprint (SHA-1 by default) and then verifies with the embedded
certificate.

[#4450] Keep response-derived text out of OmniAuth failure logs

ruby-saml builds its ValidationError messages from the response: the
Issuer, Audience values and the unsigned StatusMessage (appended verbatim
by validate_success_status, which runs before any signature check, up to
the gem's 250,000-byte cap). omniauth-saml rescues those into
fail!(:invalid_ticket, exception), and the message was then logged
unbounded by omniauth's logger, the [OmniAuth FAILURE] line and the
omniauth_failure audit event: anyone who can start a login could forge
or flood auth log lines.

RequestBoundSAML now overrides fail!: a gem exception is swapped for a
Refusal with a fixed message, and the gem's text reaches the log only as
the bounded, single-line detail of the existing scalar
[saml_response_refused] event. loggable also flattens control
characters. The failure hook bounds and flattens the message for every
provider as defense in depth.

[#4450] Validate a tenant SAML SSO URL for a CSP-safe origin, not for SSRF

The server never fetches a SAML SSO service URL; it is a browser
navigation target. The SSRF host check the OIDC issuer gets (discovery
DOES fetch that URL) refused any IdP that resolves to a private address,
which is a legitimate configuration for a browser that can reach it.

What the URL's origin IS admitted into is the domain's CSP form-action
and HttpOrigin allowances, so the API now accepts a URL only if
AuthConfig.origin_from_url — the funnel those consumers use — derives an
origin from it (https, no userinfo, a host free of CSP-hostile
characters, kept by otto's extras validator). origin_from_url becomes a
public class method so the API reaches the one rule without depending
on whichever auth_config instance a process or test mock installed.

[#4450] Cover platform SAML sign-in end to end in its own lane

No lane drove the platform SAML surface: every full lane boots the saml
route as the tenant placeholder and the tenant e2e asserts the canonical
host refuses, so a regression in configure_provider's real-credential
branch, in Saml.platform_sp_entity_id or in the canonical-host ACS URL

platform surface needs its own process, mirroring full-mfa: lane

matrix row, and a lane_env entry for SAML_IDP_ENTITY_ID.

The lane provides the three public strings; the IdP keypair is minted
by the spec at load time and its certificate installed in ENV before the
first boot, so no key material is checked in (the pre-commit hook
refuses private keys anyway). The spec pins registration from the env,
the derived SP EntityID and canonical-host ACS URL in the AuthnRequest
and SP metadata, bare-EntityID identity keying that never matches a
domain-scoped tenant row, and the InResponseTo, replay, issuer and
signature-algorithm refusals on this surface.

MockAuthConfig#sso_idp_origins is new and env-aware: HttpOrigin is
mounted on the auth app in every environment and the platform IdP's

origin set through production's own derivation. The tenant e2e's
comment claiming HttpOrigin is not mounted was wrong and is corrected.

[#4450] Refuse a SAML SSO service URL whose host ends with a dot

AuthConfig.origin_from_url admits the URL's origin into the CSP form-action
and HttpOrigin allowances, and otto's normalize_origin strips one trailing

HttpOriginOptions compares as a raw string against the stripped
'https://idp.example.com' — so a record with such a URL saves fine but
every callback is refused with 403. Refuse the URL in Saml.sso_url_problem,
which covers the platform vars_valid, the model invariant, PUT/PATCH and
test_connection in one place, and pin it on each surface.

the accounts would get a fresh JIT identity at next login. Refuse a saml

pasted scoped value must not be double-prefixed), and name the scoped form,

[#4513] Add exact-match OIDC discovery issuer validator

Onetime::SsoProvider::DiscoveryIssuer compares a configured issuer to the
issuer a discovery document declares using exact String equality, as OIDC
Discovery 1.0 section 4.3 requires. No trailing-slash, case, or URL
normalization. Missing, empty, or non-string discovered issuers and a
missing configured issuer are failures. Returns an immutable Result with
ok?, reason, configured, and discovered.

[#4513] Extract SSRF-safe OIDC discovery fetcher from TestConnection

Onetime::SsoProvider::DiscoveryFetcher takes over TestConnection#fetch_url

following. Timeouts are configurable (default 10s), and a new body size
cap (default 256 KiB) is enforced on Content-Length and during the
streamed read, with a total deadline over the read.

fetch returns a typed Result instead of raising. TestConnection maps it
onto its existing error codes unchanged, plus discovery_too_large for the
new cap. Spec stubs now yield the response to the request block, matching
how Net::HTTP streams it.

explaining that issuer identifiers are exact, including trailing slashes

[#4450] Refuse SAML assertions valid longer than the replay marker

The replay guard clamped its marker TTL at one hour while ruby-saml puts
no ceiling on Conditions/@NotOnOrAfter, so an assertion the IdP issued
for longer than that became replayable once the marker expired. Refuse
such assertions up front (:saml_assertion_lifetime_exceeded) instead of
clamping; the marker now always outlives the gem's acceptance window.

[#4450] Bind SAML callbacks to the signed assertion and to a real POST ruby-saml checks InResponseTo on the unsigned Response element and only consults SubjectConfirmationData/@InResponseTo when present, so a valid signed assertion that omits it could be rewrapped in a Response naming whatever request id the victim's session was waiting for. Require the pending id on every bearer SubjectConfirmation of the signed assertion (:saml_in_response_to_unbound). IdPs that omit it for SP-initiated sign-in are refused by design; Okta, Entra ID and AD FS emit it. This settles the design question left open in the PR body. callback_phase also consumed the pending id before checking the request was a POST with a SAMLResponse. With the SameSite=None cookie the POST binding needs, a cross-site GET could burn the id and cancel a sign-in in progress. Anything but a POST carrying a SAMLResponse is now refused (:saml_response_missing) without touching the pending id.

ever passing valid_issuer_host?. Mirror PUT on create, and validate the
effective issuer whenever a record switches into oidc so records created
before this fix cannot take that path either.

[#4450] Bar SAML strategies from the legacy sentinel identity grace

No SAML identity was ever stored under the '' issuer sentinel:
resolve_issuer raises rather than return it, and tenant SAML postdates
migration 008. A (route, '', uid) row under the SAML route can therefore
only be another protocol's `sub`, left behind when SAML_ROUTE_NAME was
pointed at a route OIDC/GitHub/Google once served. Gracing it on the
platform path would let an IdP-asserted NameID equal to that old `sub`
sign in as, and permanently rebind, someone else's account.

The backfill CLI already refuses SAML domains for this reason; the live
lookup now refuses the same way, keyed on the strategy class.

off. Only a bare PATCH could disable it, and only that case had a spec.

when it was stored; only a changed value is a new value to accept. This
keeps the expiry rule (not a model invariant, so a config can always be
switched off) true for the form, not just for a hand-written request.

subdomain therefore showed a button whose sign-in could not complete.

Upgrade otto to 2.11 and drop IsolateResponseHeaders

Otto 2.11 copies a configured static not_found / server_error triple on
every request (Otto::Static.copy_response, delano/otto#272): the headers
container keeps its class, each Array-valued header is copied, and an
Array body is copied. That is the same per-request copy
Onetime::Middleware::IsolateResponseHeaders made around every router
(#4401), so the middleware, its mount in Base#build_rack_app and its unit
spec are removed.

The regression guard stays: spec/integration/all/router_fallback_response_headers_spec.rb
passes 19/19 on 2.11 without the middleware, and fails 10/19 on 2.10.0
without it (session cookies accumulate across API misses), so the Gemfile
floor is what now keeps the leak closed.

2.11 also rejects fallback triples whose body responds to neither #each
nor #call. Every app's not_found / server_error body is an Array; ACME
sets no fallback and the Auth app is Roda.

[#4450] Refuse re-enabling a SAML config under an incompatible session cookie

validate_saml_fields! skipped the session-cookie check for every existing
record, so a PATCH could flip a disabled saml record back to enabled
under SameSite=Lax or Secure=false. Every sign-in through it then fails
as saml_no_pending_request, and with enforce_sso_only that locks the
tenant out while SSO stays advertised. Treat a disabled-to-enabled flip
as activation, the same as introducing the config. Editing a record that
stays disabled, or one already enabled, is still allowed.

[#4450] Accept only one PEM certificate block as idp_cert

parse_single_cert counted BEGIN CERTIFICATE markers and handed the whole
text to OpenSSL, which parses the first certificate it finds and ignores
the rest. A pasted bundle carrying a private key before or after the
certificate was therefore accepted, stored whole, and served back in
plaintext by the SSO config API, which treats idp_cert as public data.
Require the value to be exactly one certificate block, surrounding
whitespace aside, and parse only that block.

[#4450] Label host-derived SAML SP identifiers as a preview

Before a saml record is saved the SP Entity ID and ACS URL are composed
in the browser from the domain host, the default route and https. An
operator route override (SAML_ROUTE_NAME) or site.ssl=false makes those
differ from what the server derives once the record exists. Hiding the
values until saved would block IdPs that require ACS and Audience at
app creation, so keep the preview but say that it is one and that the
saved values are the ones to confirm. Plumbing the real route through
bootstrap config stays tracked in #3932.

[#4450] Drop the Auth0-specific rows from the SSO docs; restore the macOS spec pointer

No AUTH0_* variable exists: the omniauth-auth0 gem was dropped in #4512
and Auth0 is configured as generic OIDC, which the docs already
describe. The provider table and the CSP form-action table advertised a
provider that the registry never consumed. The macOS companion README
was a pointer stub to the spec's new home, removed in e986eec1bd as a
dead spec; deleting it turned an existing documentation URL into a 404,
so it is restored byte for byte.

[#4450] Record why the SAML replay key is not scoped by tenant or trust anchor

Review of #4450 proposed adding the pinned certificate or a tenant id to
the replay scope. A coarser scope can only refuse more presentations,
never admit a replay; a cross-tenant false refusal needs two IdPs
sharing an EntityID and minting the same assertion ID, which SAML Core
requires to be unique and unpredictable; and the one legitimate
shared-EntityID shape, one IdP serving several domains, pins the same
certificate anyway. Write that down next to the key derivation.

[#4513] Keep the cached OIDC issuer verdict out of restrict_to and HttpOrigin

The per-process issuer verdict now only withholds the login button
(AuthConfig#sso_providers), and never under restrict_to 'sso', where an
empty provider list renders the standard multi-method form.

provider_active? no longer reads the verdict. Before, one worker's cached
mismatch on an OIDC-only install made restrict_to_available? false, which
also took down custom domains that inherit the restriction while their own
tenant OIDC still worked, and narrowed the HttpOrigin callback origins.

[#4513] Treat a discovery response without a string issuer as unknown, not a mismatch

A 200 whose JSON is not a discovery document (an edge proxy's error
object) says nothing about OIDC_ISSUER. It was cached as a rejection for
REJECTED_TTL, showing "misconfigured" for two minutes past the outage.
Only a document that names a different issuer is now a mismatch; the rest
fail open to the gem's own discovery check, like a timeout or non-JSON body.

[#4513] Bound the OIDC discovery status line and headers by the total deadline

The deadline was checked only between body chunks. Net::HTTP reads the
status line and headers before yielding, each read bounded only by
read_timeout, so a server dripping header bytes could hold a sign-in
thread past open + read timeout. The deadline now wraps the whole
exchange.

[#4450] Report each SAML browser matrix case by engine and policy

The Playwright harness aborted the whole matrix on the first failed
expectation, so the Ruby spec could not say which engine or cookie
policy failed. Each case now records passed or failed with the failing
line, and the spec's matrix assertion names it.

Whether the session cookie travelled on the cross-site POST is taken
from the server's observation only. WebKit does not expose the Cookie
request header through Playwright, which failed the None control on
WebKit even though the server saw the cookie. Chromium, Firefox and
WebKit now pass all nine Lax, None and Strict cases.

[#4450] Stage SAML callbacks only for hosts with an active route

Stage refused nothing: any POST to the callback path was staged, and
HttpOrigin admits an Origin-less non-browser POST, so one client could
fill the global admission bucket and deny SAML sign-in to every tenant,
while pushing oversized junk into the datastore that also holds
secrets. Stage now answers 404 unless the resolved host has an active
SAML route at the exact path. The predicate is the one the null-Origin
allowance already used, extracted as
HttpOriginOptions.saml_callback_route_active?, so the two admission
decisions cannot drift. It authorizes nothing on the GET side.

The SAMLResponse value must be base64 characters (whitespace allowed:
IdPs wrap lines and form decoding turns a bare plus into a space). The
value bound drops from 350,000 to 128,000 bytes and the form bound from
500,000 to 200,000; real responses are well under 100 KB.

Admission limits are configurable: SAML_CALLBACK_GLOBAL_LIMIT (default
256) and SAML_CALLBACK_SOURCE_LIMIT (default 64, was a fixed 20 per
masked source), read once, validated as positive integers, the source
share clamped to the global cap. A fixed 20 per masked /24 per two
minutes would 429 an office behind one address during a sign-in rush.

The platform route check ignores case, as OmniAuth and the transport's
own path match already did, so a mixed-case path cannot sidestep the
host restriction. A trailing slash on the callback path is stripped
before the transport's path match so the Boundary strips cookies and
bounds the body on that spelling too; it is still never staged.

The tenant and platform suites assert the staging contract on every
successful callback (303 with a handle and no Set-Cookie) instead of
following the redirect only when one appears, so they fail without the
transport.

[#4450] Accept only staged GETs in the SAML strategy

The strategy still had a direct-POST branch: a POST that reached
callback_phase (a path spelling the transport does not stage, such as
a trailing slash, or a stack without the transport) was parsed and
validated, with the pending request id consumed before validation.
Only the Origin check stood in the way. Any callback that was not
staged is now refused outright with saml_response_missing; only a GET
carrying a staged handle supplies an assertion, and nothing is
consumed before validation succeeds.

The strategy spec stages into an in-memory store and completes with
the handle GET, as the transport produces in production, and pins that
a direct POST with a valid response is refused, retains the pending id
and never reaches the store.

[#4450] Require Recipient and NotOnOrAfter on every SAML bearer confirmation

Replay retention is derived from the signed bearer SubjectConfirmationData
expiries, but a confirmation with no Recipient or no NotOnOrAfter was
silently skipped, and ruby-saml accepts such confirmations. A crafted
assertion could therefore stay acceptable after its replay marker
expired, within the same session and pending request. Every bearer
confirmation of the signed assertion must now name this ACS and carry a
parseable NotOnOrAfter, enforced in post_validation_refusal next to the
every-bearer InResponseTo rule; a defect refuses the callback with
saml_bearer_confirmation_unbounded. The latest-eligible-expiry retention
logic is unchanged.

[#4450] Refuse a transient NameID without a uid attribute; warn on NameID format changes

A tenant could save the transient NameID format, which then refused
every sign-in because tenant records have no uid attribute; the
platform surface accepted it with SAML_UID_ATTRIBUTE unset for the same
outcome. name_id_format_problem now takes the uid attribute, so
transient is refused at tenant validation (422 on every write path)
and at platform boot (provider skipped, both variables named), through
the one strategy-options builder. The tenant contract enum drops
transient.

Changing the NameID format re-keys every user's identity, since the
uid is the NameID, and nothing said so. PATCH and PUT on an existing
SAML record now log domain_sso_name_id_format_changed at warn level
(formats themselves are sensitive and stay out of the log), and the
policy docs and .env.reference state that existing identities will not
match after a change unless a uid attribute supplies the key.

[#4450] Document the Lax cookie requirement; pin the platform SAML lane to lax

Since the staged callback transport, SAML needs a Secure session cookie
with same_site lax or none; strict cannot recover the initiating
session. .env.reference, auth_config.rb, the test config and the lane
comments still told operators that SAML requires same_site none, which
re-creates the cross-site cookie problem the transport removed. The
cookie-samesite design spec gets a status note pointing at the
transport doc instead of a rewrite.

The full-saml-platform lane and its hardcoded copy in spec.rake now
pin SESSION_COOKIE_SAME_SITE=lax, the default-compatible policy the
transport is designed for, so the Rack integration suite proves the
Lax path rather than the None compatibility path. The transport doc's
validation section records that CI runs the Chromium, Firefox and
WebKit matrix on every PR.

Classify indeterminate TXT checks separately from mismatches

Approximated returns actual_values: false when its own DNS resolution
fails. Reading that as a mismatch demoted correctly-configured domains
on every refresh run. The strategy now returns validated: nil with
indeterminate: true for that case, and falls through to a native TXT
lookup that can only promote (exactly one value, equal to the challenge).

Extend indeterminate discipline to vhost status checks

Accept ACTIVE_SSL_PROXIED as ready (hosts fronted by another proxy such
as Cloudflare CNAME setups) and treat status: UNKNOWN as indeterminate
so is_resolving comes back nil and the stored flag is left alone —
mirroring the TXT-check contract.

Carry indeterminate and demoted signals through VerifyDomain results

Add dns_indeterminate and dns_message to Result, indeterminate_count and
demoted_count to BulkResult, and a demoted? predicate for the run that
just lost :verified. The operation warns on both notable outcomes so an
operator can find them in the log without a console session.

Surface indeterminate and demoted signals in job, API, and CLI

Extend the refresh-job summary, colonel + domains verify responses, TS
schema, and CLI output with the new fields. The CLI shows an
INDETERMINATE row and the run summary breaks out indeterminate/demoted
counts so an operator can spot Approximated flapping without reading
raw logs.

Hold verified through failed TXT checks after operator override

The Colonel override is the operator's standing assertion of ownership for
domains DNS checks cannot reach (private networks, a broken upstream
checker). Before this change, the next refresh run would still demote the
domain when its TXT check failed, undoing the assertion silently.

verified_by_override records the assertion on the model; VerifyDomain
leaves verified alone while it is set, clears it once DNS validates on
its own, and reports the outcome as :override_held through the new
dns_outcome label (validated / indeterminate / override_held / failed).
The Colonel, admin API, CLI, and admin UI carry the marker and the
label through to the operator, and the verifyOutcomeNotice util picks
the notification once so the three admin-view call sites agree.

Refresh domains via a persisted cursor walk over the full set

The job used to take the newest batch_size on every run, so every domain
past the first batch stayed at whatever cached vhost/resolving state it
had, forever. The cursor now resumes from the last offset, advances one
batch per run, wraps when the page comes up short, and expires after a
day so a stalled walk restarts at zero. One batch per run keeps a run
bounded by the Approximated rate limit; the worst case from membership
changing between runs is a domain refreshed twice or one cycle late.

Probe Approximated's NXDOMAIN semantics before staying indeterminate

Approximated's contract for actual_values is either an Array of values
it saw or the literal `false` "when DNS resolution or the record-type
lookup failed." That leaves a gap: if the TXT record is deleted, the
checker might report it as either state, and Ruby's resolver reports
NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL the same way, so the native fallback cannot pick
between them.

The strategy now issues one extra check-records-match-exactly against a
random subdomain that cannot exist, only when the primary check has
already come back indeterminate and the native lookup has failed to
promote. The sentinel reveals which state covers NXDOMAIN for this
deployment:

  actual_values is []     -> the checker distinguishes NXDOMAIN, so the
                             primary `false` is a transient upstream
                             fault, not a deletion.
  actual_values is false  -> the checker conflates NXDOMAIN with
                             SERVFAIL. A deleted TXT record cannot be
                             demoted through this checker, because
                             native resolution cannot settle it either.

Either way the result stays indeterminate; the probe outcome is
recorded on the result hash so operators can tell "checker is broken
today" apart from "checker will never demote a deleted TXT record."

Derive the domain refresh page from the clock instead of a cursor

The persisted cursor needed a Valkey key, a TTL, and wrap/reset logic to
walk the full domain set. The page is now computed per run: whole
check_interval ticks since the epoch, modulo the page count, times
batch_size. There is no position to store, expire, or get stuck.

The modulus is pages rather than domains. With `(tick * batch) % total`
a short last page skips the head of the set for the whole lap (201
domains at batch 200 refreshes domain 0 once per 201 ticks), and any
single add or remove re-randomizes the offset because tick is large.
Page-aligned windows cover every domain once per cycle and only
re-phase when the set crosses a batch_size boundary.

Interval parsing lives in ScheduledJob#interval_seconds, next to `every`,
using the same rufus parser that schedules the interval so tick length
cannot drift from the firing cadence. Job subclasses still never name
rufus. A skipped or doubled scheduler tick costs one page an extra cycle
or a repeat refresh.

Add a TXT resolver that reports the DNS response code

Resolv::DNS#getresources and #fetch_resource surface NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL,
REFUSED and timeouts identically (no exception, no resources), because
Resolv::DNS::Config#resolv rescues its own NXDomain and OtherResolvError.
TxtResolver sends the query itself using the Resolv::DNS::Message codec so
callers can tell a definitive negative answer from a failed lookup. Names
are queried as absolute so the resolv.conf search list is never applied.
The spec runs against an in-process loopback DNS server.

Add a shared TXT ownership verifier with three outcomes

TxtVerifier checks the TXT challenge with our own lookup and returns the
BaseStrategy#validate_ownership contract: exactly one matching value is
true; NXDOMAIN, an empty NOERROR answer, or any other set of values is
false; SERVFAIL, REFUSED, timeouts and exceptions are nil/indeterminate so
a failed lookup never changes stored state. Results carry source 'native'
and Approximated-shaped :data. Loaded with the strategies; not yet used by
them.

Verify TXT ownership under the Caddy on-demand strategy

CaddyOnDemandStrategy#validate_ownership returned validated: true without
checking anything. It now checks the TXT challenge record through the shared
TxtVerifier, with the same three outcomes and the same 'exactly one matching
value' rule as the Approximated strategy. Caddy completing an ACME challenge
shows where the name resolves; it is not an ownership check.

VerifyDomain needs no change: a definitive negative demotes (unless an
operator override holds), an indeterminate lookup leaves stored state alone.
The tryout drives VerifyDomain with the real strategy over a scripted
resolver and checks CustomDomain#ready?, which the ACME ask endpoint reads.

Use the shared TXT verifier for Approximated's native fallback

ApproximatedStrategy had its own native lookup built on
Resolv::DNS#getresources, which returns [] for NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL and a
timeout alike, so it could only ever promote. It now calls TxtVerifier when
the upstream checker is indeterminate and passes the three outcomes through.

Promotion is unchanged. A definitive negative from our own resolver (NXDOMAIN,
NOERROR without TXT data, or values that are not exactly one match) now
returns validated: false, so a removed TXT record demotes even while the
upstream checker gives no answer; an operator override still holds. SERVFAIL,
REFUSED, a timeout or an exception stay indeterminate. The NXDOMAIN sentinel
probe runs only when the native lookup is indeterminate too, and its
telemetry is kept. The reasoning is in the classify_ownership comment.

Document the TXT ownership check under the Caddy on-demand strategy

The strategy README, config reference, ADR-016/017 and the admin strategy
description said or implied that Caddy's ACME challenge stands in for domain
validation. They now describe the TXT check, its three outcomes, and that
certificate issuance is not an ownership check.

The ACME endpoint README still documented check_verification=false as a way
to skip DNS verification. The HTTP interface has ignored that parameter since
it was removed; the README now says so.

Move the response-code-aware DNS transport into a shared stub resolver

TxtResolver keeps its TXT lookup and Answer; the UDP/TCP exchange, time

the table cannot: per-tier completion state naming failed and skipped

lane apart from setup); and each step against the per-step median of
recent successful main runs, flagged only when both 25% and 15s slower.

so a change in coverage cannot hide as a change in time.

Set up new worktrees from post-checkout, and move bin/setup's spine to tools/setup

A new worktree starts with no dependencies, config or generated files. Zed
ran bin/setup --test for its own worktrees through a create_worktree task;
worktrees made with plain `git worktree add` got nothing. The one hook that
every `git worktree add` runs is post-checkout, which git calls with an
all-zero previous ref only when it creates a worktree (or a clone).

tools/setup/new-worktree.sh is that hook, wired as a pre-commit
post-checkout stage. It is opt-in per clone (`git config
ots.worktreeSetup true`), because the hook is installed for every
contributor who runs bin/setup. A worktree whose name starts with "dev"
gets bin/setup --dev, every other one --test. The name is the worktree's
directory, or its parent when the directory is named after the main
checkout (worktrees/onetimesecret/dev-api/onetimesecret), so an ancestor
such as ~/Projects/dev/ never selects the dev lane. The hook always exits
0: git reports a failing post-checkout as a failed `git worktree add`,
although the worktree exists. Output goes to tmp/worktree-setup.log.

Zed runs post-checkout for its worktrees too, so .zed/tasks.json would
have set each one up twice; it is removed. Tools that create worktrees
without running git hooks are not covered, as the docs say. bin/setup's
dev and test lanes end with a one-line pointer to the opt-in until a
clone has set it.

The hook shares logic with bin/setup through its lib, which ADR-042 calls
a tool package: scripts/setup/lib.sh moves to tools/setup/, beside the
hook, with a README and the package's own shell test. scripts/tests/run.sh
now also runs tools/*/tests/*-test.sh, so the static-analysis shell job
picks it up. The Dockerfile copies tools/setup/lib.sh alone into both
final stages; the path filters of fresh-clone, installer and
devcontainer-ci follow the move, and installer.yml's bash 3.2 parse gate
covers the hook as well. bin/setup still holds the lane logic ADR-042
wants out of bin/<domain>; the package README records that as a separate
migration.

Route every bin/ots migrate path through one recorded runner

Single-ID and file runs called Base.cli_run directly, bypassing dependency
checks and applied-state recording; rollback ran `down` without `prepare`
or a run mode and dropped applied state even when writes were skipped; a
migration that returned false or isolated record errors was recorded as
applied by the upstream Runner. Add Onetime::CLI::MigrateRunner
(subclassing Familia::Migration::Runner) with one invariant: a modifying
run is dependency-checked, runs the full lifecycle, and is recorded
exactly once, only after it succeeds.

- `--dry-run` is a real option; every action is a dry run without `--run`,
  and `--dry-run` alone previews all pending. `--run --dry-run` is refused.
- `--rollback ID` previews; `--run` instantiates in actual-run mode, calls
  `prepare` then `down`, and records the rollback only on success.
- Outcomes: success (recorded on --run), skipped, partial (record errors,
  unrecorded, exit 1), failed (raise or false return, unrecorded),
  already_applied (modifying single run refused). A batch stops at the
  first non-ok outcome; a batch dry run treats its own previewed successes
  as satisfied dependencies.
- Bare IDs: exact, then unique partial match; ambiguous matches are
  refused. A file path selects its migration regardless of basename.
- `--status` outranks every action.

Separate queue wait from runtime per test job in the CI metrics breakdown

The jobs API carries created_at (the moment a job's `needs` finished and
it was queued) next to started_at and completed_at, so a job's wait for
a runner and its runtime are separable. In the run this was built
against, Ruby Unit Tests waited 1m 36s for a runner after a 1m 29s
dependency wait, then ran 5m 53s — a third of its "from start" figure
was waiting, and the stagger across the thirteen T2/T3 jobs released in
the same second says it was the runner pool, not GitHub latency.

A Jobs table (T2/T3/T4) now shows result, queued, ran, ran on main and
the delta, flagged on runtime by the same 25%/15s rule as steps; a line
under it says when the test jobs were released and the longest wait
against the main median. Queue time is never flagged: it is runner
availability, not the change under test. Failed and skipped jobs show
no delta, and with no baseline at all nothing is marked new.

Redact URIs in HttpOrigin check-failure warnings

The three SSO callback rescues in HttpOriginOptions logged inconsistently:
two printed the exception message verbatim and one dropped it, and no
layer between them and the log scrubs anything. redis-client quotes its
server URL in every ConnectionError; its 0.30 server_url carries host,
port and db only, but the message is the one place a credential-bearing
URI could reach the log unscrubbed, and the message is also what says
why a check failed (which host refused, which SAML field was invalid).

All three rescues now log through one helper that keeps the class and
message and passes every embedded URI through redact_uri_userinfo, via
a new OT::Utils.redact_uris_in_text. A URI span runs to the next
whitespace, so an unescaped ")" or "," in a password stays masked.

Split container E2E into blocking simple and full auth lanes

e2e.yml booted the OCI image in simple auth mode and then ran e2e/full/
against it as a continue-on-error step. Part of that suite asserts
full-mode UI (the Security settings section is visible only when
isFullAuthMode), so the step was red by construction and gated nothing.

The job is now a fail-fast: false matrix with two lanes, each on its own
runner with its own image build, Valkey container and SQLite authdb:

- simple: e2e/all/ against the container as configured before, with
  AUTHENTICATION_MODE=simple now stated rather than defaulted.
- full: e2e/full/ against the same image in AUTHENTICATION_MODE=full,
  with a boot-migrated sqlite://data/auth.db (resolves to /app/data,
  created owned by appuser in the Dockerfile) and per-run masked
  ACCOUNT_ID_SECRET and AUTH_SECRET, both of which Rodauth's secret
  guards require at boot under RACK_ENV=production. A health check
  asserts the authdb exists so the lane cannot silently run simple mode.

Both lanes run the flaky gate and upload lane-scoped report, trace and
container-log artifacts; the app and Valkey logs are now kept on every
run instead of printed only in debug mode. notify-results fails unless
every lane passed. No ruleset or branch protection requires a check
from this workflow today; notify-results is the stable name to require.

The pull_request path filter now covers everything the image is built
from (apps, lib, etc, bin, migrations, Gemfile*, config.ru, docker/, ...)
because the full lane tests the backend baked into the image.

Secrets are passed to docker as bare -e NAME so they stay off the
command line, which clears the two baselined SC2155 findings; the
baseline entry is removed. Comments in playwright.config.ts, the a11y
overview and the full a11y spec now describe the lanes instead of the
removed informational step.

Stop requiring login-confirm on signup when verify_account is off

The SPA signup form sends one email field. Rodauth defaults

every SPA signup with 422 "logins do not match". State it next to the

The field is a typo guard the caller fills in itself, so this changes no

Let e2e auth setup continue past a signup for an existing account

Full mode answers a signup for an existing login with 400 "Unable to
create account" (overrides/duplicate_signup.rb) where simple mode answers
success. The setup waited only for /check-email, so once the first attempt
had created the account, every Playwright retry timed out at signup and
hid the real failure behind it.

Wait for either /check-email or the signup error alert and go on to sign
in in both cases; sign-in stays the guard. A signup error is recorded as a
signup-error annotation so a following sign-in failure names its cause.

The header said registration is idempotent because the backend answers
success for existing accounts, and that AUTH_AUTOVERIFY=true makes the
account sign-in-able. Both hold only in simple mode; full mode needs
AUTH_VERIFY_ACCOUNT_ENABLED=false.

AUTH_AUTOVERIFY is read only by simple-mode signup, so full-mode accounts
were created unverified and global.setup's sign-in answered 403. Setting
AUTH_VERIFY_ACCOUNT_ENABLED=false turns off Rodauth's verify_account, so
the setup account is open at once; that works now that signup no longer
requires login-confirm with verify_account off.

CREATE_ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false because the full/ suite signs up
several accounts from one IP, each retried up to twice, and a real failure
could run past the 10-per-hour cap and hide under 429s. e2e-full-auth.yml
sets it for the same reason.

The comments that credited AUTH_AUTOVERIFY with making the full-lane
account sign-in-able now say what it does in each mode.

Keep organization settings mounted when switching tabs

setActiveTab navigated with router.replace. App.vue keys the routed view by $route.fullPath, so every tab switch remounted OrganizationSettings: it refetched permissions, the organization, members and invitations behind the skeleton, and the arrow-key handler's nextTick focus() reached the destroyed instance's tab. Keyboard users lost focus on ArrowRight/ArrowLeft (WAI-ARIA tabs), which is the org-settings keyboard failure in the full-auth E2E lane.

Tab switches now rewrite the address bar with history.replaceState, as Login.vue already does for the same fullPath-remount trap. history.state.current is updated with the URL so Vue Router's next push does not write the old tab back into the entry Back returns to. router.currentRoute therefore keeps the mounted location, so an afterEach hook re-applies it when a link to that location is dropped as a duplicate or Back/Forward lands on it without a remount. Without the hook, the user menu's Activity item would do nothing after the user left the Activity tab. URL writes stop once the view unmounts, so a late checkInitialTabRedirect cannot rewrite the next page's URL.

No guard reads :tab and the tab gates stay in the component, so skipping the router on tab switches does not change access.

Keep org settings mounted across tab switches through the router

6c7f6f4629 stopped tab switches from remounting OrganizationSettings by rewriting the address bar with history.replaceState. That left router.currentRoute on the tab the view mounted with, so everything that reads the route went stale after a tab click: the org switcher's 'same' target pushed the mounted tab (open /org/A/domains, click Members, switch to B, land on /org/B/domains), and a link to the tab on screen pushed a duplicate entry and remounted the page.

Tab switches are router navigations again. The remount came from App.vue keying the routed view by fullPath; a route can now list params in meta.keepMountedAcrossParams, which routeViewKey leaves out of that key. The org settings route lists :tab, so a tab switch keeps the instance (no refetch, keyboard focus survives) while the router, the URL and history stay in step. The router keeps the scroll position for such a navigation. The replaceState rewrite and its afterEach resync are gone.

The :tab watcher now ignores a route for another org: that route remounts the view, and its tab must not be gated with the old org's permissions. Guards still run on every tab switch, and the tab gates stay in the component, so access is unchanged.

Formatting only, so the fixes to this spec that follow show only their own changes.

SEC-INV-001 and SEC-INV-004 now assert the 400 and that no session exists. SEC-INV-002 checks what is left of the verification risk: no account exists to verify. A sign-in with the refused credentials fails, while the same address signs up and signs in without a token (the control that the refusal came from the token). The empty-token case asserts the plain signup succeeds.

SEC-INV-003 (valid token signs the new account in) was quarantined as needing mail and a seeded invitation. The owner's invitations API returns the token, so it now runs: the storageState owner invites, a fresh context signs up on the invite page, lands on direct_accept and is signed in. It never accepts, so the owner's org gains no member. Its QUARANTINE row is removed.

Add Onetime::LogScrubber, a Semantic Logger URI scrub

An on_log subscriber that rewrites each emitted event before the async
queue and appender fan-out, so every appender (stdout/stderr and the
ColonelAudit syslog destination) sees the same scrubbed event. It runs
OT::Utils.redact_uris_in_text over the message, tags, named tags, the
logged exception and its causes, and String/Symbol/URI/Exception/Set
values and keys inside Hash/Array payloads. URI userinfo and whole
query strings are masked; emails and identifiers are kept, unlike the
Sentry scrub.

Copy-on-write: caller payloads, strings and exceptions are never
mutated; exceptions are replaced by dup'd copies with scrubbed
message/to_s/inspect/cause. Work is bounded (16 KiB per URI-bearing
string, 64 KiB scanned per event, 1000 values, depth 8, 5 chain links)
and fails closed with [log scrub: ...] placeholders. Any internal error
withholds the event instead of letting Semantic Logger queue the
original. Not yet registered.

Register the log scrubber at boot and in SetupLoggers

Onetime.boot! registers Onetime::LogScrubber as its first statement,
before Config.load and the early initializers log anything, so no event
can sit in the async queue unscrubbed until an appender arrives.
SetupLoggers#execute registers it again before adding any appender; the
call is idempotent and covers the initializer running outside boot!.

Specs cover registration order, running execute twice, the ColonelAudit
syslog appender end to end (::Syslog stubbed at its three calls), and the
production backtrace-trimming formatter.
